1. Rinse, peel and then grate 550 grams carrots. In cup measurement, you will need 4 cups grated carrots.
2. Grease a pan or tray with 1/2 to 1 tsp ghee and keep aside.
3. Then in a kadai or thick bottomed pan, melt 2 tbsp ghee (clarified butter).
4. Add the grated carrots. Mix very well.
5. Then on a low to medium flame, with frequent stirring saute the carrots till they are almost cooked. Takes about 10 to 12 minutes on a low to medium flame.
6. Then add 1 cup milk powder (100 to 105 grams).
7. Mix the milk powder with the carrots very well. Saute for a minute.
8. Then add 1/3 cup sugar and 1/2 tsp cardamom powder.
9. Mix the sugar and cardamom powder with the rest of the ingredients very well.
10. The mixture will loosen up as the sugar melts. Continue to saute with frequent stirrings for about 7 to 9 minutes on a low to medium flame.
11. When the mixture thickens and reduces, its time to switch off the flame and pour the mixture in the greased pan. 
12. A test is to take a small mixture and cool it. Then roll into a small ball. It should easily form a ball.
13. Immediately, pour the barfi mixture in the greased pan and with a spatula or spoon smoothen the top part.
14. Sprinkle chopped pistachios (18 to 20 pistachios) on top and gently press them with a spoon or spatula on the halwa.
15. Cover and allow the carrot barfi to cool and set at room temperature. You can also keep in the fridge after the barfi cools down at room temperature.
16. Slice and serve gajar ki barfi. Leftovers can be refrigerated.

1. Begin with rinsing the mint leaves and keeping them aside. 
2. We will use 1 cup tightly packed fresh mint leaves of which half is added to the dough and the other half is added to the spice mix.
3. Then start with the dough preparation - in a mixing bowl or pan, take 2 cups whole wheat flour (240 grams), 2 tsp oil or ghee or butter and 1/2 to 1 tsp salt or add as per taste.
4. Mix very well.
5. Then add 1/2 cup tightly packed fresh mint leaves (finely chopped). Again mix very well.
6. Now add water in parts. Initially you can add 1/3 to 1/2 cup water.
7. Mix and begin to knead the dough.
8. Add more water as required and knead to a smooth dough. Overall I used 2/3 cup of water to knead the dough. Depending on the quality of flour, you may need to add more or less water.
9. Cover the dough and keep aside for 30 minutes.
10. In a pan, add 1/2 cup tightly packed fresh mint leaves.
11. On a low flame or sim with frequent stirs, roast the mint leaves. Some mint leaves will darken, but continue to roast them till they turn crisp.
12. Once the leaves are roasted and dried, then remove and keep aside.
13. In the same pan, add cumin seeds, fennel seeds and roast for half a minute on a low flame.
14. Next add 1 dry red chili, broken and seeds removed. Red chili is optional, but I do add for the bit of heat it provides in the parathas.
15. Roast till the cumin seeds become fragrant. Remove aside and add them in a dry grinder or a spice grinder.
16. When the cumin and fennel seeds become warm or cool down, add the dried mint leaves.
17. Grind to a semi fine mix or a fine powder.
18. Remove in a plate. Also add 1 tbsp chaat masala.
19. Mix both the spice blends very well. Keep aside.
20. After 30 minutes, make medium sized balls of the dough.
21. Take the dough ball on the rolling board and sprinkle some flour on both sides.
22. Roll the ball to a large thin chapati of about 9 to 10 inches.
23. Spread or brush some oil all over. Sprinkle some flour evenly.
24. Now sprinkle the spice mixture that we had prepared.
25. Begin to fold from the edges like a fan with pleats.
26. Fold towards the end and then roll tightly to a circle. Press the loose end at the center downwards.
27. Prepare the pleated roll balls like these and keep aside covered to rest for 12 to 15 minutes.
28. Now take one pleated ball and dust some flour on both sides.
29. Roll to a paratha of about 5 to 6 inches.
30. Place the paratha on a hot tawa.
31. When you see the paratha puffing up at some places and is ¼th cooked then flip.
32. Spread some oil or ghee on this side.
33. Flip again and spread some oil or ghee on this side too.
34. Flip a couple of times to get even roasting and cooking of the parathas.
35. Press the edges with a spatula so that they are cooked well.
36. You can make these parathas more crisp by cooking for some more time.
37. Remove and place the pudina paratha on a plate or tray. Crush them between your palms taking care of the heat, so that the layers separate.
38. The pudina paratha is ready to be served now. 
39. Make all pudina paratha this way. If you are unable to serve them immediately, then stack them in a casserole or a roti basket and serve them once you have made all the parathas. 
40. Do note that these parathas have to be served hot or warm.

1. First chop the paneer into cubes and keep aside.
2. Finely chop the onion. 
3. Peel and crush the ginger-garlic to a fine paste in a mortar-pestle.
4. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Add the onions.
5. Keep on stirring whilst the onions are sauteing, so that there is uniform browning.
6. Saute till the onions start turning golden.
7. Then add the ginger-garlic paste. Saute till the raw aroma of the ginger-garlic goes away. About 20 to 30 seconds.
8. On a low flame add the coriander powder, red chili powder and turmeric powder.
9. Stir and saute the spice powders for a couple of seconds. Make sure you don't burn them. 
10. Then add the paneer cubes. On a low flame gently saute and stir the paneer cubes till they are coated with the masala.
11. Add cream and and continue to gently stir till the cream coats the paneer cubes well. 
12. Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes after adding the cream. Season with salt and stir.
13. Lastly sprinkle crushed kasuri methi & garam masala. Stir gently.
14. Garnish with a few coriander leaves and serve malai paneer hot as a starter snack or with naan, rotis, chapatis or bread. 200 to 250 grams Paneer

instructions:
1. In a mixing bowl, take 1 cup (125 grams) all purpose flour or maida. Add 2 tbsp besan or gram flour, a pinch of baking soda and ⅛ tsp turmeric powder.
2. Mix all the above dry ingredients with a spoon or spatula.
3. Then add water. The amount of water to be added depends on the quality of flour used. I added 1 cup water. Depending on the quality of flour and besan, you can add from ¾ to 1 cup water.
4. With the spatula or spoon, first mix. Break the small or tiny lumps with the spatula or spoon while mixing.
5. Then in round circular directions stir the batter briskly for 4 minutes. This adds volume to the batter and makes it even and smooth.
6. The batter should have a flowing consistency. Cover and keep the batter to ferment in a warm place for 12 to 15 hours. I kept for 15 hours. If you live in a cold climate, you can keep for 20 to 24 hours.
7. This is how the batter looks the next day. You will see small bubbles on the top.
8. Stir the batter and if you carefully see, the batter would have become thinner than what it was before fermentation.
9. So to thicken the batter again, add 1 to 2 tbsp of all purpose flour.
10. With a spoon mix very well.
11. Now pour this batter in the squeezy tomato ketchup bottles that we get in the market. You can also use coconut shell and make a small hole in it. You can also use a piping bag or make your own with butter paper. Depending on the capacity of the bottle, you can pour less or more in it.
12. Take 1 cup sugar in a pan. Add 1/4 tsp saffron strands to it. Do add saffron as it gives a nice orange yellow color and also its aroma to the jalebis.
13. Add 1/2 cup water.
14. Keep this pan on stove top on low flame and begin to stir, so that the sugar dissolves.
15. On a low to medium flame, cook the sugar syrup.
16. Cook till you get one string consistency in the sugar syrup.
17. Once you get the one string consistency, switch off the flame and add 1/4 tsp lime or lemon juice. Stir well. Keep the sugar syrup on the burner itself so that it remains warm when you add the jalebis in it.
18. Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai or pan. You can also use ghee or half-half of oil and ghee. Ghee gives a better flavor.
19. To check the temperature of oil, add a tiny amount of batter to the oil. If it comes up quickly and gradually the oil is hot enough for the jalebis to be fried. The frying temperature is 350 degrees fahrenheit/176 degrees celsius.
20. Now squeeze the bottle and make concentric rings with the batter.
21. Either start from the center and move outside or vice versa. Be careful while making the jalebis as the oil is hot.
22. You won't get perfect shapes as the jalebis keep on moving while you make the circles. This does require practice and it also depends on what equipment you are using to make them.
23. When one side is partly cooked, turn over and fry the other side.
24. Some jalebis will be cooked faster than others.
25. Fry till the oil stops sizzling and the jalebis are a light golden. Remove with a tongs or a bamboo skewer. While removing shake to drain the extra oil.
26. Then immediately put the fried jalebis in the sugar syrup. The sugar syrup should be slightly hot or warm when you add the jalebis in it.
27. Turn over after after a minute so that both sides are coated with the syrup.
28. Keep them in the syrup for about 2 to 3 minutes. If you keep for two minutes, they will be lightly colored and if you keep for 3 minutes, they will have a deep color.
29. Remove with a wooden skewer or tongs. Shake lightly so that the excess sugar syrup falls back in the pan. Place them in a plate or tray lined with a foil or butter paper.
30. Make all jalebi this way. Its better to have a help while doing so. Otherwise it is kind of multi-tasking.
31. Serve jalebi hot, warm or at room temperature. The leftovers can be kept in an airtight container and refrigerated. 1 cup all purpose flour 
2 tablespoon besan 
⅛ teaspoon turmeric powder 
1 pinch baking soda 
1 cup water 
1 to 2 tablespoon all purpose flour 
1 cup sugar 
½ cup water 
¼ teaspoon saffron strands 
  oil for deep frying

1. Rinse 250 grams okra in water. Then wipe dry them with a kitchen towel or just allow them to dry them naturally on a plate.
2. Slice off the crown and base of each okra and make a slit on one side.
3. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp chaat masala and 1/4 tsp salt.
4. Mix and toss the okra very well with the salt and chaat masala. Keep aside for 5 minutes.
5. Heat 4 to 5 tbsp oil in a pan and add the okra. Stir very well.
6. Saute the okra till they become tender and are just about cooked. No need to brown them.
7. Drain them on kitchen paper towels.
8. In a dry grinder, powder 14 to 15 cashews finely. If some fat releases while powdering the cashews, its alright. Keep aside.
9. Beat 1/2 cup fresh curd till smooth and keep aside.
10. Crush 1 inch ginger + 4 to 5 garlic + 2 green chilies, crushed to a paste in mortar-pestle. You can also grind these in a small grinder. Also slice the onions thinly and chop the tomato.
11. In the same pan, add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida. Saute till the cumin seeds crackle.
12. Then add 1 heaped cup of sliced onions. Stir very well.
13. Saute the onions till they light golden.
14. Then add the crushed ginger-garlic-green chili paste. Stir and saute till the raw aroma of ginger-garlic goes away.
15. Add 1/3 cup finely chopped tomatoes.
16. Stir and then add the ground cashew powder.
17. On a low to medium flame, stir and saute for 5 to 6 minutes till you see oil releasing from the sides.
18. Then add 2 tbsp besan or gram flour, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder and 1/2 tsp coriander powder.
19. Stir and saute for a minute.
20. Lower the flame and then add the beaten curd gradually.
21. As soon as you add the curd, quickly stir so that the curd does not curdle.
22. Stir and mix very well.
23. Now add 1 to 1.25 cups water. Stir again well. Season with salt as required.
24. Simmer the gravy for 2 minutes. Then add the sauteed okra. Stir very well.
25. Now add 1 tbsp milk powder/dairy whitener. 2 tbsp milk powder can also be added, but it makes the gravy a little more sweet. 
26. Substitutes for milk powder is fresh cream and khoya. If adding khoya you can add once the tomatoes are sauteed well. Saute the khoya for a minute. If adding cream, then add right at the end when the okra gravy is done.
27. Stir again. Cover and allow the okra curry to simmer for 7 to 8 minutes on a low flame.
28. Lastly add 1/2 tsp garam masala powder. You can also add 1/2 tsp kasuri methi at this step. Stir well.
29. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve shahi bhindi with chapatis or rotis. 250 grams bhindi

1. Clean up tamarind.  Check for any seeds, skin or unwanted particles and discard them.
2. Heat 3 cups of water.
3. Soak tamarind in 1.5 to 2 cups of hot water for about 45 to 60 minutes in a large bowl.
4. If your tamarind is clean then blend it well until smooth. This saves lot of time. Avoid blending if your tamarind has debris or is unclean.
5. Mash the tamarind as much as possible and pass through a filter to a heavy bottom tall pot(no wide pan). Discard more stones or debris that you might find in the filter.
6. Add the pulp back to the bowl along with left over water that was heated. Use only as required, we want to make a thick paste. Squeeze the pulp and pass through the filter once more.
7. The filtered pulp will be thick. Boil this for about 5 minutes on a medium flame. This keeps the tamarind good for a long time.
8. Cover the pot partially towards you to prevent splashes. You may stir it twice while boiling without opening the lid fully from a side.
9. After 5 minutes, turn off the flame.
10. Cool tamarind paste completely and store it in an airtight glass jar. Prevent using plastic jars and spoons.

1. First rinse and then chop the cauliflower to medium florets. Keep the cauliflower in warm water for 15 to 20 minutes. This is an optional step and only if there are insects in cauliflower. Later drain and keep aside.
2. Next rinse, peel and then chop the carrots and turnips in batons or sticks of 1.5 to 2 inches.
3. Bring 8 to 9 cups of water to a rolling boil in a deep pot.
4. Add the cauliflower florets, carrots and turnips.
5. Stir and blanch for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain the blanched veggies very well.
6. Spread them evenly on a cloth and keep to dry them in a shade or sunlight. You can also keep the ceiling fan on and let the veggies dry. The vegetables should have no moisture or water on them and must be completely dry. 
7. If there is moisture than the pickle gets spoiled. You can keep in the sunlight for half or full day. In the shade you can dry for a day or two. You can also slow dry in the oven at the lowest temperature for a few hours.
8. Once the vegetables are dried, then proceed to the next step. Add chopped onions, ginger and garlic in a blender or grinder jar.
9. Blend to a smooth paste without adding any water. Keep this ground paste aside.
10. In another pan, take 2 cups grated or powdered jaggery with 1 cup vinegar. You can also add jaggery as per your taste.
11. Keep the pan on stove top and stir so that the jaggery dissolves. Get ready to smell vinegar while cooking 🙂 however, the taste is good.
12. Simmer this jaggery and vinegar mixture on a low flame.
13. You have to cook this mixture till you get 1/2 string or 1 string jaggery consistency. I stopped at 1/2 string consistency. Keep aside.
14. In another deep pot or pan, heat 1 cup mustard oil till it smoking point.
15. Add the ground onion+ginger+garlic paste. Stir and saute.
16. You have to saute often as the onions tend to stick to the pan. So continue stirring.
17. Saute till the onion become light brown. The raw aroma of onions should go completely away. Takes about 15 to 18 minutes on a low flame.
18. Once the onions are sauteed, add the veggies. Then add 8 tsp salt, 4 tsp garam masala powder, 6 tsp red chili powder and 2 tsp split mustard seeds (optional).
19. Stir very well. Add the jaggery + vinegar solution.
20. Stir again. Simmer for 8 to 9 minutes on a medium flame.
21. Allow the pickle to cool down. Don't cover with a lid. Just place a clean kitchen towel on the pan. In a clean sterilized jar, spoon the pickle.
22. Cover tightly with a lid and allow the pickle to jar to sit at room temperature for 2 to 3 days. You can even keep for 4 to 5 days. If you want, you can keep the pickle in the sun also for 2 days.
23. Serve this sweet and sour gobi gajar shalgam achar with parathas or as a side condiment with dal rice.

1. Blend everything except the cream, cardamom powder and saffron in a blender till smooth.
2. Then add the cream, cardamom powder and saffron.
3. Blend till the cream is mixed and incorporated well in the mixture.
4. Pour the kulfi mixture in kulfi moulds or small bowls.
5. Cover with a lid or aluminium foil and keep in the freezer for the kulfi to set.
6. Once set, serve the kulfi sprinked with crushed saffron or rose water or kewra water.
7. To remove the kufi, place the kulfi moulds under running water for some seconds or rub them between your palms. With a butter knife, gently remove the kulfi. 1.5 cups whole milk

1. Take 250 grams of khoya in a plate or bowl. The khoya used for kala jamun is the soft khoya also known as hariyali khoya or chikna khoya. This is a soft khoya, so it mashes and kneads very well.
2. Mash the khoya very well with your hands. Keep aside. There should be no lumps or small bits or pieces in the khoya. You can also grate and then mash the khoya.
3. Grate 100 grams paneer and keep aside. 100 grams paneer yields about 1/2 cup grated paneer.
4. Now add the grated paneer and 3 tbsp all purpose flour (maida) to the khoya.
5. Add 1 tbsp milk. gently mix everything very well.
6. Bring together this mixture and form into a dough. Do not knead the dough. Just mix and gather to a dough. If the mixture looks dry and does not cling together to a dough, you can add 1 tbsp more of the milk.
7. Now pinch small marble sized balls from the dough and roll them in a round shape between your palms. Roll lightly and not heavily.
8. Now roll the ball again between your palms to give a oblong cylindrical shape.
9. Roll all the jamun this way and keep them covered with a cotton kitchen towel.
10. Take 2 cups sugar in a pan and add 1.5 cups water.
11. Keep this pan on stove top on a low to medium flame and stir so that the sugar begins to dissolve.
12. When all the sugar is dissolved, add 1/4 tsp lemon juice. The lemon juice does not allow the sugar syrup to crystallize.
13. Cook the sugar syrup on a low to medium flame till you get 1/2 string consistency or the syrup becomes sticky.
14. When the sugar syrup is cooking, you can begin frying the kala jamun. As when you add the kala jamun, the sugar syrup has to be hot. Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai or deep pan on a low to medium flame.
15. Switch off the flame and add 1/2 tsp cardamom powder and 12 to 15 strands of saffron, crushed. Also add 1 tbsp rose water.
16. For testing, slid a tiny dough ball in the hot oil.
17. The ball should come up slowly and not quickly. This is the temperature at which we will fry the jamuns.
18. Keep the flame to a low and fry this small jamun till it becomes golden.
19. Now gently slid the kala jamun. Do not crowd and add the jamuns as per the size of the pan.
20. When you see faint golden spots, turn over the jamun gently.
21. Keep on turning them in the oil, like a gentle swirling with the slotted spoon, so that they brown evenly. When frying the jamun have to feel light and not heavy.
22. Fry till they turn a shade or two darker than the golden fried color.
23. Place them on paper towels.
24. Whilst they are hot, quickly add them to the sugar syrup.
25. Fry all the kala jamun in the same way and add them to the sugar syrup.
26. Cover and allow them to soak in the sugar syrup. Once the sugar syrup cools down, keep the bowl covered in the fridge.
27. Serve kala jamun at room temperature or chilled as a dessert or sweet.

instructions:
1. Rinse and take tomatoes, onion, halved or quartered, 15 to 18 cashews in a heat proof bowl. 
2. Pour 2 cups of hot water. Cover and blanch these ingredients for about 25 to 30 minutes. 
3. Meanwhile, rinse or wipe dry the mushrooms. Slice or chop them. Rinse, peel and chop the potatoes in small cubes. Keep aside.
4. After 25 to 30 minutes, drain and chop the tomatoes roughly. Add the tomatoes along with their juices, blanched onions, cashews in a grinder or blender jar. 
5. Also add 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves. Without adding any water, grind to a smooth fine paste. Keep aside.
6. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Add the whole spices - 1/2 tsp caraway seeds/shahjeera or 1/2 tsp cumin seeds/jeera, 1 medium sized tej patta, 3 cloves, 2 green cardamoms, 1/2 inch cinnamon and 1 single mace strand. 
7. Saute till the spices crackle and become fragrant.
8. Then add the sliced or chopped mushrooms.
9. Stir very well and begin to saute the mushrooms.
10. While sauteing the mushrooms would begin to loose water.
11. Continue to saute on a medium flame till all the water dries up.

1. Rinse and then boil/steam potatoes till they are completely cooked. 
2. You can cook them in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles or steam them in a steamer or electric cooker.
3. When the potatoes are still warm, peel them. Crumble and keep aside.
4. In another bowl, take 1 cup fresh curd/yogurt and whisk till smooth.
5. Add 2 to 2.5 tbsp besan.
6. Next add 1.5 cups water and whisk this mixture till smooth. There should be no lumps of besan.
7. Chop the onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic and green chilies finely.

9. Then add 1/3 cup finely chopped onions.

1. To make rasmalai you will need 12 to 15 rasgullas. Either you can buy them from stores or make them at home. 
2. Boil ½ cup water. Then add almonds & pistachios. Cover and keep aside for 30 to 40 minutes.
3. After 30 minutes, peel the almonds, pistachios and slice them. Keep aside.
4. When the almonds are blanching, take 1 litre of milk in a thick bottomed pan or kadai.
5. Bring the milk to a boil on medium flame.
6. Whilst the milk is coming to a boil, take 2 tbsp milk from the pan in a small bowl. Let this milk
7. Become warm and then add crushed saffron strands. Stir and keep aside.
8. Once the milk has come to a boil, then lower the flame and simmer the milk. Collect the floating cream on the sides. Continue to cook this way till the milk is reduced to half.
9. Keep on collecting the cream which floats on the top and move it to the sides. Also keep on stirring the milk at intervals so that the milk does not get scorched at the bottom.
10. Add sugar and stir well so that the sugar dissolves.
11. Then add cardamom powder.
12. Add the sliced almonds & pistachios. Reserve a few almonds & pistachios for garnishing.
13. Also add the saffron dissolved milk.
14. Stir again. Keep simmering the reduced milk at a low flame.
15. Take each rasgulla and with a spatula apply pressure, so the excess sugar syrup is removed from it. You can also press the rasgulla in your palms. Be gentle and don't apply too much of pressure. As then the rasgullas will break. Do this with all the rasgullas.
16. Now place the rasgulla in the simmering milk and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
17. Switch off the flame and then add 1 tsp rose water or kewra water (pandanus extract).
18. Stir gently. Cover and let the rasmalai come to room temperature. Then chill and serve it garnished with some sliced almonds or pistachios and saffron strands.
19. You can also serve rasmalai warm or at room temperature.

1. Rinse the bhindi (okra) in water very well using a colander or strainer. Drain all the water. Then wipe them dry with a kitchen towel. You can even keep them spread on a plate and let them dry naturally. The bhindi should be completely dry before you proceed with the second step.
2. Slice of the crown part of each bhindi. This part is discarded. Then Slice of the base tip. This part is also discarded.
3. Next, with a knife give a slit on the bhindi without breaking it into two parts. The whole bhindi (okra) should be intact. 
4. With your thumbs and fingers gently open the sliced part and check to see if there are any worms. If there are worms or black spots, then discard the bhindi.
5. Repeat the above steps with all of the bhindi. 
6. Combine all the spice powder ingredients and salt except asafoetida in a bowl. Mix very well.
7. Stuff the masala in each bhindi with a small spoon or with your fingers.
8. Repeat with the entire lot of bhindi.
9. Take a heavy pan or kadai. Heat 2 to 3 tablespoons oil in it. Keep flame to a low and add 1 pinch asafoetida (hing). Stir. If you do not have asafoetida, then skip it.
10. Then immediately add the stuffed bhindi in the oil and gently stir.
11. If any masala remains you can add it to the bhindi. Also, add the masala which must have fallen on the chopping board while stuffing bhindi.
12. Gently mix and stir again. Cook the stuffed bhindi on a low flame. Do not cover the kadai with any lid. Let the bhindi cook on a low flame. We don't want the masala to burn hence the bhindi needs to be cooked on a low flame. Also do not add any water.
13. The bhindi should not be on top of each other. Hence arrange them separately so that each bhindi is evenly cooked. Cook the stuffed bhindi on a low flame.
14. Ensure that you check the bhindi in between and also give a gently stir after every 3 to 4 minutes. Cook on a low flame. After giving a stir make sure each stuffed bhindi is arranged separately for even cooking.
15. Slow cook till the bhindi is done and well cooked. At this point, check taste of bhindi and if salt is less then sprinkle some salt from above and stir.
16. Take ½ teaspoon kasuri methi (dry fenugreek leaves) in your palms. Crush kasuri methi and sprinkle on the bharwa bhindi. Also add ¼ teaspoon garam masala powder. If you do not have kasuri methi, then skip adding.
17. Mix very well and switch off the flame.
18. Lastly, add 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves and mix again. 
19. Serve bharwa bhindi with rotis and yogurt or raita. It also goes well with a combination of dal and rice. You can garnish it with coriander leaves. You can even squeeze lime or lemon on bharwa bhindi before you serve. 2 to 3 tablespoons oil

½ teaspoon cumin powder

1. Soak cashews in hot water for 30 mins.
2. Rinse the mushrooms very well. Wipe them and then chop them.
3. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Add the mushrooms and saute till they become light golden.
4. The mushrooms would first begin to release its juices.
5. When the juices dry up and the oil is seen, saute the mushroom further till they get light golden at the edges. Remove them and keep aside.
6. Steam or cook the peas (matar) till they are tender. Drain and keep aside.
7. Make a paste of the onion, ginger and garlic with 1 tbsp water in a grinder or blender.
8. Drain the soaked cashews. Add to a grinder or blender and make a paste of the tomatoes and cashews.
9. No need to add water while making the tomato-cashew paste. The juices of the tomatoes would be enough to make the paste. 
10. Make sure the cashews are ground thoroughly and there should be no bits and pieces of cashews in the paste.
11. In the same pan which we fried mushrooms, add 1 tbsp butter. Melt the butter.
12. Add bay leaf and saute for a few seconds.
13. Add the onion-ginger-garlic paste and saute stirring often till the paste becomes golden.
14. Then add the tomato-cashew paste and saute stirring till the oil leaves the sides of the paste.
15. Add all the spice powders - red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala and coriander powder.
16. Stir and saute for 2-3 minutes more.
17. The whole mixture would come together as one mass with the fat being seen at the sides.
18. Add the water, salt and sugar.
19. Stir and then add green chilies. Simmer till the makhani gravy thickens.
20. Then add the crushed kasuri methi, cream and julienned ginger.
21. Stir and simmer the curry for half a minute.
22. Serve hot with naan or chapati or cumin rice.

1. Take 1/3 cup sugar in a dry grinder or a small blender.

5. You have to stir often while roasting the flour so that there is even roasting and browning.

8. Begin to mix very well.
9. Keep on stirring and roasting this mixture for 3 to 5 minutes more. Again here timing will vary with the material, size and thickness of the pan.

3. When the rice is soaking, rinse and chop the methi leaves and other veggies. 
4. Crush ginger, garlic and green chilies in a mortar-pestle. You can also grind them in a small chutney grinder.
5. Heat in a 2 or 3 litre pressure cooker and fry the following spices until they splutter and are fragrant –  cumin seeds, cardamom, green cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves and single strand of mace (optional).
6. Then add thinly sliced onions. Stir often and sauté the onions until they start turning golden.
7. Then add the crushed ginger+garlic+green chilli paste. Stir and saute for a few seconds until the raw aroma of ginger and garlic goes away.
8. Now add the finely chopped methi leaves. Stir and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes on a low to medium heat.
9. Then add chopped mix vegetables and mix well. You can add veggies of your choice.
10. Add turmeric powder, red chili powder and coriander powder. Mix very well again.
11. Add the soaked basmati rice. Stir and saute for a minute.
12. Pour water. Season with salt as required and mix. You can also make the methi rice in a pan or pot. Add 2 to 2.5 cups of water if making in a pan.
13. Pressure cook on medium to high flame for 2 to 3 whistles or 8 to 9 minutes. When the pressure settles down on its own, remove the lid. Gently fluff the rice.
14. Serve methi pulao hot with plain curd or raita. I served with aloo raita. 
15. With raita: Serve methi rice with plain curd or raita. Methi pulao will pair nicely with most raita varieties like onion raita, cucumber raita, boondi raita or onion tomato raita. 
16. With Dal: Even with a simple dal fry or dal tadka, methi pulao tastes delicious.
17. In a lunch box: Methi rice also stays good in the lunch box for some hours. When packing it in a lunch box, add a side of veggie salad or a mango or lemon pickle. You can also pack it for short travels.
18. I do not recommend to freeze or make a large batch for freezing. Cooked rice is better had fresh on the same day. If you have any leftovers than store in the fridge for a day only and not more than a day. Before serving, steam in a pan or Instant pot for 5 minutes. 1 cup basmati rice 
2 cups methi leaves 
1 cup chopped mix vegetables 
1  medium to large onion, 
1 inch ginger 
¼ teaspoon turmeric powder 
½ teaspoon red chili powder 
½ teaspoon coriander powder 
2 cups water 
2 to 3 tablespoon oil 
  salt 
½ teaspoon cumin seeds 
1  black cardamom 
2  green cardamoms 
1 inch cinnamon 
3 to 4  cloves 
1 or 2  single strand of mace

1. Wash rice and cook to slightly grainy. Do not make the rice mushy.
2. I cooked 2 cups basmati rice with 3½ cups water in a pressure cooker for 1 whistle on a medium high flame.
3. Released the pressure manually using a spoon. Fluff up with a fork and cool completely. While the rice cooks, make the capsicum masala ready.
4. Heat oil in a pan. Fry cumin & bay leaf or curry leaves till it turns aromatic. 
5. Add onions and chili fry until the onions turn slightly pink.
6. Then add ginger garlic paste and saute till the raw smell goes away. Transfer capsicum and green peas. Fry for 3 minutes.
7. Add mint, coriander, chilli powder, garam masala and salt. Fry for about 2 minutes till the mixture turns aromatic.
8. Add the 2 tbsp water and cook on a low flame till the water evaporates.
9. Then add cooled rice to the capsicum mixture along with lemon and salt. Mix well. Serve capsicum rice warm with a raita.
10. Press SAUTE button on the Instant pot and pour oil to the inner steel insert.
11. Add cumin. When the seeds splutter, add curry leaves, green chilli and onions. Saute until the onions turn golden.
12. Next add ginger garlic and saute for 30 seconds. Then add in the capsicum and peas.
13. Saute for 2 to 3 mins until the capsicum is done to your liking. Then add salt, turmeric, red chilli powder, garam masala and mint leaves.
14. Give a good stir and pour 2 tbsps of water. Press CANCEL button.
15. Deglaze the pot and mix everything well. The heat in the pot will cook the masala and evaporate the water completely. 
16. Remove this to a plate and set aside.
17. Add soaked rice and pour water. For 2 cups basmati rice, you will need 2.5 cups water. For 2 cups sona masuri rice, you will need 4 cups water. 
18. Give a good stir to ensure there are no food particles stuck at the bottom. Secure the Instant pot with the lid and position the steam release handle to sealing.
19. Press PRESSURE COOK button and set the timer to 5 mins for basmati rice or 10 mins for sona masuri rice. 
20. For basmati rice, release the pressure manually after 5 mins. Remove the pot and cool the rice a bit. 
21. Then add the coriander leaves,  capsicum masala and lemon juice to the pot. Give a good mix. Adjust salt if needed.Serve capsicum rice with yogurt or curd. 2 cups rice  uncooked
2 tablespoons oil  or as needed
1 medium onion thinly sliced
1 green chili  slit (optional)
¾ to 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste (or chopped)
½ cup green peas (optional)
1½ to 2 cups capsicums or bell pepper chopped 
2 tablespoons coriander leaves chopped
¼ cup mint leaves (pudina) chopped
1½ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
2 tablespoons water
2 tablespoons lemon juice or as needed (optional)
1 sprig  curry leaves or biryani leaf or bay leaf 
½ teaspoon cumin or jeera or shahi jeera
1½ teaspoons garam masala or bisi bele bath or biryani masala (adjust as needed)
½ to ¾ teaspoon red chili powder (skip if included in masala)
¼ teaspoon turmeric or haldi

1. Soak sabja seeds in water for about 20 to 30 mins. Once they swell then drain the extra water and keep aside.
2. Prepare the falooda sev according to package instructions.
3. Some require just soaking the falooda sev in warm water. I had to cook them in boiling water much like noodles. So I heated up 1.5 cups water and let it come to a boil. You can heat about 1.5 to 2 cups water. 
4. Then added 5 tablespoons sev (roughly ⅓ cup). If the faluda sev are long, then just chop them before cooking. 
5. Boil the faluda sev in the hot water on medium flame till they are softened and cooked well.
6. Once cooked, using strainer or colander, drain the extra water. Then rinse the cooked falooda sev in fresh water. Drain the water again. Keep covered aside till they are cooled completely at room temperature. 
7. Chop the nuts. 
8. In 4 tall glasses each, add 1.5 to 2 tablespoons rose syrup. Depending upon your taste you can add less or more of the rose syrup. 
9. Then add 2 tablespoons soaked sabja seeds. 
10. Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of the faluda sev.
11. In a slow stream, pour about 1 cup milk.
12. Then top with one scoop of vanilla ice cream.
13. Garnish with a few raisins, sliced pistachios, almonds or cashews. Prepare the remaining falooda drink in the same way. 
14. Serve the falooda immediately. while drinking, with a spoon mix the rose syrup settled at the bottom with the milk and then drink. ½ tablespoon sabja seeds 
1 to 1.25 cups water 
5 tablespoons falooda sev

6 tablespoons rose syrup 
6 tablespoons soaked sabja seeds 
12 tablespoons cooked falooda sev 
4 cups chilled whole milk 
4  scoops of vanilla ice cream 
10 to 12  unsalted pistachios 
10 to 12  almonds

10 to 12  golden raisins

instructions:
1. First take 2 cups whole wheat flour, ½ tsp salt and 2 tsp oil in a mixing bowl or pan.
2. Mix very well. then add ½ cup water and begin to knead. 
3. Add more water if required while kneading.
4. Knead to a soft and smooth dough. 
5. Cover and keep aside for 30 minutes.
6. Steam fresh green peas in a pressure cooker or electric rice cooker. Steam the green peas and do not boil them in water. 
7. For steaming, take the green peas in a pan. Add 1 cup water in the cooker. 
8. Place the pan with the green peas in the cooker. Now pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistles. I used electric rice cooker to steam the green peas.
9. Drain the green peas very well. there should not be any water in them. Allow them to become warm or cool at room temperature.
10. Mash the green peas coarsely with a potato masher. Keep aside.
11. Heat a pan. Lower the flame and add ½ tsp cumin seeds in it.
12. Roast the cumin seeds till they become fragrant.
13. Remove and add the roasted cumin seeds to the mashed peas.
14. In the same pan, on a low flame, add 1 tbsp besan. Stirring often, roast the besan.
15. The besan should become aromatic. its rawness should go away. The color of besan will also change. Do not brown too much or burn the besan.
16. Add the roasted besan to the mashed peas.
17. Add 1 green chili, finely chopped, a pinch of asafoetida (hing), 1 to 1.5 tbsp finely chopped coriander leaves, salt as per taste. 
18. You can also add 1/4 tsp garam masala powder. mix very well.
19. Pinch small balls from the dough. Roll them and keep covered.
20. Take 2 small balls and dust them with whole wheat flour.
21. Roll each of them to a round of 4 to 5 inches in diameter.
22. Place the green peas stuffing on one of the rolled round.
23. Cover with the second one and seal the edges firmly. Sprinkle some wheat flour on both sides.
24. Roll gently to a paratha of about 6 to 7 inches. Sprinkle flour as required while rolling.
25. Heat a tawa and let it become hot. Place the peas paratha on the hot tawa. On a medium to high flame, begin to roast the paratha.
26. When one side is partially cooked (about 1/4th) then flip the paratha.
27. Spread some oil or ghee on top. Flip the matar paratha again.
28. Now spread some oil or ghee on this side too.
29. If the matar paratha has been stuffed and rolled well, it will start puffing up while cooking.
30. Flip again. Press the paratha edges with a spatula too, so that they are cooked.
31. Flip once more and roast till the peas paratha is evenly cooked and has golden blisters on top.
32. Serve peas paratha hot. you can also stack them in roti basket and later serve warm. Serve peas paratha for breakfast with a side accompaniment of lemon or mango pickle. You can also serve with some butter or curd. 2 cups whole wheat flour 
½ teaspoon salt 
2 teaspoon oil 
½ to ⅔ cup water for kneading, 
1.25 cups fresh peas 
½ teaspoon cumin seeds 
1 tablespoon besan 
1 to 1.5 tablespoon finely chopped coriander leaves 
1  green chili 
1 pinch asafoetida 
¼ teaspoon garam masala 
  salt as required 
  oil

1. On a low or medium flame, heat oil or ghee in a deep pan.
2. Add 1 inch cinnamon stick, 1 teaspoon caraway seeds, 1 bay leaf, 3 cloves, 2 to 3 green cardamoms and 2 black cardamoms.
3. Fry the spices till the oil becomes fragrant.
4. Now lower the flame. Add the ½ teaspoon dry ginger powder (saunth) and 1 teaspoon fennel powder (saunf powder). stir well.
5. Add 1 cup of soaked and drained basmati rice and stir.
6. Add 2 pinches of crushed saffron (kesar). saute for a minute.
7. Pour 2 cups of water and salt as required. Stir and cover the pan tightly. When the rice is cooking, prepare the garnish.
8. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a frying pan. Add the sliced onions.
9. Also add a pinch of salt and fry the onions till they are golden or caramelized and crisp. Remove and drain on paper tissues.
10. In the same oil, first fry the 10 to 12 almonds till they become crisp. Remove and drain fried almonds on paper tissues.
11. Now fry 10 to 12 cashews till they are crisp and lightly browned. drain them on paper tissues.
12. Also fry 10 to 12 walnuts till they are crisp and lightly browned. remove fried walnuts. Drain them on paper tissues.
13. Cook the rice till all the water is absorbed and the rice is cooked. When done, fluff the rice.
14. While serving the kashmiri pulao, garnish with the fried onions and dry fruits.
15. Serve kashmiri pulao hot with raita or salad. ['rice minutes',

1. Add rinsed tuvar/arhar dal, onions, garlic, green chillies, turmeric and asafoetida/hing in a 2 litre pressure cooker.
2. Add water. Pressure cook the lentils for 10 to 11 minutes or 8 to 9 whistles till you get a smooth mashable consistency in the dal.
3. Mash the dal with a spoon or wired whisk. 
4. If the dal become thick, you can add some hot water and make it medium consistency. You can also have a thick consistency of this dal, if you prefer. Season with salt. Stir and keep aside.
5. Heat ghee or oil in a small pan. Splutter the cumin first.
6. Then add garlic. Saute the garlic for some seconds. A light brown garlic is also fine.
7. Switch off the flame and add red chili powder, asafoetida (hing) and dry fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). Stir.
8. Pour the entire tempering in the lasooni dal. Stir.
9. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve dal lasooni hot, with steamed basmati rice or a fragrant rice like ambe mohur. You can also serve it with rotis and bread too.
10. You can also add some lemon juice to the dal toward the end, to give a slight tang to dal lasooni. ½ cup arhar dal 
1.5 to 1.75 cups water 
1 to 1.5 tablespoons garlic 
¼ cup finely chopped onions 
1 to 2  green chillies 
1 pinch asafoetida 
½ teaspoon turmeric powder 
  salt as required 
1 teaspoon  garlic 
½ teaspoon cumin 
1.5 to 2 tablespoons ghee 
½ teaspoon kashmiri red chilli powder 
1 pinch asafoedita 
½ teaspoon dry fenugreek leaves 
½ to 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves 
½ teaspoon lemon juice

1. Take the rice in a small bowl or pan. Mash the rice with your hands or with a spoon. Mashing the rice gives a soft texture to the pakoras.
2. Its always better to use rice which are cooked really well. 
3. If the rice appears dry after removing from fridge, then just sprinkle some water on it and microwave for a few minutes.
4. Add all the rest of the ingredients to the rice - besan/gram flour, chopped onions & ginger, coriander leaves, green chilies and all the spice powders. Add salt.
5. Mix well and keep aside for for 8 to 10 minutes. The onions would release their juices and make the mixture a bit soft. Then you can add water as required.
6. After adding water, stir and mix very well.
7. Heat oil for frying in a kadai or pan.
8. Take spoonfuls and drop the mixture in hot oil. Keep the temperature to medium heat.
9. Let the rice pakora get cooked & browned lightly and then you turn them over and continue to fry.
10. Deep fry till the rice pakoda are crisp and golden. 
11. Drain on paper kitchen towels to remove excess oil.
12. Serve rice pakora with green chutney or tomato sauce. 1 cup cooked rice 
1  medium onion, 
1  green chili 
1 inch ginger 
¼ cup chopped coriander leaves 
½ teaspoon ajwain 
½ teaspoon cumin powder 
½ teaspoon coriander powder 
¼ teaspoon turmeric powder 
1 pinch asafoetida 
5 tablespoon besan 
5 to 6 tablespoon water 
  salt as required 
  oil for deep frying

1. First blanch the almonds in hot water. Soak 20 to 22 almonds in 1/2 cup of bubbling hot water for 30 to 40 minutes. Cover and keep aside.
2. In a pan, take 3/4 cup roughly chopped onions and add 1/4 cup water.
3. Heat the chopped onion and water together stirring at intervals. If in case the water dries up while cooking onions, then add some more water.
4. Simmer till the onions soften.
5. After 30 minutes, peel the almonds and keep aside.
6. Add the blanched and peeled almonds and 1/4 cup of the soaking water to a grinder or small blender.
7. Make a smooth paste from the almonds without any tiny bits or pieces. Remove and keep the almond paste aside.
8. To the same blender, add the cooked onions along with the remaining stock. Grind to a smooth paste.
9. Take 6 tbsp full fat fresh curd/yogurt in a bowl or measuring cup and whisk well till smooth.
10. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pan.
11. Add the whole spices - 1/2 tsp shah jeera (caraway seeds), 1 inch cinnamon, 2 to 3 green cardamoms, 4 cloves, 2 to 3 single strands of mace and 1 small to medium tej patta/indian bay leaf. Saute the spices for some seconds till aromatic.
12. Now add the ground onion paste and stir very well.
13. Add 2 tsp ginger garlic paste. Stir again.
14. Saute the onion paste till you see some fat releasing from the sides and the paste thickens. We don't need to brown this paste as we are preparing a white gravy.
15. Now add the ground almond paste.
16. Stir continuously and saute for two minutes on a low flame.
17. Then add 1 or 2 slit green chilies, 1/4 tsp black pepper or white pepper and 1/2 tsp coriander powder. Stir again.
18. Saute for a minute on a low flame.
19. Now just add 1 to 1.5 tbsp of the beaten curd (yogurt or dahi) on a low flame.
20. Briskly stir and incorporate the curd with the rest of the mixture.
21. Then add again 1 to 1.5 tbsp of the curd.
22. Stir quickly again. Adding yogurt in small amounts like this does not allow it to curdle in the gravy.
23. Finish off all the curd/yogurt this way and keep on stirring.
24. Then add 3/4 to 1 cup water.
25. Stir very well so that the whole gravy has a uniform consistency. Add salt as required.
26. Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer on a low flame. About 4 to 5 minutes.
27. Then add the paneer cubes. 200 grams paneer which have been chopped in cubes and stir gently. Simmer for a minute.
28. Then add 3 tbsp low fat cream. Stir well and switch off the flame.
29. Lastly, add 1 tsp of rosewater or kewra (pandanus) water or half-half of both. Stir the gravy gently.
30. Serve paneer korma garnished with crushed saffron or saffron powder.
31. This paneer kurma goes very well with naans, tandoori roti, chapatis or parathas. It also goes well with cumin rice or veg pulao. 20 to 22  almonds 
¼ cup water for soaking almonds 
4 tablespoon water or the almond soaked water for grinding almonds 
150 grams onions 
¼ cup water for cooking onions 
200 grams Paneer 
½ teaspoon shah jeera 
¼ teaspoon black pepper powder 
½ teaspoon coriander powder 
1 inch cinnamon 
2 to 3  green cardamoms 
4  cloves 
2 to 3  single strands of mace 
2 teaspoon Ginger-Garlic Paste 
1  green chili, 
6 tablespoon full fat fresh curd 
3 tablespoon low fat cream 
1 teaspoon rose water 
¾ to 1 cup water 
2 tablespoon ghee 
  a few pinches of crushed or powdered saffron for garnish 
  salt as required

1. Blanch 6 to 7 dried figs and 1 tbsp raisins in hot water. For blanching, boil 1/3 cup water and take it in a bowl. Add the dried figs and raisins. Cover and keep the bowl aside for 20 minutes. After 20 minutes, drain and keep aside. If the figs are not too dry, then you do not need to blanch them.
2. When the figs are blanching, take the following dry fruits in a grinder or food processor - 1/4 cup almonds, 1/4 cup cashews, 1/4 cup pistachios and 1/4 cup walnuts.
3. Pulse the dry fruits for 3 to 4 times or more till you get them in small bits and pieces. Don' t make a powder or paste. You can also chop them finely. For saving time use a mixer or food processor. After pulsing, if you get slightly large pieces of almonds in the mixture, then remove and chop them.
4. Remove the coarse mixture of dry fruits and keep aside.
5. In the same grinder jar, add figs, raisins and 3/4 cup dates (chopped).
6. Now grind these into a coarse paste. Keep aside.
7. Heat 1 tsp coconut oil in a pan. Add 1 tbsp white sesame seeds. You can use ghee instead of coconut oil.
8. On a low flame, stir and saute till the sesame seeds crackle and their color changes. Sesame seeds are optional and you can skip them. You can also add poppy seeds instead of sesame seeds. Let the poppy seeds crackle before you add coconut.
9. Then add 2 tbsp desiccated coconut. Just stir the coconut. No need to brown it.
10. Then add the ground dry fruits.
11. Stir and saute for about 3 to 4 minutes on a low flame.
12. Add the ground dates-figs-raisins paste and stir lightly.
13. Then switch off the flame and add 2 tsp rose water. You can also use 1/4 to 1/2 tsp cardamom powder or a few saffron strands instead of rose water.
14. Keep the pan down and mix very well.
15. When the barfi mixture is less hot or warm, then divide into two parts.
16. Apply a bit of coconut oil on your palms and roll each mixture part into a log.
17. Allow to cool at room temperature and then slice. 
18. You can also spread the dry fruits barfi mixture in a greased plate or tray. 
19. On cooling slice in squares. Remove the slices and keep them covered in a container. Refrigerate.
20. Serve dry fruits burfi as a diwali sweet or as an after meal dessert.

1. Prepare the whole wheat dough and keep it aside.
2. Grate the mooli (radish) and keep aside for 15-20 minutes and later squeeze the water from it. 
3. This is done so that the mooli paratha do not break while rolling the dough. This radish juice can be used to make the dough instead of water.
4. Add chopped green chilies to the grated mooli.
5. Now take two lemon sized ball from the dough and roll them into a small circle, about 5 to 6 cms on the rolling board dusted with wheat flour.
6. Take a good amount of the mooli stuffing and place it on one of the rolled dough. 
7. Don't use too much stuffing as in that case the mooli parathas can break while rolling.
8. Sprinkle evenly one or two pinch of salt, red chilli powder and garam masala powder. Cover with the other rolled round and join the edges.
9. In the meantime, heat the griddle or tava. Roll the dough into the size of a paratha or roti. 
10. Care should be taken while rolling the dough as the paratha may break.
11. We have added salt to the mooli and thus as a result some juice will start oozing out from the mooli paratha. Its ok.
12. Fry the paratha on a hot tava or griddle using ghee and oil. 
13. The paratha should become golden and crisp from both sides.
14. Make sure that the paratha edges are fried well. You can use spatula to press them.
15. Use a liberal amount of ghee or oil to fry the paratha. A well-fried paratha will have some brown spots and might puff up little.
16. Serve Punjabi Mooli Paratha hot with butter or curd or the pickle of your choice. 1  medium to large mooli 
1 or 2  green chilies 
  red chilli powder 
  Garam Masala Powder 
  whole wheat flour dough 
  ghee 
  white butter 
  salt

1. Rinse the palak or spinach leaves (250 grams) very well in running water. Just chop roughly and keep aside. 250 grams spinach gives about 5 cups roughly chopped spinach.
2. Boil 3 cups water in a pan or microwave or electric heater. If using an electric heater, then pour the hot water in a bowl. Add ¼ tsp salt to the hot water and stir.
3. Then add the spinach leaves in the hot water. Close with a lid and let the spinach leaves sit in the water for 2-3 mins.
4. Strain the spinach leaves. Keep the stock aside as we can use later. Immediately add the strained spinach leaves in a bowl containing cold water. Water in which some ice cubes are added. Just add 8 to 10 ice cubes to 3 cups water to get cold water. Allow the spinach leaves to be in the cold water for a minute or two.
5. Now add the spinach leaves in a blender or grinder along with a chopped green chili, 1/2 inch ginger (chopped) and 1 or 2 garlic (chopped).
6. Blend to a smooth puree. No need to add water while blending. Keep the puree aside.
7. In a pan or kadai/wok heat 2 tbsp oil. Then add the whole spices - 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 inch cinnamon, 2 green cardamoms, 3 to 4 cloves, 1 tejpatta/indian bay leaf & 1 black cardamom. Saute for some seconds till the spices become fragrant.
8. Then add 1/2 cup finely chopped onion.
9. Saute till the onions start becoming golden.
10. Then add each 1 tsp chopped ginger and garlic. Saute till their raw aroma goes away.
11. Now add 1/2 cup finely chopped tomatoes.
12. Saute the tomatoes till they soften completely and you see oil releasing from the sides of the mixture. Takes about 2 to 3 minutes on a low to medium flame.
13. Add 2 cups chopped mushrooms. Stir them well.
14. When sauteing the mushrooms, in the beginning, you will them releasing a lot of water.
15. Continue to saute till all the water dries up and the mushrooms start turning light golden around the edges.
16. Add 1 tsp kasuri methi which has been crushed. Stir.
17. Then add 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp red chili powder and 1/4 tsp garam masala powder.
18. Stir very well again so that the spices get incorporated evenly in the mushroom mixture.
19. Add the spinach puree. Stir again.
20. Now add 2/3 to 3/4 cup water. You can adjust the amount of water as required. Season with salt.
21. Stir and bring the curry to a simmer on a low to medium flame for 6 to 7 minutes.
22. Now add 2 to 3 tbsp fresh cream. The cream can be low fat or whipping cream.
23. Stir the gravy very well so that the cream is mixed evenly in it and then switch off the flame. Check the taste and add more salt or red chili powder or garam masala powder if required.
24. Serve palak mushroom hot with some naan bread, tandoori rotis, steamed rice, cumin rice or veg pulao.

1. First rinse and then soak 2 to 3 dry red chillies in ⅓ cup hot water for 20 to 30 minutes. Use kashmiri red chilies or byadagi chilies, which have low heat. Otherwise the curry will become spicy. When the chilies are soaking, you can prep other ingredients like removing spices, chopping onions, coriander and mint leaves.
2. In a grinder jar take the following spices - 2 teaspoons coriander seeds, ½ teaspoon cumin seeds, 1 inch cinnamon, 2 cloves, 2 green cardamoms, 3 to 4 black pepper and seeds from 1 black cardamom.
3. Grind coarsely.
4. Then add 1 cup roughly chopped onions and the soaked dry red chilies. Also add 2 to 3 tablespoons of the soaked red chilies water.
5. Grind to a smooth masala paste. Keep aside.
6. In another bowl, take ⅓ cup fresh curd and whisk it till smooth.
7. Melt 3 tablespoons ghee in a pan. Lower the flame.
8. Add the ground masala paste. stir well.
9. Cover the pan as the paste splutters.
10. Remove the lid when the mixture stops spluttering.
11. Then add ½ teaspoon ginger-garlic paste.
12. Mix and continue to sauté the masala till you see ghee releasing from the sides. The masala paste will thicken and you will see the fat releasing from the sides.
13. Next add 1 green chilli (slit or sliced), 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves and 1 tablespoon chopped mint leaves or ½ teaspoon dried mint leaves. Mix very well.
14. Next add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder.
15. Mix turmeric powder very well with the masala.
16. Keep the flame to a low and add the beaten curd. As soon as you add the beaten curd, quickly stir and mix it very well with the masala.
17. On a low to medium flame, sauté this mixture. After adding curd, if mixture splutters, then cover with lid and cook.
18. Saute till you see ghee floating on the top and at the sides.
19. Then add the chopped veggies. Season with salt. mix very well.
20. Add water. Water can be less or more as per the gravy consistency you want.
21. Cover the pan with a lid. Simmer the gravy on a low to medium flame till the veggies are cooked.
22. Do check a couple of times when the veggies are cooking.
23. Simmer till the veggies are done and tender.
24. Serve vegetable masala hot with chapatis, tandoori rotis or naan. 105 grams onion 
2 to 3  red chillies 
2 teaspoons coriander seeds 
½ teaspoon cumin seeds 
1  inch cinnamon 
2  cloves 
2  green cardamoms 
4  whole black peppers 
  seeds from 1 black cardamom 
3 to 4 tablespoons water 
1.25 to 1.5 cups mixed vegetables, 
⅓ cup Curd 
1  green chilli 
1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves 
1 tablespoon chopped mint leaves 
¼ teaspoon turmeric powder 
½ teaspoon Ginger-Garlic Paste 
3 tablespoons ghee 
¾ to 1 cup water 
  salt as required 
1 tablespoon coriander leaves for garnish

1. Take 2 cups whole wheat flour/atta in a mixing bowl or a large plate.
2. Add all the spices - 1/4 teaspoon cumin seeds, 1/4 teaspoon carom seeds, 1/4 teaspoon crushed black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala powder and 1/2 teaspoon dry mango powder. Also add salt as per taste.
3. Mix very well.

33. Also add the leftover marinade. Stir and saute for 4 to 5 minutes.
34. Now add 1 cup water. Stir so that the water gets evenly mixed with the rest of the masala.
35. Add salt as required. Add 1/4 to 1/2 tsp sugar or as required.
36. Bring the curry or gravy to a simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.
37. Add the sauteed or grilled mushrooms.

1. Soak tamarind in water overnight or for 4-5 hours in a small bowl or pan.
2. With your hands, squeeze the pulp from the tamarind in the same bowl or pan.
3. Strain the pulp and keep aside.
4. Heat oil in a small pan. lower the flame & add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
5. Add ginger powder, red chili powder, asafoetida. Stir and add the strained tamarind pulp. cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
6. Add the jaggery and salt and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more. the mixture would thicken.
7. Let the saunth chutney mixture cool.

10. Remove and keep aside in a small bowl.
11. Rinse ½  cup urad dal and 4 tbsp moong dal in water a couple of times. Then soak both the lentils overnight or for at least 4 to 5 hours.
12. Drain them very well. Add the lentils to a grinder jar along with ½ tsp cumin seeds and a generous pinch of asafoetida. You can also add 1 tsp of roughly chopped ginger if you want.
13. Add water in parts and grind all the ingredients to a smooth fluffy batter. On touching the batter, it should not feel grainy. I added 6 to 7 tbsp water. Depending on the quality of lentils and the capacity-volume of grinder, you can add less or more water. Don't add too much water as then the vadas become too crispy and soak a lot of oil.
14. Take the ground batter in a bowl and add salt.
15. Stir the batter briskly for a couple of minutes. This brisk stirring makes the batter more light and fluffy.
16. The test to a correct consistency of this batter is the floating test. Take some water in a small bowl. Add 1 tsp of a batter in the water. The batter should float. If it does not float, this means the consistency is thin. Add some sooji or rice flour to the batter to thicken it.
17. Heat a kadai or pan with oil for deep frying.
18. When the oil becomes medium hot, add a small amount of batter in the oil. It should come steadily and quickly on the surface. This means it is the right temperature to fry. Too cold oil will make the vadas soggy with oil and too high will brown them faster from outside, leaving the center uncooked.
19. Add spoonfuls of the batter in the oil. Add according to the capacity of the pan or kadai.
20. When they become pale golden, then turn them.
21. Fry the vada till they become golden and crisp. Turn them a couple of times for even frying.
22. Fry till golden and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon.
23. Drain on paper towels. Fry all the vadas in the same way.
24. Once all the vadas are done with frying, then take 2.5 cups water in a wide bowl or pan.
25. And add the vada to the water. Soak them for 20 to 25 minutes.
26. Take each vada and flatten and press between your palms to remove excess water. Do this with all the vadas.
27. Take 2 cups fresh chilled curd in a bowl and beat it till smooth.
28. Now gently place these vadas in the curd.
29. Gently mix if you have used medium sized bowl, like how I have used. Now you can keep the vadas with the curd in the fridge and assemble when you want to serve. Or use them right away as the curd is chilled.

1. First soak 12 to 15 cashews in hot water for 30 minutes.

1. In a mixing bowl, take 2 cups whole wheat flour/atta (240 grams) and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Also add 1 tablespoon ghee or oil.
2. Now add water in parts and knead to a smooth soft dough. I added 3/4 cup water. Depending on the quality of flour, you can add 3/4 to 1 cup water.
3. Knead till smooth and soft. Cover the dough and keep aside.
4. In a mortar-pestle take 1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds and 1/2 teaspoon saunf (fennel seeds). Lightly crush them and keep aside.

7. Now add 1/2 teaspoon ajwain, 1/2 teaspoon nigella seeds and 1/2 teaspoon red chilli powder, 1 to 2 teaspoons chopped green chilies, 1 teaspoon finely chopped ginger, 1 teaspoon finely chopped garlic, 2 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves and 1/4 teaspoon black salt. 16. Now place the stuffing.

1. Take sugar in a grinder jar.
2. Grind to a fine powder. Remove in a plate and keep aside.
3. Keep all the ingredients ready before you begin. Heat desi ghee in a heavy kadai. Please do not use a non-stick kadai. A heavy iron kadai or aluminium kadai works best for frying gond.
4. Let the ghee melt. Keep flame to medium low.
5. Add almonds. stirring often fry almonds till their color changes and then remove with a slotted spoon. Keep aside.
6. Now add cashews. stirring often fry cashews till they become light golden or golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and keep aside.
7. Add pistachios. Fry for some seconds till their colour changes. remove and keep aside.
8. Now in the same ghee, add one piece of gond. 
9. If the gond comes up gradually and puffs up, the oil is ready for the gond to be fried. If the gond settles down in the oil, then increase the flame and let oil become hot. If the gond comes up quickly, then oil is very hot. Reduce the flame to lower the oil temperature.
10. Add gond in two batches. If you are an experienced cook, then add gond in a single batch. 
11. Stir non-stop and fry gond till all of them puff up.
12. The gond pieces have to be fried evenly. So stir non-stop. Fry them well in ghee and do not burn them.
13. Remove the puffed up gond in a slotted spoon. keep fried gond aside.
14. Reduce the flame to a low and then add 2 cups whole wheat flour in the same ghee.
15. Mix flour very well with ghee. begin to roast flour with the ghee.
16. Meanwhile when atta is getting roasted, add dry fruits in a grinder jar. also add the fried gond in a dry grinder jar.
17. Pulse and grind to a semi fine or coarse powder. You can keep dry fruits whole if you want. Do note that atta is getting roasted when you grind gond. If you are not able to multitask then switch off flame after frying gond. Crush gond in grinder. Then switch on flame again and let ghee become slightly hot. Add atta and roast. You can also use a belan (rolling pin) and crush gond. Keep the powdered gond and dry fruits aside.
18. Continue to keep on stirring and roasting the atta.
19. Roast atta till its color changes and you get a nutty aroma.
20. Then stir nonstop when you see the flour changing its color.
21. Stir and roast till the atta becomes golden or brown. Overall it took me a total of 17 minutes for the atta to get roasted to perfection (i had used a heavy iron kadai). Note that the timing will vary with the material, size and thickness of the kadai or pan. If you use steel kadai, then it will take less time.
22. Switch off the flame. Keep the kadai down and raisins and cardamom powder.
23. Next add the powdered sugar. add the crushed gond and dry fruit mixture.
24. Begin to mix with a spoon. While mixing, break the sugar lumps if any in the ladoo mixture with a spatula or spoon. mix very well.
25. When the laddu mixture is still hot and the heat is tolerable to you, take a heaped size portion of it in a spoon or in your palms. Shape in a round ladoo. 
26. In case the heat is not tolerable, then do wait for some minutes. Avoid burning your hands. If the mixture does not hold shape, then add 1 to 2 tablespoons ghee. Note that the ghee should be in a semi-solid state at room temperature.
27. Make medium sized ladoo from this whole mixture. Store them in an airtight steel container (steel dabba). 
28. They stay good for a couple of months. This recipe can be easily doubled or tripled. From this gond laddu recipe, you can make 17 to 18 laddu.
29. Serve gond ke laddu just by itself or with some hot or warm milk. 250  grams  whole wheat flour 
100  grams  gond  
200  grams  sugar  
2  tablespoons  almonds 
2  tablespoons  cashews 
2  tablespoons  pistachios  
2  tablespoons  raisins 
1  teaspoon  cardamom powder 
½  cup  desi ghee + 4 tablespoons at room temperature https://i2.wp.com/www.vegrecipesofindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/gond-ke-laddu-1-280x280.jpg

1. Soak the lobia overnight or for a few hours. 
2. Drain and rinse the lobia with water. Again drain and keep aside.
3. In a pressure cooker or pressure pan, heat oil.
4. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
5. Then add the chopped onions.
6. Stir and saute till the onions become translucent.
7. Add the chopped ginger, garlic and green chilies. Saute till the raw aroma of the ginger and garlic goes away.
8. Then add the chopped tomatoes and stir.
9. Next add the all the dry spices - turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder and garam masala.
10. Stir and saute the masala on a low flame, till the tomatoes become soft and the entire tomato-onion mixture starts to leave the sides of the pan or cooker and you see the oil leaving from the sides. This cooking method is called as bhunao in punjabi and takes some time.
11. Now add the lobia or black eyed beans. Stir well.
12. Then add 3 cups water. Add salt and stir.
13. Pressure cook till the lobia is cooked completely. I cooked it for 8 to 9 whistles as I had soaked it for only half an hour. If you have soaked it overnight or for 2 to 3 hours, it will take less time to cook. The lobia should be soft enough and when pressed with your fingers, it should get mashed easily. Check the lobia once its done.
14. Once the lobia beans are cooked, simmer the gravy without the lid so that it gets thickened.
15. You can also mash a few cooked beans to thicken the  lobia masala gravy.
16. The consistency of the lobia masala gravy is neither thin nor thick.
17. Lastly add 2 tbsp chopped coriander leaves and give a final stir. You could also garnish lobia masala with chopped coriander leaves.

instructions:
1. Rinse, peel and then grate lauki in a tray or bowl.
2. Add 1 tsp finely chopped green chilies, 1/2 tsp garam masala powder and 1/2 tsp carom seeds/ajwain and salt as required. Substitute 1/2 tsp red chili powder if you do not have green chilies.
3. Mix everything very well.
4. Then add 2 cups whole wheat flour and 1 tbsp oil.
5. First mix the the flour with the rest of the mixture. Start gathering the mixture and kneading to a smooth dough. 
6. Don't add any water while kneading. The juices from the lauki is enough to knead. In case the dough becomes sticky, then add some more flour and knead again.
7. Take a small to mediums sized ball from the dough.
8. Place it in a tray or box containing whole wheat flour.
9. Take the dough ball on the rolling board and begin to roll it with a rolling pin.
10. While rolling, dust some more flour if required.
11. Roll to a small or medium sized paratha with a rolling pin.
12. Place the rolled lauki paratha on a hot tava or griddle.
13. When one side is partly cooked (about 1/4th) then flip it.
14. Spread some oil or ghee on the partly cooked side.
15. Flip again and spread some oil or ghee on the second side.
16. Flip again a couple of times. Also while roasting press the sides of the paratha so that the edges are cooked well.
17. Roast till the paratha is cooked well and you see some golden or brown spots on the paratha. 
18. You can serve these lauki parathas hot or stack them up in a roti basket or casserole and later serve warm. Make all doodhi  parathas this way.
19. Serve lauki paratha with plain curd/yogurt (plain or sweetened with some sugar) or some raita like carrot raita, beetroot raita or makhana raita. 2 cups grated lauki 
1 or 2  green chilies 
1 pinch asafoetida 
½ teaspoon Garam Masala Powder 
½ teaspoon ajwain 
2 cups whole wheat flour 
1 tablespoon oil 
  salt as required 
  ghee

1. In a large mixing bowl or plate/tray take 1 cup whole wheat flour, ¼ tsp salt, 1 tsp oil or ghee. Add some water.
2. Mix everything and begin to knead into a smooth and soft dough. Add more water if required while kneading. 
3. Cover and keep the dough aside for 20 to 30 minutes.
4. In a bowl or plate, take all the stuffing ingredients.
5. Mix everything very well. 
6. No need to add salt as cheese already has a lot of salt. Keep aside.
7. Pinch two small balls from the dough. Roll them between your palms.
8. Flatten them and dust with whole wheat flour.
9. With a rolling pin, roll them into about 4 to 5 inches diameter rounds. Try making both the rounds of the same size.
10. On one of the rolled dough circle, place the cheese stuffing in the center and keep about 1 inch empty space from the sides.
11. Gently place the second circle on top and press and seal the edges with your fingertips.
12. Dust some flour on the stuffed paratha.
13. Begin to roll the paratha. Dust some more flour if required.
14. Roll the paratha into a round of about 7 to 8 inches in diameter or about the size of a normal roti or chapati.
15. On a hot tava (skillet or griddle) place the rolled paratha. 
16. The tava should be hot and not at a low temperature. Cooking parathas at a low flame will harden them. Parathas ideally are crisp as well as soft.
17. When the base is partly cooked, flip the paratha. Spread some ghee on the partly cooked part.
18. Flip again and this time this side has to be cooked more than the previous side. You will see brown spots on the paratha.
19. Spread some ghee on this side too.
20. Flip again once or twice till both the sides are cooked properly. You should see crisp brown spots on the paratha. 
21. Press the paratha edges with a spatula or spoon, so that they are fried well.
22. Once the paratha has cooked well. Remove them from the tava and serve them hot. Make all parathas this way.
23. Serve these cheese paratha hot with yogurt or mango pickle or tomato ketchup. 1 cup whole wheat flour 
¼ teaspoon salt 
1 teaspoon oil 
  water 
½ cup tightly packed grated cheese, 
¼ cup finely chopped onions 
1 or 2  green chilies 
¼ to ½ teaspoon crushed black pepper 
  ghee 
  some whole wheat flour

1. Rinse the baby corn first. Slice the base thinly.
2. Then chop the baby corn either diagonally, vertically or into 1 inch slices.
3. Take all the ingredients mentioned under the list "grind to paste" in a blender or grinder.
4. Add little water and make a smooth paste. Don't add too much water as then the masala splutters while frying.
5. Heat oil in a pan or kadai.
6. Add bay leaf and fry till fragrant for 7-8 seconds.
7. Add the masala paste. Saute and keep on stirring the masala paste.
8. After 10-12 minutes add all the spice powders - turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala powder and coriander powder.
9. Stir well. Continue to saute, stirring quite often till the oil separates from the masala.
10. The masala has to really sauted very well.
11. This takes approx 20-25 minutes on a low to medium flame.
12. Next add water and baby corns.
13. Bring to a boil and then simmer the gravy for 12-15 mins on a low to medium flame till you get a medium consistency gravy and the baby corn have cooked.
14. Lastly add crushed kasuri methi and salt as required.
15. Stir and check the taste of curry. add more salt, red chilli powder or garam masala powder if required.
16. Serve the baby corn masala curry hot with some naan, rotis or jeera rice. 200 to 250 grams baby corn 
1  medium sized tej patta

½ teaspoon red chili powder 
¼ teaspoon turmeric powder 
¼ teaspoon Garam Masala Powder 
½ to ¾ teaspoon kasuri methi, 
1.5 to 2 cups water 
3 tablespoon oil 
  salt as required 
  few chopped coriander leaves for garnishing 
1  medium sized onion 
3  medium sized tomatoes 
3 to 4  garlic 
¾ inch ginger 
1  green chili 
1  black cardamom 
1 inch cinnamon 
2  green cardamoms 
2  cloves

1. Heat 1.5 to 2 tbsp oil in a shallow frying pan or kadai. Add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and saute till they splutter and change color.
2. Add 1/2 cup finely chopped onions.
3. Saute till the onions turn translucent or a light brown.
4. Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste. Stir and saute till the raw aroma of ginger-garlic goes away.
5. Then add 1/3 cup tightly packed chopped tomatoes and 1 green chili, chopped.
6. Saute for 2 minutes.
7. Then add 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/4 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp coriander powder and 1/2 tsp garam masala powder or pav bhaji masala.
8. Stir and saute for two minutes more or till the tomatoes have softened.
9. Add the chopped potatoes and shredded cabbage. Stir and mix.
10. Season with salt. Stir again.
11. Add 1/2 cup water. Stir very well.
12. Cover the pan tightly with its lid and simmer the veggies on a low flame.
13. Do check at intervals if the water has dried or not. If all the water has evaporated, then add some water. I used 2/3 cup water. Depending on the quality of veggies, the pan size etc, you can add from 1/2 to 2/3 cup water. Do add more water if required.
14. Once the potatoes are cooked well, switch off the flame. 
15. There should be no water in the dish. If there is any water left, then cook the cabbage sabzi without the lid, till all the water evaporates. But there will be moisture in the dish as there will be some moisture and juice in the cabbage and potatoes. So a kind of semi-dry dish.
16. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve patta gobhi sabji with chapatis or as a side dish. 150 grams cabbage

instructions:
1. Rinse the potatoes very well. Brush or scrub the mud etc from them.
2. First parboil or half cook 250 grams baby potatoes. If pressure cooking, then just pressure cook for 1 whistle. Drain the potatoes very well.
3. Let them become warm and peel them. Halve them if they are larger in size. Keep aside.
4. Take 1/2 cup thick curd or hung curd in a mixing bowl.
5. Add the following spices - 2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp ajwain/carom seeds, 1.5 to 2 tsp kashmiri red chili powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala powder, 1 tsp chaat masala powder, 1 tsp coriander powder/dhania powder, 1/2 tsp kasuri methi, crushed (optional), 1/8 tsp or 2 to 3 pinches turmeric powder (optional) and black salt as required.
6. Mix very well.
7. Now add 3 tbsp low fat cream and 1 tbsp besan or gram flour. Again mix very well.
8. You can also add 1 to 2 drops of natural color orange extract. This is optional.
9. Mix again very well.
10. Check the taste of the marination and add more black salt if required.
11. Now add the potatoes in the curd marination.
12. Mix very well. Cover and allow to marinate for 30 minutes or for a couple of hours.
13. Thread the potatoes on a skewer and place them on a tray which has been lined with a foil or butter paper.
14. Place the tray in the oven which has been preheated at 250 degrees celsius for 10 to 15 minutes. Grill the aloo tikka at the same temperature of 250 degrees celsius till the potatoes become golden with a few charred spots.
15. Whilst baking, remove the potatoes once or twice. Turn over the skewers and brush with some oil.
16. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a shallow frying pan.
17. Coat each tikka with the marination and place them in the hot oil. You can fry in batches too.
18. On a low to medium flame fry them.
19. When one side becomes slightly crisp and cooked, turn each potato piece and fry their other sides.
20. Fry till the potatoes become crisp and the marination masala coating the potatoes, has also become crisp and golden.
21. Place aloo tikka on a kitchen paper towel.
22. Serve the tandoori aloo with mint chutney accompanied with onion and lemon slices. You can also sprinkle some chaat masala on top of the aloo tikka while serving. 250 grams baby potatoes 
½ cup Hung Curd 
3 tablespoon low fat cream 
1 tablespoon besan 
2 teaspoon Ginger-Garlic Paste 
½ teaspoon ajwain 
1.5 to 2 teaspoon kashmiri red chili powder

1. In a bowl or vessel take 2 cups whole wheat flour along with salt as per taste.
2. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons of ghee or oil. next add water as required in parts.
3. Knead the whole wheat flour with water to a smooth dough. Cover and keep aside for 20 to 30 minutes.
4. Later make medium sized balls from the dough. Cover the bowl or the pan with a napkin or lid.
5. Take a dough ball. Roll it into 6 to 7 inches diameter disc on a dusted rolling board.
6. Apply ghee or oil liberally on the paratha disc. Sprinkle some flour on the top.
7. From the edges start to fold & pleat the paratha till the end.
8. Roll the pleated edges tightly. Join the edges.
9. Lightly dust with flour and now roll into round parathas of about 4 to 5 inches in diameter.
10. Heat the tava or griddle. The tava should be hot. Place the paratha on the tava.
11. Turn the paratha when one side is partly cooked. Apply ghee on this side. Cook for a minute.
12. Now turn again and apply ghee on the other side.
13. Flip again for a couple of times, till the parathas are browned evenly and well cooked. Press the sides with the spatula while frying the parathas.
14. Alternatively, you could also add some ghee on the tava and then fry the paratha.
15. Serve the lachha paratha hot with any indian dal or a vegetable curry of your choice. 2 cups wheat flour 
1 to 2 teaspoon ghee 
  salt as required 
  water as required for kneading 
  ghee or oil as required for applying on the dough as well as roasting

1. Firstly heat 1.5 cups of milk in a thick bottomed pan till it comes to a boil.
2. At the same time, when you keep the milk for boiling, on another stove top keep a thick bottomed pan. Add ¼ cup of ghee in it.
3. Once the ghee melts, then lower the flame.
4. Add 1 cup of gram flour (besan) and mix very well with the ghee.
5. Keep on stirring continuously so that the besan is evenly roasted.
6. Mix and stir well for 14 to 15 mins on low heat, till the besan leaves a nutty aroma.
7. Soon the gram four will start releasing ghee.
8. By now the milk must have also got boiled. In case the milk gets boiled earlier, before the besan gets roasted, then switch off the flame and cover the milk pan. The milk has to be poured in batches. Keep the flame to a low and first pour 1 cup of hot milk gradually into the roasted gram flour. While you are pouring the milk, simultaneously keep on stirring also. Mix the milk very well with the roasted gram flour.
9. Then pour the remaining 1/2 cup milk.
10. Continue to mix and stir the mixture for 1 to 2 mins.
11. Add 1/3 cup of sugar.
12. Stir well so that no lumps are formed. Keep continuously stirring for 5 to 6 mins on a low flame.
13. Soon the mixture will start thickening. You have to continuously keep stirring the mixture, then only halwa will be smooth and without lumps.
14. Add cardamom powder, chopped pistachios and almonds.
15. Continue to stir and mix well.
16. You will see the halwa leaving ghee at the sides. The besan halwa will also start leaving the edges of the pan.
17. Switch off the flame. The besan halwa will become thick as it cools down.
18. Serve besan halwa hot or warm or chilled. If you want you can garnish halwa with chopped nuts and saffron strands.

1. Soak the chickpeas overnight in water.

3. Make the onion paste with garlic and ginger.

1. Wash and peel onions. Wash and slice them thinly. Chop chllies, mint, coriander and curry leaves.

3. Add all the flours, chili powder, turmeric and ajwain. Mix together.

1. First, take the jaggery and soak it in 3/4 cup water for 30 to 45 minutes.
2. Pick, clean and wash the rice. Soak the rice for 15 to 20 minutes.
3. In a pressure cooker add the rice and 3/4 cup water.
4. Pressure cook for 2 to 3 minutes. The rice should be half cooked. Once the pressure settles down, open the cooker lid.
5. Fluff the rice in the cooker itself.
6. Add the jaggery dissolved in water plus the oil. Stir it gently with the half cooked rice.
7. Now add the cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, raisins and peanuts.
8. Stir this too gently with the rice mixture.
9. Now close the cooker with the lid and pressure cook again for 2 to 3 minutes.
10. Garnish the cooked jaggery rice with dry fruits of your choice.
11. Serve hot or warm, plain or with some milk. ¾ cup rice,
