1. Rinse the rice a couple of times in water. Drain and let them dry on their own or wipe the grains dry with a kitchen towel.
2. Take the rice grains in a dry grinder or coffee grinder. Grind the rice till the consistency resembles sooji (rava or fine semolina) or corn meal or couscous .
3. You can also soak the rice in water for 30 mins and then drain and grind to a semi fine powder.
4. Reserve a few almond slices for garnish.
5. Set the ground rice aside.
6. Take hot boiling water in a small bowl. Add almonds and cover the bowl.
7. Blanch almonds for 30 minutes.
8. When the almonds become warm, then peel them and slice the almonds.
9. Heat milk in a thick bottomed broad pan or sauce pan or kadai.
10. When the milk becomes warm, take 1 tbsp from it in a bowl.
11. Stir the saffron strands in this warm milk and keep aside.
12. Let the milk reach to a boil. Then lower the flame and add the ground rice. Stir and add sugar also.
13. On a low to medium flame cook the ground rice in the milk. Do not cover the pan.
14. Keep on stirring at intervals so that the lumps are not formed.
15. Also powder the cardamoms in a mortar-pestle. Discard the almond peels.
16. When the rice is almost cooked, add the almonds, cardamom powder and saffron dissolved milk.
17. Stir and cook firni for a further 5 to 6 mins or more or till the firni thickens.
18. If adding rose water, add once the firni is done.
19. Pour the phirni in serving bowls. Garnish phirni with the remaining chopped almond slices.
20. Cover the bowls and once cooled at room temperature, refrigerate phirni.
21. Serve phirni once cooled.
22. Store firni in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days and in the freezer, for a couple of weeks.

1. Firstly keep all the ingredients ready for making meethi seviyan. Break the seviyan and keep aside.
2. Chop the dry fruits and place aside.
3. Heat a pan and then add 1 tbsp ghee.
4. Let the ghee melt and then add 1 cup of the broken seviyan.
5. On a low to medium flame, with frequent stirring roast the seviyan till they become golden. Since I used pre roasted seviyan, I didn't have to roast the seviyan much. However, if you use seviyan which is not roasted, then you will need to roast for some more time.
6. Add all the chopped dry fruits and raisins. Stir them nicely.
7. Lower the flame and pour 2 cups of milk. Instead of milk you can also add water.
8. Stir and mix very well. Then continue to stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
9. Now add ¼ cup of sugar. Keep stirring the mixture.
10. Add ¼ cup of milk powder. If you do not have milk powder, then just skip it. Mix again
11. Sprinkle ½ tsp cardamom powder and stir well.
12. The mixture will start thickening and the seviyan will also begin to absorb milk. When all the milk has been absorbed, switch off the gas.
13. Serve meethi seviyan hot or warm or chilled. You can even garnish with some sliced dry fruits while serving 1 tablespoon ghee 
1 cup of broken vermicelli

1. Take all the ingredients in a mixing bowl, except oil.
2. Mix very well. Check the taste and add more spice powders or salt if required.
3. Mix everything very well. When you are mixing, the rice will also get mashed.
4. Shape the mixture into small to medium sized patties or tikkis.
5. Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a frying pan or tawa (skillet). 
6. When the oil becomes medium hot, place the rice cutlets on the tawa.
7. When the base is lightly browned, flip them and fry the other side.
8. Flip again and fry till they are crisp and golden.
9. When nicely crisp and golden, remove them and place them on kitchen paper towel.
10. Serve rice cutlets hot with coriander chutney or mint chutney or tomato ketchup. 1 cup tightly packed cooked rice 
½ cup tightly packed mashed potatoes

1. In a mixing bowl take 2 cups maize flour or cornmeal, 1 teaspoon carom seeds and salt as required. Mix them together with a spoon.
2. Heat 1 cup water separately in a pan till it comes to a boil. Add this hot water to the flour.
3. Mix with a spoon. Cover and keep aside till the dough mixture becomes warm.
4. When the mixture becomes warm and the heat is fine to handle, begin to knead to a smooth yet firm dough. If the dough looks dry, then add some warm water. If the dough looks sticky, then add a few tablespoons of maize flour.
5. Knead into a smooth yet firm dough. fine cracks will be there. So not to worry. make medium sized balls of the dough. Shape them into a neat ball and flatten them.
6. Sprinkle some maize flour on the rolling board. Place the dough ball on the rolling board. Then sprinkle some maize flour on the dough ball also.
7. Begin to gently roll with a rolling pin (belan). Add more flour if required. 
8. Roll to small to medium-sized round circle. Make into the size of a phulka or chapati but not very thin, but a little thick. 
9. You can even use a ziplock bag. If using a zip lock bag, then keep the bag on the rolling board or on a plate or on a surface which you can move. Place the dough ball in the bag. Press it slightly with your hands. Now with the rolling pin (belan), slowly roll. Sprinkle some flour. Move the rolling board and roll again. This is to ensure that all the sides of the roti are evenly rolled.
10. Makki roti can also be made by patting the dough. Sprinkle some maize flour on the dough ball all over and also on the rolling board. 
11. Now with your fingers gently press and pat the dough. As you press the dough, also move it clockwise. add flour as required when patting the dough. 
12. Continue to press and pat the dough till you get a neat makki roti. Do not make thin but slightly thick roti. When the dough is patted, the edges won’t be even. 
13. Now spread some ghee or oil on a hot tawa.
14. Gently place the roti on the tava or griddle. If there is a crack on the roti, then gently pat that portion with a few drops of water.
15. When one side is a little browned, flip the roti with the help of a spatula.
16. When the other side gets browned, flip again. Flip a couple of times and cook till the roti is well browned and cooked from all sides. Press the edges with a spatula so that they get cooked well. 
17. Pour some ghee on the sides whilst cooking the roti. If the dough is kneaded very well, the makki di roti will start puffing up also or you can see puff coming up at some spots.
18. Serve the makki ki roti hot with sarson ka saag and jaggery cubes. If you don’t mind then you can add some white butter (makhan) on top of the makki di roti while serving them hot and that’s how they are relished and served in punjabi families.

1. Boil or steam potatoes till they are cooked very well and can be easily mashed.
2. Drain and peel them. Mash them when they are still hot or warm.
3. Add all the herbs and spices powders - chopped green chilies, coriander leaves, red chili powder, garam masala powder, dry mango powder, cumin powder and salt. Mix very well.
4. Check the seasoning and add more of salt, red chili powder, dry mango powder if required.
5. Spread butter on half of the bread slices.
6. Take some portion of the potato stuffing and spread it on the buttered bread slices.
7. Optional step - sprinkle some grated cheese.
8. Cover the bread slices with the remaining buttered slices.
9. Spread some butter on the top of the bread sandwiches.
10. Place the sandwiches buttered side down in a preheated grill carefully.
11. Now spread butter on the top of the bread slices facing you.
12. Cover the grill and grill for 2-3 minutes or till the sandwiches are golden and crisp.
13. Serve potato sandwich hot with tomato sauce or cilantro chutney or both. 8 to 10  bread slices 
2 to 3  medium potatoes 
1 or 2  green chilies, 
¼ teaspoon kashmiri chilli powder or deghi mirch 
¼ teaspoon Garam Masala Powder 
1 teaspoon dry mango powder

½ to 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves 
  salted butter at room temperature

1. Steam or pressure cook the potatoes with rock salt.
2. When warm, peel and mash the potatoes.
3. Add all the other ingredients including oil.
4. Mix well first.
5. Add very little water and knead the dough.
6. Don't add water unless required.
7. Knead the dough and if it looks dry or lumpy in some parts, then add little water and knead again.
8. The dough should be smooth and pliable.
9. The dough should not be sticky.
10. Otherwise you won't be able to roll the pooris.
11. Take small or medium sized balls from the dough.
12. Sprinkle some water chestnut flour on the rolling board.
13. Roll the balls in to small or medium sized pooris.
14. Don't make thin or thick pooris.
15. The thin ones will break when frying and the thick ones will get browned quickly from out leaving the insides uncooked.
16. Heat oil in a kadai for deep frying the pooris.
17. When the oil is hot, place the poori gently in the oil.
18. When one sides puffs up... (you can aid the poori to puff up by gently nudging it with the slotted spoon) gently turn over and fry the other side.
19. When singhare ki pooris are golden, remove from the slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
20. Serve the singhare ki poori hot with vrat ke aloo.

1. Rinse the moong dal 3 to 4 times in water.
2. Soak moong dal with 2 to 3 cups of water for 3 to 4 hours or over night.
3. The moong dal will swell or double up in size. Discard the water.
4. In a grinder, grind soaked moong dal with ¼ cup of water. 
5. Don't add too much water else they might not grind evenly. We need a smooth and lump free batter for moong dal chillas.
6. Take the batter in a bowl. Add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder, ¼ teaspoon red chili powder, ½ teaspoon roasted cumin powder and 1 teaspoon salt or as required.
7. Mix very well. 
8. Then add add ¼ cup coriander leaves, ¼ cup finely chopped onion, 1 teaspoon grated ginger, finely chopped green chilies and a pinch of hing. 
9. Again mix very well. 
10. Allow the batter to rest for 15 -20 mins.
11. The onions will leave some moisture. check the consistency of the batter. If its too thick, then add 1 to 2 tablespoons more water. Adding too much water will not be good as it will not spread evenly on the tawa.
12. The consistency of the batter has to be of pouring consistency, neither too thick nor too thin.
13. Heat the pan. This is important as the pan has to be hot before you make the cheelas.
14. Add a scoopful of batter towards the center of the pan.
15. The batter will spread a little on its own.
16. Just rotate the batter with the back of spatula giving a round and even shape.
17. Drizzle few drops of oil around the edges of the chilla.
18. Cook the chilla on medium heat. After a minute they will look crisp and brown.
19. Flip the chillas and cook the other side for a minute.
20. Once the moong dal chilla appear crisp and brown, remove and place aside. 
21. Similarly make all other chilla. You can stuff the chilla with some grated paneer if you want. 
22. Serve moong dal chilla with tomato ketchup or green chutney. 1 cup moong dal 
2 to 3 cups water 
¼ cup water,

1 pinch hing

1 to 2  green chilies 
1 teaspoon salt 
1 to 2 tablespoon oil for cooking chillas

1. Take chopped bananas and sugar in a mixing bowl. Mash very well with a fork or vegetable masher. Mix the sugar with the bananas as you go on mashing. 
2. Add the wheat flour, fennel seeds, cardamom powder and salt to the mashed banana and sugar mixture. 
3. Add half a cup of water first. Mix well and add more water as required to make a batter that is neither too thick nor too thin. Check the notes section of this recipe card for tips on batter consistency and adding water. 
4. The batter should be slightly thicker than a pakoda batter
5. In a deep pan or wok or kadai heat ghee or oil. Let the oil become hot. 
6. Drop spoonfuls of the batter in the hot oil. Fry the gulgule on a medium flame. 
7. Note that the oil should not be less hot, otherwise the batter may stick. The oil or ghee should not be very hot, otherwise the gulgule may get burnt.
8. Do not overcrowd the pan. You can easily fry 8 to 12 gulgule at a time depending on the size of the pan or kadai. While frying if the oil becomes too hot, then reduce the flame. 
9. The gulgule will puff while frying. When one side is light golden, gently turn over and fry the other side. Keep on turning and frying them till they are golden brown. Remove them and place on kitchen paper towels for the extra oil or ghee to be absorbed.
10. When frying, they may stick, but get separated once browned.
11.  Serve the gulgule or meetha pua hot with Indian tea. ½ cup  chopped bananas 
6 tablespoons raw sugar

8 to 11 tablespoons water 
  oil as required

1. Peel and then rinse 2 large onions (200 grams). Chop one onion and if required some portion of the second onion, in one inch squares. You will need ¾ cup onion squares.
2. Finely chop the remaining onion. You will need ½ cup finely chopped onions. 
3. Also finely chop 2 medium to large tomatoes (150 grams) and 200 grams button mushrooms (about 2 to 2.5 cups chopped mushrooms).
4. Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a kadai or pan.
5. Add the onions which have been cut into squares. On a medium-low or medium flame, begin to saute the onions.
6. Stir at intervals while sautéing the onions. Saute the onions till the edges turn golden.
7. Remove the onions with a slotted spoon and keep aside.
8. Lower the flame and in the same pan, add 1 small to medium tej patta.
9. Add ½ cup finely chopped onions and saute till translucent or till light golden. 
10. Then add ½ teaspoon ginger-garlic paste.
11. Mix well and saute till the raw aroma of ginger-garlic goes away.
12. Then add the finely chopped tomatoes. Mix very well and sauté for a minute.
13. Add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon red chilli powder, ½ teaspoon coriander powder and ½ teaspoon cumin powder. Mix very well.
14. Saute the masala till the tomatoes soften and become mushy.
15. Add the chopped mushrooms. Also add salt as per taste. 
16. Mix very well. Begin to saute the mushrooms on a low to medium flame.
17. First the mushrooms would release water.
18. Continue to saute till the water dries up and the mushrooms are cooked. Then add the sautéed onion squares. Mix very well.
19. Next add ½ teaspoon garam masala powder, 3 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves and 1 to 2 green chilies (slit or sliced).
20. Mix very well and then switch off the flame.
21. Serve mushroom do pyaza hot or warm with chapatis or parathas. You can also serve it with bread or pav. While serving garnish with some chopped coriander leaves. 200 grams mushrooms

1. First boil 2 small to medium potatoes in a steamer or pressure cooker till they are thoroughly cooked and of a mashable consistency.
2. In a pan or bowl take the amaranth flour. I ground the flour at home using raw amaranth grains. 1/2 cup of amaranth grains yielded about 3/4 cup flour.
3. When the potatoes are slightly hot, peel them. Then mash them lightly and add to the amaranth flour.
4. Then add the crushed green chili paste, cumin powder and rock salt (sendha namak). You can also add some chopped coriander and ginger paste. Mix everything well.
5. Add 1 or 2 tbsp water in parts and knead to a smooth dough. The addition of water depends on the quality of flour. Hence add as accordingly. Make sure you don't add too much of water. Allow the dough to come at room temperature as it will be slightly warm due to the addition of the hot mashed potatoes.
6. Make a small or medium sized balls from the dough. Dust with amaranth flour.
7. Roll to a small or medium sized paratha. While rolling add some more flour if required.
8. Then gently lift up with a spatula and fry the paratha on a hot tava.
9. Keep a moist kitchen cotton napkin or towel on your workplace. Take a small or medium sized ball from the dough and place it on the moist kitchen cloth.
10. With your palms or with your fingers, gently press the dough ball and flatten it till till it increases in size. The edges come out neat this way and are not uneven.
11. Now gently remove the paratha from the cloth or place the cloth upside down on a hot tava and peel of cotton cloth. I do the first method of removing the rajgira paratha from the cloth and then placing it on the hot tava.
12. One side is partly cooked, flip with the help of spatula. Use a non-stick pan or well seasoned pan as the paratha might stick.
13. Apply ghee or oil on this side. Flip again. Apply ghee or oil on this side.
14. Flip a couple of times till the roti has become evenly golden and roasted evenly.
15. Serve these rajgira roti hot or warm with curd or any curry meant for fasting.

1. Take the whole wheat flour, besan (gram flour) and ajwain (carom seeds) in a mixing bowl or a pan.
2. Add finely chopped onion, chopped green chilies, a pinch of asafoetida (hing) and oil. Mix very well.
3. Then add ½ cup water. Begin to mix and knead the dough.
4. Add more water as required and knead to a smooth soft dough. 
5. I overall added ¾ cup water. The amount of water required depends on the quality of flour. So you can add 2/3 to ¾ cup water or more if required.
6. Allow the dough to rest for 10 minutes and then make medium sized balls from the dough.
7. Take the dough ball on the rolling board. 
8. Dust some dry wheat flour on both sides of the ball.
9. Roll to a circle of about 5 to 6 inches. 
10. Sprinkle some more flour if required while rolling. Roll to medium thick rotis.
11. Place the roti on a hot tawa. The tava should be hot and not at a low temperature.
12. When the base is partially cooked, flip the roti.
13. Spread some ghee or oil on the partly cooked part.
14. When the second side is cooked and brown spots can be seen, then flip again. Spread some ghee or oil on this side too. Flip again.
15. Press the edges with a spatula so that the sides are also cooked well.
16. Flip once or twice more, so that the roti is evenly cooked. Also, do not cook too much as then the rotis will become dense.
17. Serve the missi roti immediately or place them in a roti basket or a casserole and serve warm. Make rotis this way and stack them up in a roti basket or casserole.
18. Serve them hot or warm with a sabzi, dal or with a pickle or yogurt or butter. 2 cups whole wheat flour 
1 cup besan 
1 teaspoon ajwain 
1 to 2  green chilies, 
50 grams onion, 
1 pinch asafoetida 
1 teaspoon salt 
3 teaspoon oil 
⅔ to ¾ cup water 
  oil

1. Pick and then rinse the dal for a couple of times in water.
2. Soak the chana dal in enough water for 3 to 4 hours or overnight.
3. Drain the soaked dal and add them to the grinder.
4. Add 1.5 to 2 tbsp chopped onion along with the chopped green chilies, ginger and garlic, asafoetida, fennel seeds, cumin seeds in the grinder.
5. Add 1.5 to 2 tbsp water and grind to a smooth batter.
6. Take the ground batter in a bowl. Add 2 tbsp chopped onion and salt.
7. Also add a pinch of baking soda if using. Mix the batter very well.
8. Heat oil for deep frying in a pan or kadai. 
9. Drop spoonfuls of the batter in medium hot oil.
10. Fry the pakoras till crisp and golden. 
11. Drain the pakoras on paper towels to remove excess oil.
12. Serve chana dal pakoras hot or warm with green chutney or coconut chutney or tomato ketchup. ½ cup chana dal 
1 teaspoon fennel seeds

1. First take  1 cup corn flour (100 grams) in a mixing bowl. add 1 cup water.
2. Mix very well with a wired whisk. There should be no lumps. Keep aside.
3. Line a tray or pan with butter paper or parchment paper. Alternatively you can grease the pan on the bottom and sides with some ghee. Keep aside.
4. In a heavy kadai take 1 cup sugar (200 grams). add ½ cup water.
5. Add 5 to 6 drops of natural orange color extract. You can use any natural color extract like yellow, red, pink, green. You can also use about 1 pinch of saffron strands for a faint yellow color.
6. Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice. mix well and keep the pan on a stove top.
7. Keep the flame to medium-low and begin stirring the solution, so that the sugar solution dissolves. Then reduce the flame to a low or sim. Keep the flame to its lowest.
8. Let the sugar solution come to a boil.
9. Now take the corn starch solution and stir it again as the corn starch settles down at the bottom, so you have to mix everything again before you add in the sugar syrup.
10. Add a part of the corn flour solution. Add corn flour solution in two to three parts.
11. As soon as you add mix very well with a wired whisk.
12. Then add the second part of the corn flour solution. mix and stir very well.
13. Continue to mix and stir at non stop on a low flame. Now use a spatula or a spoon for stirring instead of wired whisk.
14. The corn flour will begin to become sticky and thicken. Keep on stirring.
15. Stir and mix till the entire mixture thickens.
16. Once the entire mixture thickens, add ¼ cup ghee in two to three parts.
17. As soon as you add ghee, mix well so that all of the ghee is incorporated in the corn flour mixture.
18. All of the ghee should be mixed well. 
19. Then add the second portion of ghee. mix again.
20. Continue to stir and mix when adding ghee in parts.
21. Add the last portion of ghee.
22.  stir and mix again and cook for 1 to 2 minutes stirring often, till the mixture gathers in one mass. By this time the mixture must have already left the sides of the kadai or pan. You will also see ghee releasing from the sides.
23. Take a small portion of halwa in a plate
24. Then check if you can form into a ball. If yes then the karachi halwa is ready. While checking you have to be quick and not keep the halwa cooking in the kadai. So either cool the halwa portion by placing it in water or use a napkin and with the help of the cotton napkin shape the halwa.
25. Once the mixture gather in one mass and has a translucent appearance, switch off the flame and quickly add 1 tablespoon sliced almonds, 1 tablespoon chopped cashews and ½ teaspoon cardamom powder.
26. Then quickly add 1 teaspoon rose water. Rose water can be skipped. mix immediately.
27. Quickly add the halwa mixture in the lined or greased tray.
28. Begin to spread the halwa mixture in the tray.  then level with a spatula. level neatly.
29. Then add 2 teaspoons sliced almonds and 2 teaspoons sliced cashews all over the halwa.
30. Press the nuts with spatula so that they stick to it.
31. Allow to cool at room temperature.
32. Once cooled, remove the karachi halwa. then slice it in squares.
33. Serve karachi halwa as a festive sweet or an after meal sweet. Leftover can be stored in an air tight box and then refrigerated. 1  cup  corn flour  
1  cup  water  
1  cup  sugar 
½  cup water 
1  teaspoon  lemon juice 
5 to 6   drops of natural orange color extract 
¼  cup  ghee  
½  teaspoon  cardamom powder 
1  teaspoon  rose water 
1  tablespoon  sliced almonds 
1  tablespoon  chopped cashews 
2  teaspoons  sliced almonds 
2  teaspoons  sliced cashews

1. Boil potato (aloo) till its completely cooked.
2. Peel and mash the potatoes when still warm.
3. In a bowl, mix the mashed potatoes, coriander leaves, green chilies and rock salt with the kuttu ka atta.
4. Add very little warm water like 1 to 2 tablespoons and begin to knead.
5. Keep on adding little warm water in parts and knead till a dough forms and it stays together. Overall you can use 3 to 4 tablespoons of warm water. 
6. Don't make too smooth or too moist as you won't be able to roll the parathas.
7. On a moist cloth, sprinkle some flour lightly.
8. Take a medium sized ball and place on the cloth.
9. Fold the cloth and roll the ball with a rolling pin.
10. Pick up the folded napkin and rotate so you get a round shaped paratha.
11. While making rotis, you roll it slightly thin and for making parathas you can roll slightly thick. You can use a zip lock bag or a banana leaf also to roll these parathas. 
12. Heat griddle or tava.
13. Place the roti or paratha side on your right palm and gently remove the cloth/napkin from the other side.
14. Then place the roti or paratha on the tava.
15. When one side is partly cooked, flip and let the other side cook.
16. Spread ½  teaspoon ghee or oil on top and then flip again.
17. Cook for a few minutes and meanwhile spread again ½ teaspoon ghee or oil on the top.
18. Flip once or twice till the kuttu ki rotis have golden brown patches.
19. Prepare all kuttu ka atta ki rotis or parathas this way and stack them in a roti basket. 
20. Serve kuttu ki rotis or parathas hot or warm with a side vegetable dish or curry. 2 cups kuttu ka atta 
1 tablespoon finely chopped coriander leaves 
1  medium to large potato 
1  green chili or hari mirch 
3 to 4 tablespoon warm water  
1 teaspoon rock salt  
  oil for ghee as required,

1. First take 2 cups whole wheat flour, ½ teaspoon salt and 2 teaspoon oil in a mixing bowl or pan. Mix very well.
2. Then add ½ cup water.
3. Begin to knead. Add more water if required while kneading.
4. I added overall 2/3 cup water. Depending on the quality of flour, you can add less or more water.
5. Knead to a soft and smooth dough. Cover and keep aside the paratha dough for 30 minutes.
6. Rinse, peel and grate 350 grams beetroot or 4 medium sized beetroots. You should be able to get 2 cups tightly packed beetroots.
7. Heat a pan and add 1 teaspoon oil. Then add the grated beetroot.
8. Saute the beetroot on a low flame for 5 to 6 minutes, till there is no moisture in them. They will be partly cooked and also appear dry.
9. Now add the following seasonings - 1 to 2 green chilies (finely chopped), 1 teaspoon amchur powder or dry pomegranate powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala powder and salt as required.
10. Mix very well. Switch off the flame. Keep the beetroot mixture aside.
11. Pinch medium sized balls from the dough. Roll them and keep covered.
12. Take a dough ball. Flatten it a bit. Sprinkle with some whole wheat flour.
13. Roll to a round of 5 to 6 inches in diameter.
14. Place 2 to 3 tablespoons of the beetroot stuffing on the rolled dough.
15. Begin to pleat the edges.
16. Then bring them together at the center and press them at the center.
17. Flatten the pressed edges with your fingers and dust some flour on the stuffed dough. You can also roll two small rounds and then place the beetroot between the dough circles.
18. Gently roll to a paratha of about 7 to 8 inches. Sprinkle flour as required while rolling.
19. Heat a tawa and let it become hot. Place the paratha on the hot tawa.
20. On a medium to high flame, begin to roast the paratha.
21. When one side is partially cooked (about ¼th) then flip.
22. Spread some oil or ghee on top and flip again.
23. Now spread some oil or ghee on this side too. If the paratha has been stuffed and rolled well, it will start puffing up while cooking. Flip again.
24. Press the paratha edges with a spatula too, so that they are also roasted well.
25. Flip once more and roast till the paratha is evenly cooked and has golden blisters on top.
26. Serve beetroot paratha hot. you can also stack them in roti basket and later serve warm. Serve them for breakfast with a side accompaniment of a sweet mango pickle. You can also serve with some butter or curd. 2 cups whole wheat flour 
2 teaspoon oil 
½ teaspoon salt 
½ to ⅔ cup water 
1 teaspoon oil 
350 grams beetroot 
1 to 2  green chilies, 
1 teaspoon dry mango powder 
½ teaspoon Garam Masala Powder 
  salt as required 
  oil

instructions:
1. Soak the sabudana or tapioca pearls in enough water overnight or for 4-5 hours.
2. Drain and keep aside in a mixing bowl.
3. Boil the potatoes, peel and chop roughly.
4. Roast the peanuts in a pan till browned and crisp.
5. In a mortar-pestle, coarsely crush the roasted peanuts.
6. Add all ingredients to the drained sabudana, including the chopped potatoes and peanuts.
7. Mix well. check the taste and add more salt or sugar if required.
8. Heat oil in a kadai or pan.
9. Make small balls with your hands or using a spoon drop the mixture in to medium hot oil.
10. Let the pakoras become opaque and then turn them with a slotted spoon.
11. Deep fry till the pakodas become light golden and crisp. Then remove them with a slotted spoon draining as much oil as possible.
12. Place them on paper napkins to remove excess oil.
13. Serve sabudana pakodas hot with tomato sauce or green chutney or coconut chutney. If you are making them for fasting then serve them with phalahari chutney.
14. Best to have them hot for best taste.

1. In a mixing bowl or pan, take 2 cups whole wheat flour and 1 cup all-purpose flour.
2. Then add 1.5 teaspoons baking powder, ¼ teaspoon baking soda, 2 teaspoons sugar and 1 teaspoon salt.
3. Mix very well with a spoon or spatula.
4. Add 3 tablespoons buttermilk or 3 tablespoons curd.
5. Then add ⅔ to ¾ cup water in parts.
6. Mix well and then add 3 tablespoons oil or butter.
7. Again mix and begin to knead.
8. Knead very well to a soft, smooth and pliable dough. Add more water if required while kneading dough. 
9. Flatten the dough. Brush some water or oil all over the dough. Cover the bowl and allow to leaven the dough for 2 hours.
10. After 2 hours grate cheese and keep aside. You will need 1 cup grated cheese. You can use cheddar cheese, mozzarella cheese or processed cheese.
11. Make medium sized balls from the dough.
12. Dust some flour on the dough ball.
13. Roll in to a 5 to 6 inches diameter circle.
14. Add 2 to 3 tablespoons grated cheese. You can even add less cheese if you want. But it will be like a cheese flavoured naan and not cheese naan.
15. Fold the edges from all around.
16. Bring the edges in the center and then join them. Press the joined edges back on the dough.
17. Dust some more flour and roll the cheese stuffed naan.
18. Roll to 7 to 8 inches circle. brush some water on the side facing you.
19. Sprinkle some nigella seeds or sesame seeds all over and press them with the brush or with your fingers, so that they stick to the naan.
20. Now place the cheese naan with the nigella seeds side down on a hot tawa.
21. Roast naan on a medium to high flame. It will begin to puff up.
22. When you see some blisters and the naan begins to puff up, flip it. Cook the other side.
23. Flip again when this second side is cooked. You can flip a couple of times more for even roasting.
24. Take them in a plate and spread some butter on top.
25. Then cut the cheese naans in two or four pieces if serving immediately. Make all the naans this way. You can serve them hot or stack them in a roti basket or casserole and then serve later.
26. Serve hot or warm with a dal or curry. 2  cups  whole wheat flour 
1  cup  all purpose flour 
1.5 teaspoons baking powder 
¼  teaspoon  baking soda 
2  teaspoons  sugar 
1  teaspoon  salt 
3  tablespoons  buttermilk  
3  tablespoons  oil

1. Take all the ingredients - 2 cups besan, ½ cup desi ghee, 1 cup sugar, 5 almonds+5 cashews (chopped) and 1 tablespoon magaz (melon seeds).
2. Grease a pan or a tray very well with some ghee. You can also line a pan or tray with some butter paper or aluminium foil and then spread some ghee on the butter paper or foil.
3. Take ½ cup desi ghee in a heavy kadai and let it melt. Keep the flame to a low.
4. Once the ghee has melted, then add 2 cups besan in parts. Please use a heavy kadai, so that the besan roasts evenly. Also do not use a non stick pan as there is a lot of stirring involved.
5. When the first portion of besan is added, mix it with the ghee.
6. Then add the second part of besan. mix it again with the ghee.
7. Mix very well and continue to stir the besan non stop on a low flame.
8. Initially the ghee will be absorbed by the besan and you will see the mixture getting thicker.
9. Continue to stir and fry the besan in ghee.
10. The besan mixture will become like one whole lump of mass or you may see it getting thicker and granular. Continue to fry stirring very well. Scrape the mixture from the bottom when you stir.
11. After some minutes of stirring, you will see that the besan mixture starts to become molten and ghee will be released from the sides.
12. Continue to stir and fry besan till it starts having a nice nutty aroma and the color changes to a golden color. Stir non stop even after the ghee has released and till the besan gets roasted well and changes to a slight darker golden colour. The roasted besan aroma will be felt.
13. The mixture will become more molten as you continue to fry. Do not stop while stirring or else the besan will have uneven color.
14. Stirring non-stop, you will come to a stage where the besan will have a nice golden color and will have a good aroma. Its important to fry the besan very well or else you will get the raw taste of besan in the barfi.
15. Once the besan has roasted well keep the pan down.
16. Add 1 teaspoon cardamom powder and mix well.
17. In a sauce pan or in another pan, take 1 cup sugar and ½  cup water. Keep the pan on a stove top on a low-medium flame to medium flame.
18. With a spoon stir well, so that all the sugar dissolves.
19. Continue to cook the sugar syrup on a low-medium flame to medium flame.
20. The sugar syrup will start boiling and reducing. Keep a plate handy and test a few drops of the sugar syrup till you get a two thread consistency. After adding the few drops of sugar syrup on the plate, let it cool for some seconds and then check as the syrup is very hot and can burn your fingers.
21. You need to get a two thread consistency in the syrup. Even a 1 & ½ string consistency is fine.
22. Once the sugar syrup reaches a 2 thread consistency, then quickly pour all the sugar syrup in the besan mixture.
23. Quickly and vigorously mix everything very well. You have to be quick and fast as the mixture begins to harden.
24. Mix fast and you will see the mixture thickening.
25. The mixture will also reduce.
26. The besan barfi mixture will leave the sides of the pan or kadai.
27. When mixed well, quickly pour the besan barfi mixture in the greased pan or tray.
28. Shake the pan and then with a spatula even the layer.
29. Sprinkle chopped almonds, cashews and melon seeds on top.
30. Press the nuts with the spatula so that they stick to the besan burfi.
31. Let it set till it becomes warm.
32. When still warm, slice the besan barfi in cubes or squares.
33. Store besan ki barfi in an air-tight container. No need to refrigerate. Besan barfi stays well at room temperature for about a week. Serve besan ki barfi as a sweet dessert after any indian meal.

instructions:
1. Take 2 cups buckwheat flour (or 250 grams  kuttu ka atta) in a large mixing bowl or a plate (parat).
2. Add ½ teaspoon cumin powder and 1 teaspoon rock salt (sendha namak).
3. With a spoon mix well.
4. Now add 1 cup hot boiling water.
5. With a spoon mix everything. Cover the pan and keep aside till the mixture cools down.
6. Once the mixture has cooled down, begin to knead it. While kneading add warm water if required. 1 to 2 tablespoons of water can be added.
7. Knead to a smooth dough. The dough should not be sticky. Otherwise you won't be able to roll the pooris.
8. Make small or medium sized balls from the dough. Take a dough ball and spread some oil on both sides.
9. With a rolling pin, roll to a round circle. You can keep the kuttu pooris slightly thick, but do not make them thin.
10. Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai or pan. Check the oil by adding a small piece of the dough in it. If it comes up steadily and gradually, the oil is hot enough for the pooris to be fried.
11. Then gently slide one poori in the oil. Fry on medium flame. It will come on the surface and also puff up.
12. If the poori does not puff, then gently nudge & press the surface with a slotted spoon, so that the poori puffs up.
13. Fry till you see that oil has stopped sizzling and the kuttu poori looks golden and crisp.
14. Then turn over the poori.
15. Fry the second side also till it turns crisp and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon.
16. Place them on paper towels to remove excess oil. Similarly fry the rest of pooris.
17. Serve kuttu ke atte ki puri hot with vrat ke aloo or dahi arbi or dahi aloo. 2 cups  buckwheat flour 
½  teaspoon cumin powder 
1  teaspoon rock salt  
1  cup  hot boiling water 
  peanut oil for deep frying,

1. Firstly chop 1 medium onion, 2 medium to large tomatoes, ½ inch ginger, 2 to 3 small to medium garlic and 1 or 2 green chilies.
2. Then add all the chopped ingredients (onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic and green chilies) in a mixer or blender jar. 
3. Also add 15 cashews. If you want you can soak cashews in hot water for 20 to 30 minutes and then add.
4. Blend or grind to a smooth paste without adding any water.
5. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan. Add 1 tej patta.
6. Then add the ground onion-tomato-cashew paste. Be careful as the mixture splutters. So keep flame to low when adding this paste. Mix very well.
7. Keep a lid on the pan allowing some steam to pass as this paste splutters a lot. Do check at intervals if the masala paste has stopped spluttering or not and give a stir.
8. When the mixture stops spluttering, remove the lid.
9. Now add ¼ turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon coriander powder and ½ to 1 teaspoon kashmiri red chili powder.
10. Mix very well and saute till you see oil releasing from the sides of the masala paste.
11. Now add chopped potatoes. Do chop the potatoes in smaller size so that they cook faster.
12. Add salt as per taste. mix very well.
13. Add 1.5 to 1.75 cups water. For a medium consistency gravy or a slightly thinner version, add more water.
14. Cover the pan with its lid and cook the potatoes on a medium-low to medium flame. Do check while the potatoes are cooking and if required add water. Alternatively, you can also use a pressure cooker to save time. Add less water if cooking potatoes in pressure cooker.
15. Once done check the potatoes by sliding a fork or knife through a few pieces. The knife should slid easily. 
16. Once potatoes are cooked and gravy is done, you will see some oil specks on floating on top of the gravy.
17. Add 200 grams paneer (cut in cubes).
18. Add ¼ teaspoon kasuri methi, crushed and ½ teaspoon garam masala powder.
19. Mix very well and cook the paneer for a minute.
20. Lastly add 2 to 3 tablespoons coriander leaves. Mix well.
21. Serve aloo paneer with chapatis, phulkas, parathas or naan. 1   medium onion

1. Rinse and then chop the palak/spinach leaves roughly.
2. Boil or steam the potatoes till they are completely cooked.
3. When they are still warm, peel and then mash them. Keep aside.
4. Heat through 1 or 1.5 cups water in a pan. Just heat the water till it comes to a gentle boil.
5. Add the palak or spinach leaves and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
6. Using a strainer or colander drain the spinach.
7. While straining, collect the stock in which we blanched the spinach in a bowl and keep aside.
8. Puree the palak/spinach with a hand blender or in an electric blender.
9. In a bowl or large plate, add all the above ingredients, except for ghee/oil meant for frying.
10. Begin to knead to a smooth dough.
11. You may not require adding water while kneading the dough.
12. But if the dough looks dry and needs water, then add the strained stock in which we simmered the palak leaves.
13. Add very less stock and knead to a smooth dough. Keep aside for 15-20 minutes.
14. Make medium sized balls from the dough and roll into 5-6 round parathas.
15. Fry the paratha on a hot tava or griddle with a few teaspoons of oil or ghee till brown spots appear on both sides and they are cooked.
16. Serve aloo palak paratha hot with pickle, curd or butter. 15 to 18  medium to large palak leaves

1. Heat 1 tablespoon ghee in a kadai or pan.
2. Then add 1 heaped cup sattu flour. Mix the flour with the ghee and begin to roast sattu flour on a low flame.
3. Stir often while roasting. The sattu just needs to be lightly roasted. Roast sattu for 2 minutes on a low flame.
4. Remove in a separate bowl.
5. Add 1/2 cup jaggery powder. You can also add grated jaggery. Even powdered sugar can be used.
6. Add 1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder.
7. Mix very well.
8. Then add 2 tablespoons ghee. The ghee can be at room temperature.
9. Begin to mix very well. If there are small granules in the jaggery powder, then you can just run the ladoo mixture in the mixer-grinder till the mixture becomes smooth. Or you can run the jaggery powder in the mixer before you add to the sattu flour.
10. Shape into ladoos while the mixture is still warm. If you are unable to form ladoos, then add a few teaspoons more of the ghee.
11. Serve sattu laddu as a sweet snack. These ladoos stay good at room temperature for a week. If its too hot and humid in your city, then do refrigerate these ladoos.

1. Rinse and then finely chop 2 to 3 medium sized spring onions. You will need 1/2 cup finely chopped spring onions. Keep aside.
2. Take 2 cups whole wheat flour in a mixing bowl or a large plate.
3. Now add the chopped spring onions along with 1/2 teaspoon ginger garlic paste, 1 green chili, chopped, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1/4 teaspoon red chilli powder, 1/4 teaspoon garam masala powder,1/2 teaspoon ajwain seeds. You can add cumin seeds if you do not have ajwain seeds (carom seeds).
4. Also add salt as required and 1 tablespoon oil.
5. Mix the flour with the spring onions, spice powders, oil and salt.
6. Add 1/3 cup water in parts and then begin to first mix and then knead the dough.
7. First add less water and bind the dough. While mixing and kneading, the onions release water. So be careful in adding water. If required then only add water. You can add 1/4 to 1/3 cup water. I added 1/3 cup water.
8. Allow the dough to rest for 10 minutes.
9. Then form small to medium sized balls from the dough.
10. Dust the dough ball with some flour.
11. Gently roll to a round of about 7 to 8 inches.
12. Heat a tawa or griddle. When the tawa becomes hot, place the paratha on it.
13. When one side is partially cooked, about 1/4 cooked, then flip the paratha.
14. Spread some oil or ghee on this partially cooked side.
15. Flip again when the second side is half cooked.
16. Spread some ghee or oil on this side too.
17. Flip twice or thrice, till the parathas are evenly roasted and cooked. Prepare all parathas this way.
18. Serve them hot or stack them in roti basket or a warm casserole.
19. Serve spring onion paratha with pickle, yogurt or white butter. 2 cups whole wheat flour

1. In a mixing bowl take all the ingredients mentioned "for kulcha dough" above, except water.
2. Then with a spoon or with your hands lightly mix everything.
3. First add 1/4 cup water. Add water in parts while kneading. The amount of water to be added, depends on the quality of flours. So add accordingly.
4. Mix and then begin to knead.
5. Add more water as required and knead to a smooth soft dough. Cover the dough and keep aside for 2 hours for it to leaven.
6. Before preparing kulchas, crumble or grate paneer. If the paneer is fresh and soft, then you can crumble easily.
7. Add all the herbs, spices powders and salt to the paneer.
8. Mix the spices and herbs with the crumbled paneer very well. 
9. Check the taste and add more of the salt, green chilies, red chili powder, garam masala powder and dry mango powder if required. Cover and keep aside.
10. After 2 hours, lightly knead the dough again.
11. Make medium sized balls from the kulcha dough. If you want you can keep the dough balls covered for another 15 to 20 minutes before stuffing and rolling.
12. Dust the dough balls with some whole wheat flour.
13. With a rolling pin, roll it into a diameter of 5 to 6 inches diameter.
14. Place 2 to 3 tablespoons of the paneer stuffing in the center. Keep 1 to 1.5 inches space all over the circumference.
15. Bring the edges together and join them at the center.
16. Press the joined edges at top and sprinkle some sesame seeds. 
17. Press the sesame seeds with your fingers or very lightly with the rolling pin so that they get stuck to the dough. Adding sesame seeds is optional. You can skip it.
18. Sprinkle some flour and gently roll to a large disc of about 6 to 7 inches in diameter.
19. On a hot tava or griddle, gently place the stuffed kulcha.
20. Flip over when one side is partly cooked. Spread some ghee or oil on this side of paneer kulcha. The amount of ghee or oil to be added, depends upon you. You can either add less or more or skip it altogether.
21. Flip again. now spread some ghee or oil on this side.
22. Flip again. press the edges with a spatula to ensure that they are cooked.
23. Flip once or twice to ensure even roasting and cooking. Place them in a roti basket. Add ½ to 1 teaspoon of butter and spread it with a butter knife or spoon.
24. Make all the paneer kulcha with the above method and stack them up. 
25. After making each paneer kulcha, wipe the tawa with a cotton kitchen towel to get rid of the browned or burnt flour particles. You can also serve them straightaway from the tawa to the plate.
26. Serve paneer kulcha hot or warm with butter, curd or mango pickle or punjabi chole or any chana or legume curry of your choice. 1 cup whole wheat flour

1. Firstly boil 3 medium sized potatoes and ⅓ cup green peas in a pressure cooker. Take the green peas in a bowl and place in the cooker. Just add some water to the bowl containing peas. 
2. Pressure cook potatoes with enough water just about covering the potatoes for about 3 to 4 whistles or 7 to 8 minutes on medium flame. When the pressure settles down, then open the lid. Drain the water and let the potatoes become warm or cool.
3. Break 1 slice of bread in pieces and add in a mixer jar.
4. Grind to get bread crumbs. Keep aside.
5. Rinse, peel and then grate 1 small carrot. You can even boil carrot along with potatoes if you want. Keep aside.
6. Take roughly chopped ½ inch ginger, 2 garlic cloves, 1 green chili (roughly chopped) and 8 to 10 black peppercorns in a mortar-pestle.
7. Crush to a coarse paste.
8. Peel the potatoes and take in a bowl. Also take the steamed green peas. Drain potatoes and green peas very well before adding in the bowl. 
9. Now mash the boiled potatoes and green peas well.
10. Add the grated carrots and 2 tablespoons coriander leaves.
11. Also add the crushed ginger+garlic+green chili+black pepper paste.
12. Add 2 pinches turmeric powder, ¼ teaspoon red chilli powder, ¼ teaspoon garam masala and salt as required.
13. In a plate or bowl take some water and dip 1 bread slice in it.
14. Remove and squeeze all the water from the bread very well. Do this method with 3 bread slices. The bread slices have to be large and similar to a sandwich bread slice.
15. Add the squeezed bread pulp in the bowl containing veggies and spices.
16. Mix very well. Check the taste and add more salt if required. For a slight tangy taste, you can even add some lemon juice or dry mango powder (amchur).
17. Take a portion and shape into a cutlet or patty.
18. In a small plate take 3 to 4 tablespoons of the  breadcrumbs.
19. Place the bread cutlet on the bread crumbs.
20. Coat the cutlet with the bread crumbs. Gently press so that the bread crumbs stick to the cutlet. Dust off the extra bread crumbs.
21. This way coat all the bread cutlets with bread crumbs. The extra bread crumbs you can keep in a small jar and freeze.
22. Heat 2 to 3 tablespoons oil in a tawa or a pan. When the oil becomes medium hot, place the bread cutlets on the tawa.
23. When one side is golden, gently flip and fry the second side.
24. Flip again and a couple of times to get an even golden color on the crust.
25. Place them on a kitchen paper towels.
26. Serve bread cutlets hot with any chutney or dip of your choice. 3  medium sized potatoes

instructions:
1. Heat oil in a 2 litre pressure cooker. Add 1 teaspoon cumin seeds.
2. Let the cumin seeds splutter and crackle.
3. Then add ½ cup chopped onions.
4. Mix and begin to sauté onions on a medium-low flame till they turn translucent.
5. Now add 1 teaspoon finely chopped ginger and 1 to 2 green chilies (chopped).
6. Sauté for some seconds till the raw aroma of ginger goes away.
7. Then add 1 to 1.25 cups tightly packed tomatoes.
8. Mix and begin to sauté the tomatoes on a medium-low flame till they become mushy and pulpy. the oil also starts to leave the masala. 
9. In the meantime when the tomatoes are getting cooked, rinse, peel and chop the lauki. Keep aside. 
10. When the tomatoes have become pulpy and you see oil releasing from the sides of the masala, then add ½ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon red chili powder and 1 teaspoon coriander powder (optional). Also add 1 pinch of asafoetida (optional).
11. Sauté for a minute.
12. Then add 3 cups chopped lauki (bottle gourd or ghia). sauté for a minute.
13. Add salt as per taste and pour 1 cup water. mix very well.
14. Pressure cook lauki sabzi for 3 to 4 whistles or 7 to 8 minutes on medium flame till the lauki is cooked well and becomes mushy.
15. When the pressure settles down on its own, open the lid of the cooker. 
16. If you find the lauki sabzi to be more liquid then dry it a little by simmering in the cooker without the lid till you get the desired consistency in the sabzi. 
17. Finally add ½ teaspoon punjabi garam masala powder or garam masala powder. You can also add 2 to 3 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves at this step.
18. Mix well.

1. Rinse or wipe dry the button mushrooms. Slice off a bit of the base stalk. Then slice or chop mushrooms. Keep aside.
2. Peel, rinse and chop onion, garlic and ginger. Also chop tomato. Keep aside. 
3. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan or kadai. add the chopped onion.
4. Mix and then saute on a low to medium flame till the onion starts turning golden.

1. First pluck the leaves from the stems of bathua greens. You will need about 4 cups of bathua leaves (175 grams). Rinse the leaves very well. Drain all the water.
2. Take the leaves in a pan. Add ¼ cup water and mix.
3. Keep the pan on the stove top. Cover it with a lid and cook the leaves on a low flame till the leaves have softened and wilted. 
4. In between do check if the leaves are done.
5. When the leaves are wilted, switch off the flame and keep the pan aside.
6. If you plan to add potatoes, then cut them in small cubes and cook with the bathua leaves. You can add about ½ cup water if using potatoes and can add 1 large potato.
7. In a another bowl, take 2 cups whole wheat flour, ½ teaspoon ajwain seeds, ½ teaspoon cumin seeds or cumin powder, a pinch of asafetida (hing) and ½ teaspoon salt or add as required.
8. Mix very well.
9. Now strain the leaves and add them to the flour.
10. Add chopped green chilies and ½ tablespoon oil. You can add about 1 or 2 green chilies, chopped. You can skip green chilies if you want.
11. Mix very well first and begin to knead. If required, then only add water.
12. Knead to a smooth dough. If you have used potatoes also, then you won't need to add any water while kneading the dough. The moisture from the bathua leaves and potatoes will be enough to bind the dough. Let the dough rest for 20 minutes.
13. Now make small to medium sized balls from the dough. Take a ball and dust it with some flour.
14. Roll to a 4 to 5 inches circle. Spread some ghee or oil on the rolled circle.
15. Make a fold and bring in the center. Make another fold overlapping the first fold. Spread ghee on these folds too.
16. Fold sideways.
17. Sprinkle some flour on the folded paratha dough. roll to a square paratha.

19. Flip when the paratha is ¼th cooked. spread some oil or ghee on the paratha.
20. Flip again when the second side is ½ cooked. spread ghee or oil on this side too.
21. Flip a couple of times and cook till the parathas are evenly roasted.

1. Firstly rinse 500 grams tinda (apple gourds) very well in water. Also rinse the other veggies like tomatoes. Keep aside.
2. Now in a blender or grinder jar or food processor/chopper, take ½ cup roughly chopped onions, 1 to 1.25 cups chopped tomatoes, 4 medium garlic cloves (roughly chopped) and ½ inch ginger (roughly chopped).
3. Without adding any water grind to a fine paste. Keep aside.
4. Peel or scrape the outer green skin of the apple gourds.
5. Now make a cross section slice on each tinda without cutting it entirely. Slice all the apple gourds this way. Keep aside.
6. Now take all of the ground onion-tomato paste in a bowl. Add ½ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon red chilli powder, ½ teaspoon coriander powder, ½ teaspoon cumin powder, ½ teaspoon garam masala powder, ½ teaspoon dry mango powder, 1 pinch of asafoetida (hing) and salt as required.
7. Mix the spice powders very well with the onion-tomato paste.
8. Take each tinda and first stuff the ground paste on one side of the cut.
9. Then stuff the ground paste on the second side.
10. This way stuff the ground masala paste in all the tinda (apple gourds).
11. There will be remaining masala paste in the bowl. Keep this aside as we will be using this.
12. Now heat 4 tablespoons oil in a pressure cooker. Add the remaining masala paste. Be careful as the paste splutters.
13. Saute for 2 minutes on a low to medium flame.
14. Now gently place the stuffed tinda in the cooker. No need to add water.

16. Once the pressure settles down, then open the lid. Check if the tinda have cooked by sliding a knife through it. If the knife slides easily, then the tinda are cooked. If not then pressure cook for 1 to 2 whistle more.

5. Now add 1 teaspoon ginger-garlic paste.

7. Then add 3 to 4 slit green chilies. Tip – use green chilies which are not very spicy or hot.
8. Mix well and sauté for a minute.
9. Then add ½ cup diced tomatoes. mix again well and begin to sauté tomatoes. When sautéing tomatoes, if masala mixture starts sticking to pan, then sprinkle some water. Mix again and continue to sauté.

11. Keep flame to its lowest. Now add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder, ¼ teaspoon black pepper powder, ½ teaspoon kashmiri red chili powder, ½ teaspoon coriander powder, ½ teaspoon cumin powder and ½ teaspoon garam masala powder.
12. Mix very well. If the mixture starts sticking to pan, sprinkle some water.
13. Season with salt as required. Mix again.

1. Soak 1 tablespoon tightly packed tamarind in ¼ cup hot water for about 20 minutes.
2. Take ⅓ cup loosely packed mint leaves in a small grinder jar. Only use the mint leaves. Do not add the stems.
3. Add the soaked tamarind along with its water. Make sure there are no seeds in the tamarind.
4. Add the following spices – 1.5 teaspoons cumin seeds, 1 teaspoon fennel, ½ teaspoon black pepper and seeds removed from 1 black cardamom.
5. Now add 1 teaspoon amchur (dry mango powder), 1 teaspoon chaat masala, 1 pinch asafoetida (hing) and black salt as required. 
6. If you do not have dry mango powder, then you can add some lemon juice. Instead of dry mango powder, kachri powder or bel powder can also be used. Instead of black salt, you can use rock salt or sea salt.
7. Grind to a smooth chutney.
8. Take the jaljeera chutney in a bowl. Also add 1.5 cups water.
9. Mix very well. Check the taste of  golgappa pani and add more salt and dry mango powder if required. You can also add some lemon juice if you want.
10. If you want then you can keep this golgappa pani in the refrigerator.
11. Rinse and then soak ⅓ cup white chickpeas and ⅓ cup black chickpeas in enough water overnight or for 8 to 9 hours. Later drain all the water and rinse the chickpeas very well in running water.
12. Add the chickpeas in a cooker. Also add 2.5 cups water. You can also add just one type of chickpea.
13. Add ½ teaspoon salt.
14. Pressure cook on medium flame for 18 to 19 minutes. When pressure settles down on its own in the cooker, open the lid and check if the chickpeas are cooked well or not. If not then pressure cook for some more time till the chickpeas are cooked well.
15. Drain all the water and take the chickpeas in a bowl.
16. In another pressure cooker, take 2 to 3 medium sized rinsed potatoes. Add enough water just about covering the potatoes. 
17. Also add ½ teaspoon salt. Pressure cook them for 5 to 6 whistles or 9 to 11 minutes on medium flame.
18. When the pressure settles down on its own in the cooker, remove the potatoes. Let them cool a bit. Then peel and chop them. Add the chopped potatoes to the cooked chickpeas.
19. Sprinkle ½ teaspoon kashmiri red chili powder, ½ teaspoon chaat masala and ¼ teaspoon black salt or add as required.
20. Mix everything well. Keep aside.
21. Keep all the elements of golgappa before assembling them – jaljeera pani, tamarind chutney, chana and potatoes stuffing. Take the golgappa puri in a small plate. Crack open the top with a spoon or with clean fingers.
22. Place the chickpeas and potato stuffing inside the golgappa puri.
23. Spoon some sweet tamarind chutney less or more as per your preferences.
24. Now spoon the jaljeera pani or golgappa pani.
25. Have them immediately.
26. You can also arrange all the golgappa elements on the dining table and let people make the golgappa for themselves.

instructions:
1. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan or kadai.
2. Add ½ teaspoon cumin seeds and let them splutter.
3. Then add ⅓ cup chopped onions.
4. Saute the onions on medium-low flame till they become translucent.
5. Next add 1.5 teaspoons ginger-garlic paste or crushed ginger-garlic.
6. Mix and saute the ginger-garlic, till the raw aroma of ginger-garlic goes away.
7. Reduce the flame to a low. Then add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon kashmiri red chilli powder and ½ teaspoon coriander powder.
8. Keep the flame low, mix the spices very well. You can even switch off the flame.
9. Next add 1 cup chopped tomatoes and 1 green chili (chopped).
10. Mix the tomatoes very well and begin to saute them on a low to medium-low flame.
11. Saute till the tomatoes become soften, becoming mushy and you see oil releasing from sides of the pan.
12. Then add 2.5 to 3 cups chopped cauliflower florets. If you want, you can even blanch the cauliflower in hot water for 15 to 20 minutes.
13. Mix the cauliflower very well with the masala.
14. Season with salt as per taste. Mix very well.
15. Then add ¾ to 1 cup water or add as required.
16. Cover the pan with a lid and cook on a low to medium-low flame till the cauliflower is cooked and tender.
17. Do check in between and if the water dries up, you can add more water.
18. Once the cauliflower is done, then add ¼ teaspoon kasuri methi. Crush the kasuri methi and then add.
19. Mix again well and switch off the flame.
20. Lastly add 2 to 3 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves. Mix well.

1. Firstly in a bowl take 2 cups water.
2. Rinse 250 grams potatoes or 3 medium sized potatoes and then peel them.
3. Grate potatoes using a medium sized grater. Do not make fine potato gratings.
4. Add the grated potatoes in the bowl containing water. Keep them soaked for 15 to 20 minutes.
5. Later from the bowl, take some portion of the grated potatoes in your palms and squeeze all the water very well.
6. Place them on a kitchen paper towel so that all the moisture is absorbed. Do this with the remaining grated potatoes as well. Spread the grated potatoes evenly on the kitchen paper towel.
7. Add 1 tablespoon rice flour. You can also use corn starch. mix very well.
8. Now take two tea strainers. One strainer should be slightly large. In the large strainer, place some portion of the grated potatoes.
9. With your fingers press and make an even layer of the grated potatoes all around the strainer.
10. You can even use a spoon and press with it to get an even layer. Spread the grated potatoes evenly all over the sides and center. The center should not be thick.
11. Meanwhile heat oil for deep frying in a heavy kadai. To check if the temperature is correct, add a few grated strands of the potatoes. They should come up steadily in the hot oil. If they take time to come up, the oil is not hot. If they come up too fast, the oil is very hot.
12. Now place the small strainer on top of the grated potatoes and gently press it.
13. Hold both the strainers. Carefully and gently keep them in the hot oil. Fry in medium flame.
14. Hold and keep the top strainer for a minute in the oil. Some oil will collect in the top strainer.
15. After a minute remove the top strainer draining the extra oil. Keep it aside. Continue to keep the strainer with the potatoes in the oil and fry.
16. With a ladle, you can even pour some oil all over the potatoes. You can do this method if you have used less oil while deep frying.
17. When the potatoes are getting fried, you will see lot of bubbles in the strainer. Use a good quality strainer so that its handle does not become hot or very hot while frying.
18. While frying you can take the strainer up to check if the potatoes are done or not.
19. Continue to Fry till the oil starts to sizzle less and you can see the potatoes becoming crisp and light golden. The potato basket will also move if you shake the strainer. This happens when the potatoes are completely fried. If the potatoes are not fried completely, there will be still some stickiness in them and they will stick to the strainer.
20. Fry till the potatoes are crisp and light golden.
21. Slowly and gently slid the strainer on kitchen paper towels.
22. The potato basket will easily slid on the kitchen paper towel. You don’t need to use a fork or knife to remove the potato basket. If fried well, it separates from the strainer easily.
23. Now using the same strainer, add the grated potatoes and press with a spoon. Don’t use your fingers as the strainer will be hot. you can also use another tea strainer. 
24. Make potato baskets with the remaining grated potatoes in the same way. Slowly and carefully fry in the oil. When you are placing and shaping the grated potatoes basket in the strainer, that time reduce the flame to medium-low. This is done so that the oil does not become very hot. later you fry at the same medium-low flame. Since by the time you make and fry each katori, the oil will be hot.
25. In a bowl take 1 cup boiled safed chana (white chickpeas). You can even use canned chickpeas. Also add 1 cup chopped boiled potatoes.
26. Sprinkle ¼ teaspoon red chili powder, ½ teaspoon roasted cumin powder, ½ teaspoon dry mango powder and ½ teaspoon black salt or add as required.
27. Mix very well.

30. Now top with some beaten curd, sweet tamarind chutney (meethi imli chutney) and coriander chutney (hari chutney).
31. Sprinkle some chaat masala and black salt as per taste.
32. Add some sev (gram flour vermicelli) and pomegranate arils as required.
33. Lastly garnish with some chopped coriander leaves. This way assemble and make all aloo katoris.

2. Crush coarsely. Keep aside.
3. In a mixing bowl take ½ cup besan.
4. Add the coarsely crushed black pepper and coriander seeds.
5. Add asafoetida, baking soda, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, sesame seeds and salt as per taste. 
6. Add 4 to 5 tablespoons water or add as required.
7. Mix to a smooth thick batter without any lumps.
8. Take 5 amul cheese cubes or 125 grams processed cheese or mozzarella cheese. Do note that the cheese cubes have to be removed directly from the fridge and then sliced. Do not use cheese cubes which are at room temperature.
9. Cut each cheese cube in two parts.
10. Heat oil for deep frying or shallow frying in a kadai or pan.
11. When the oil becomes hot, add 4 to 5 drops of the hot oil in the besan batter.
12. Mix it very well. This helps in making the pakoras crisp and they also absorb less oil while frying.
13. Now check a tiny portion of the batter in the oil. It should come up steadily and gradually on top. This means the oil is hot enough for frying pakoras.
14. Place the cheese cube in the batter and coat it evenly with the batter.
15. Now gently slid or place each batter-coated cheese cubes in the hot oil. Fry the pakoras on medium to medium-high flame.

19. Remove them with a slotted spoon.

21. Serve cheese pakora hot with any chutney or dip or sauce of your choice. Do note that cheese pakoda has to be served hot. If they are served warm or at room temperature, the melted cheese becomes thick and solidified.

1. Take 200 grams kamal kakdi or lotus stem and rinse them very well in running water. Use kamal kakdi which are fresh. If they have started to become soft and slimy then don't use them.
2. With a peeler, remove the outer skin of the kamal kakdi.
3. Now slice them thinly. You can use a knife or mandoline slicer to slice kamal kakdi.
4. Take the slices in a bowl or vessel.
5. Add enough water so that all the slices are covered and soak them for 15 to 20 minutes. Kamal kakdi has soil or sand lodged in the inner crevices of the stem. So they need to be soaked in hot water so that all the mud and sand dissolves in the hot water. 
6. Then again rinse them very well in a colander or strainer in running water. If there is still mud or sand in the crevices, then with wooden skewer or knitting needle remove the sand particles from the crevices. Then again rinse the kamal kakdi slices.
7. Now take the cleaned slices in a 2 litre pressure cooker.
8. Add 1.5 cups water.
9. Pressure cook for 4 to 5 whistles on medium flame.
10. When the pressure settles down on its own, remove the lid and check if the lotus stem slices are cooked well. 
11. They should get softened. Drain all the water very well and let them cool.
12. Then take the cooled kamal kakdi slices in a grinder or blender jar.
13. Add 2 tablespoon water and grind to a smooth paste.
14. Take the kamal kakdi paste in a mixing bowl.
15. Add 1 cup besan (gram flour), 1 green chilli (chopped), ½ teaspoon cumin seeds, ¼ teaspoon red chilli powder, ¼ teaspoon garam masala powder, ¼ teaspoon coriander powder, salt as required and 1 pinch of asafoetida (hing).
16. Mix very well. The batter has to be thick.
17. Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai.
18. Take spoonful of the batter and add in hot oil. The oil has to be medium hot.
19. When one side is light golden and crisp, then turn over and fry the second side on medium flame.
20. Fry them till they are crisp and golden. Then with a slotted spoon remove the fried koftas.
21. Place them on kitchen paper towels. This way fry all the koftas. Keep them aside.
22. In a bowl take enough hot boiling water. Place tomatoes, onions and garlic cloves in the hot water. 
23. Cover and keep aside for 15 to 20 minutes.
24. After 15 to 20 minutes, drain all the water. Chop the tomatoes, onions and garlic roughly and add them in a mixer or blender jar.
25. Grind or blend to a smooth paste.
26. Heat 4 tablespoons oil in a pan or kadai. Keep the flame to a low and then add the tomato-onion-garlic paste. mix very well.
27. The paste splutters a lot, so cover the pan with a lid keeping some open space at one side.
28. When the paste stops spluttering, then remove the lid and continue to saute the masala stirring often.
29. Saute till you see oil releasing from the sides.
30. Then add ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon red chilli powder and 1 pinch of asafoetida (hing).
31. Next add salt as per taste. mix very well and saute for a minute.
32. Then add 2.5 cups water or add as required. These koftas absorb the gravy so keep the gravy on thinner side.
33. Mix again very well. simmer on a low to medium flame.
34. Overall simmer for 12 to 14 minutes or till you see some specks of oil floating on top.
35. If you plan to serve kamal kakdi koftas immediately,, then add the koftas to the gravy. If not, then add kofta to the gravy just before serving. Do note that the gravy or curry has to be hot before you add the kofta. These koftas absorb the gravy, so add them accordingly when you serve.
36. Mix very well.
37. Then add ¼ teaspoon garam masala powder and 2 to 3 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves and then switch off the flame. At this step you can also add 2 tablespoons milk or cream. 
38. Alternatively while serving kamal kakdi koftas you can garnish with some cream or milk.
39. Mix again. If the kofta absorbs all the gravy then you can add some hot water and thin the gravy.

1. First rinse both methi leaves and palak leaves in water very well. Drain all the water. Use a colander or strainer while rinsing. 
2. In a pan heat 3 cups water till it starts boiling. Then keep the pan down.
3. Place the methi and palak leaves in the hot water. Immerse the greens in the hot water and blanch for 2 to 3 minutes.

9. Now switch off the flame and one by one add the following spice powders – ⅛ teaspoon turmeric powder, ½ teaspoon dry ginger powder, ½ teaspoon garam masala powder (or kashmiri garam masala powder), 1 teaspoon kashmiri red chilli powder, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1 teaspoon fennel powder and 1 pinch of asafoetida (hing).
10. Mix very well.
11. Add the methi-palak puree. Then switch on the flame and keep it to a low. Mix again.
12. Season with 2 teaspoons sugar and salt as per taste. mix again.

1. Firstly rinse 260 to 270 sweet potatoes very well in water.

3. After the sweet potatoes are cooked well and when they become warm, then peel them lightly and chop them. Take them in a bowl.

1. Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a pan. 
2. Fry 8 split cashews until golden and set aside for garnishing.
3. To the same pan add ½ teaspoon mustard, ¼ teaspoon cumin, 1 tablespoon broken cashews and ½ tablespoon chana dal. 
4. Fry until the dal turns golden.
5. Reduce the flame and add 10 curry leaves, 1 to 2 chopped green chilies and ¾ teaspoon ginger.

instructions:
1. Wash rice a few times and drain the water completely.
2. On a low flame cover and cook it in a large pot with 3 cups water. 
3. The rice must be cooked fully but grainy and not mushy.  OR You can also cook it in a pressure cooker by placing the rice bowl in the cooker. Cook for 2 to 3 whistles.
4. Fluff up the rice gently with a fork and cool completely. This helps to keep the rice grainy & firm. 
5. Heat a pan with ½ tbsp oil on a medium. 
6. Add peanuts or cashews and fry until golden and crunchy. Remove them to a plate.
7. Pour another 1½ tbsp of oil and add mustard, urad dal & chana dal. Fry on a medium flame until the dals turn golden & aromatic.
8. Next add ginger, green chilis, red chilies(optional) and curry leaves. Fry them until the leaves turn crisp for about 30 seconds. Do not fry for too long, ginger will turn bitter.
9. Then add hing, turmeric and salt. Immediately pour 2 to 3 tbsps water and stir.
10. Quickly water will evaporate and turn the dal softer yet keeping them slightly crunchy. Turn off the stove and remove from the heat. 
11. Transfer this to the cooled rice. (or Alternately add the cooled rice to the pan). Ensure the rice is cooled completely then squeeze the lemon juice and give a good mix.
12. Taste the lemon rice. If needed sprinkle more salt and add more lemon juice. Garnish with roasted peanuts or cashews. Serve lemon rice with plain yogurt, papad or pickle.
13. Rinse 1 ½ cups basmati rice at least thrice. Drain and set this aside. 
14. Press the saute button. When it displays hot, pour 2 tbsps oil to the inner pot of the instant pot.
15. Then add in 3 to 4 tbsps peanuts or cashews. Fry them until golden and aromatic. Remove and set aside for garnish.
16. Add 1½ tsp chana dal, 1 tsp urad dal, ¾ tsp mustard seeds, 1 to 2 slit green chilies, 1 sprig curry leaves. Fry them until lightly golden.
17. Next add ginger, a pinch of hing & ¼ tsp turmeric. Give a good stir.
18. Pour 1¾ cups water and add salt. Press CANCEL button. Deglaze by scrubbing the bottom of the pot with the spatula to avoid burn notice.
19. Add rice and mix well. Taste the water & add more salt if needed. 
20. Secure the lid of the IP with the steam release handle set to sealing position. Press the PRESSURE COOK button and set the timer to 5 mins.
21. When the Lemon rice is done, the IP beeps. Wait for the pressure to release naturally for 5 to 7 minutes. Then with the help of a spoon release the pressure manually, by moving the steam release handle from sealing to venting.
22. Open the lid and remove the inner pot & set aside. 
23. When the temperature comes down a bit, squeeze in the lemon juice and gently stir it. If needed add more lemon juice and salt.
24. Garnish lemon rice with roasted peanuts and serve with yogurt. 1½ cups rice uncooked (or 4 cups cooked rice)
2 to 3  tablespoons lemon juice  or lime juice as needed
½ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
2 tablespoon oil
¾ teaspoon mustard seeds
4 tablespoon peanuts or cashews
¼ to ½  teaspoon turmeric powder  (haldi)
2 green chili  slit (refer notes if making for kids)
1 sprig curry leaves  (kadi patta)
1 ½ teaspoon chana dal (bengal gram) (optional)
1 teaspoon urad dal (skinned black gram) (Optional)
1 pinch hing (asafoetida) (optional)
½ tbsp ginger finely chopped
2 dried red chilies broken

1. Wash dal several times and soak in lot of water for at least 4 to 5 hrs.
2. Drain the water completely and transfer the dal to a mixer grinder jar. If you have a wet grinder, you can use it. 
3. Sprinkle 3 tablespoons water. Next add salt and start grinding.
4. Next scrape off the sides and then grind again. Whenever needed sprinkle only as much as 1 ½ tsps. Ice cold water evenly. 
5. Again continue to grind to a coarse thick batter. Ensure your grinder does not become hot.
6. Sprinkle water. Grind again till the batter looks fluffy and white.
7. Transfer this to a bowl. Aerate the batter by beating it with your hand in a clockwise direction for 30 to 60 seconds.
8. Test the batter if it is aerated well.  Drop a small batter ball in bowl full of water. The ball has to float meaning it is light. This is needed to get fluffy medu vada.
9. If the batter doesn't float well, means either the batter is runny or is not aerated well. Read the notes below to know what to do with runny batter. 
10. If the batter is in right consistency still it is not floating well. Then beat the batter once more. 
11. Add crushed pepper, cumin, ginger,scurry leaves, green chilies and onions. Mix everything well.
12. Heat oil in a deep heavy bottom kadai or pan on a medium heat till hot enough. 
13. Drop a small amount of batter to check if the oil is hot. The batter raises if the oil is hot enough.
14. Dip your fingers in water or oil to moisten your fingers. Water should not be dripping.
15. Take small portions of batter.  Shape to a ball, slightly flatten with thumb. 
16. Dip the thumb in water, again no dripping water. Make a hole in the center. 
17. Gently slide the vada in the hot oil by gently shaking off the fingers.
18. Or place the ball on a greased sheet. Flatten it slightly and make a hole in the centre.
19. If the oil becomes too hot, regulate the flame to medium. 
20. Moisten your fingers again. Lift the corner part of the sheet and transfer the vada on to your fingers. Then drop it just by shaking your fingers.
21. Fry medu vada till they turn golden on both sides.
22. Make them and fry them in batches till you use up all the batter. In between every batch, wait till the oil heats up, if not hot.
23. Serve medu vada with coconut chutney or tiffin sambar. 1 cup urad dal (or skinned black gram)
⅓ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
Ice cold water
Oil  for deep frying
¼ to ½ teaspoon pepper corn  (crushed coarsely)
2 to 3 green chilies (chopped)
4 tablespoon onions (chopped) (1 small)
1 sprig curry leaves (chopped)
½ teaspoon cumin seeds (jeera)
1 teaspoon ginger fine grated

1. Cook tuvar daal with haldi and water and keep aside.
2. Cook the vegetables in water enough to soften them and add haldiand salt.
3. When vegetables are cooked add tamarind paste.
4. Heat some oil in a pan, splutter mustard, add red chillies, greenchillies, curry leaves, hing, and sambhar powder and keep stiringfor few minutes.
5. Add this to the boiling vegetables.
6. Add the tuvar daal and let it cook for a few more minutes.
7. Sambhar is ready to be served with dosa, idli or vada.

9. Vegetable Upma Recipe 
10. Vada Recipe 
11. Curd Rice Recipe 2 Cup Tuvar Dal
1/2 tsp Haldi (Turmeric)
3 Red Chilles
1 tsp Sambhar powder
1 pinch Hing
2 tsp Mustard

2 tblsp Vgetables washed & chopped ( Drumstick,Green Pepper,Eggplant, Okra)

Cooking Oil

1. Add ¼ teaspoon methi seeds and 1 dried red chilli to a small pan and begin to dry roast them on a low to medium heat.
2. When the seeds turn light golden, then add 1½ teaspoon cumin seeds & ¼ to ½ teaspoon pepper corn. Roast them briefly until the seeds begin to smell good. Turn off the heat.
3. Cool & add this to a grinder or spice jar or mortar pestle. Grind them to a fine powder. 
4. Heat oil or ghee in a pot. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds & red chili. 
5. When they begin to splutter, add 3 to 4 crushed garlic, 1 sprig curry leaves and a pinch of hing. 
6. Saute well for a minute till the leaves turn crisp.
7. Add tomatoes, salt and turmeric. Saute until the tomatoes breakdown, become mushy & soft.
8. Then add the ground spice powder. Saute for 2 to 3 minutes. The spice powder must begin to smell good.
9. Next pour water. Add tamarind and jaggery. Bring this to a boil.
10. Then simmer for 5 minutes after it comes to a boil.  Soon It thickens slightly.
11. Stir well and take little rasam in a tablespoon. Cool this and taste test. Add more salt, jaggery or tamarind to adjust the taste. I make it sweet, sour & hot.
12. Add chopped coriander leaves. Simmer for a minute. Cover and turn off the stove.
13. Serve rasam hot with rice or as a soup. 2 to 3 medium tomatoes or (1 to 1½ cups) chopped or pureed
⅛ teaspoon turmeric
½ to ¾ teaspoon salt 
2½ to 3 cups water
1 teaspoon Tamarind (optional, use as needed) or lemon juice
1 to 2 tablespoon jaggery or sugar (or as needed)
¼ cup coriander leaves with stems chopped finely
1 ½ tablespoon oil  or ghee

1. Rinse and pressure cook dal with 2 cups of water for 2 whistles or until soft. 
2. Or alternately cook in a pot until soft. If using a Instant pot, pressure cook on high pressure for 10 mins & wait for natural pressure release.
3. Mash it and set aside. If you like the hotel style tiffin sambar, you can also add pumpkin to the dal for cooking. 
4. Mash everything together and set aside.
5. Soak tamarind in little hot water, squeeze and extract the pulp. Keep this aside.
6. In a pan, dry roast red chilies, chana dal and urad dal on a medium flame until lightly golden. 
7. Next add coriander seeds and roast all of them until a nice smell comes. 
8. When the dals turn deep golden remove to a plate.
9. Next in the same pan saute methi seeds until slightly dark then add cumin. 
10. When the cumin turns aromatic remove to a plate. Cool these completely and make a fine powder.
11. Add oil to a pot and heat up. Throw in the cumin, mustard and methi. 
12. When they pop, add red chilies, curry leaves and hing.
13. When the leaves turn crisp, set aside half the tempering if you wish to add at the end.
14. Add veggies and saute for 2 to 3 minutes. Add tomatoes and saute until soft.
15. Sprinkle sambhar powder and saute for a minute without burning. 
16. Pour water and cook until the vegetables are soft cooked.
17. Next pour filtered tamarind and then the mashed dal. Stir and bring the idli sambar to a boil.
18. Taste test and add more tamarind or salt as needed. Add the rest of the tempering and coriander leaves. 
19. When it begins to bubble. Switch off. You can also make a fresh tempering but I don't do.
20. Serve idli sambar hot with soft idli, dosa, uthappam, pongal & vada. ¾ cup dal (lentils) (refer notes)
2 cups water  to cook dal
2 tablespoon tamarind (use as needed)
Salt as needed
12 to 15 shallots or 1 medium onion diced
6 to 8 french beans (green beans)
1 medium  carrot diced
½ cup pumpkin cubed (optional)
1 large tomato chopped or mashed
⅛ teaspoon turmeric
2 tablespoons coriander leaves  with stalks (chopped finely)
4½ cups water  (adjust depending on quality of dal)
1 tablespoon oil or ghee (adjust to taste)
2 sprigs  curry leaves
1 dried red chili  broken

¾ teaspoon mustard seeds
1 pinch methi seeds (fenugreek seeds)
1 pinch hing (asafoetida)

½ teaspoon cumin seeds
