1. Fine chop onions & tomatoes. Slit chilli and set aside all of these. Cube the veggies to ½ inch sizes and set aside. Keep the potatoes immersed in a bowl of water until used.
2. Make a fine paste of coconut, cashews, fried gram & saunf with 6 tbsps water. If you do not like the flavor of fennel seeds you may skip it. Set aside the kurma paste.
3. Heat a pot with oil. Then saute bay leaf, star anise, mace, jeera, cardamoms, cloves and cinnamon until they sizzle.
4. Next put in the chopped onions and green chili. Fry until they turn transparent & pink in color.
5. Fry ginger garlic paste until the raw smell goes off.
6. Next saute tomatoes with salt until mushy and soft.
7. Add turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala and coriander leaves. Saute well for 2 to 3 mins until the masala smells really good.
8. Transfer the coconut paste and saute for few minutes until the kurma masala smells good.
9. Drain the water from potatoes and add them to the pot.
10. Next add the other veggies and mix well. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes and then pour water just enough to cover the veggies. Adjust salt if needed.
11. Cook until the veggies are cooked. Garnish with coriander leaves.
12. Serve veg kurma with chapati, pulao or biryani.
13. Press SAUTE button and pour oil to the inner pot of Instant pot.  Add all the whole spices and saute for 30 seconds.
14. Next add onions and chili. saute for 3 mins.
15. Add ginger garlic and saute for 30 seconds.
16. Next add tomatoes and salt. Saute for 1 minute.
17. Move the onions and tomatoes to one side. Add the potatoes to the other side.
18. Cover with an external lid and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
19. Saute all of these for 1 to 2 minutes.
20. Add in all the spice powder and saute for 30 to 60 seconds.
21. Press CANCEL button and add the coconut paste.
22. Add the rest of the veggies and mix well.
23. Pour water and deglaze the bottom by scrubbing with a spatula. This releases bits of food stuck there & avoids a burn.
24. Taste the water and add more salt if needed.
25. Secure the Instant pot with the lid and position the steam release handle/ value to sealing.
26. Press PRESSURE COOK button (high pressure) and set the timer to 1 minute.
27. After the Instant pot beeps, wait for 1 minute. Then release the pressure manually by moving the steam release value from sealing to venting.
28. Give a gentle stir. Vegetable kurma will look runny at this stage but will thicken after it cools down a bit. ¼ cup fresh coconut or 2 tbsps poppy seeds or ¼ cup coconut milk
10 to 12 cashew nuts
1 teaspoon fennel seeds or saunf or sombu or ½ tsp powder
1 tablespoon fried gram  or pottukadalai or putnalu (optional)
6 tablespoons water or coconut milk
1 small  bay leaf or tej patta
1 star anise or chakri phool (optional)
1 strand  mace or javithri (optional)
½ teaspoon cumin or jeera
2 green cardamoms or elaichi
3 cloves or laung
1 inch cinnamon  or dalchini
2 tablespoon oil

1 green chilli optional
¾ to 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste or fine chopped
¾ cup tomatoes fine chopped  - 2 medium sized
¾ to 1 teaspoon salt
¾ cup beans (8 to 10) chopped to ½ inch pieces
¾ cup carrot (1 medium) chopped to ½ inch pieces
¾ to 1 cup cauliflower (gobi florets)
1 cup potatoes (2 medium) chopped to ½ inch
¾ cup green peas or matar
1¾ cups water
2 tablespoons coriander leaves for garnish
¼ teaspoon turmeric or haldi
1 teaspoon red chili powder kashmiri or byadgi

1. Firstly add urad dal, chana dal & methi seeds to a large bowl. Rinse them very well several times and discard the water. Soak them together in enough fresh water for 4 to 5 hours.
2. Next add rice to another bowl and rinse a few times. Pour fresh water and soak in ample water for 4 to 5 hours.
3. Soak poha in ¼ cup water 30 mins before blending the batter.
4. Drain the water from the dal & methi. Add them to a blender jar along with salt, soaked poha and ¾ cup water. You can also skip salt at this stage if you live in a hot region. Add it to the batter just before you make dosas.
5. Grind to a smooth batter until smooth & bubbly or frothy. If needed add more water about 2 to 4 tbsps. It will be of thick pouring consistency and not very runny. Transfer this to a large pot. 
6. Drain the water completely from rice & add it to the jar. Then pour ½ cup water. 
7. Blend to a smooth or slightly coarse batter. It will be of thick pouring consistency and not very runny.
8. Pour this to the urad dal batter and mix well both of them well with your clean hand. Warmth in the hand will help in fermentation. The consistency should not be too thick & too runny otherwise the batter will not ferment. (Check video to understand the consistency)
9. Cover the pot and ferment it in a warm place until the batter rises and turns bubbly. If you live in a warm region, then you can just keep it on the counter overnight. It may take anywhere from 5 to 16 hours depending on the temperature.
10. To ferment in colder regions, preheat the oven at the lowest setting (140 F or 60 C) for 10 mins. Turn off the oven and keep the dosa batter inside with the oven light ON. You can also use your instant pot to ferment with the yogurt settings. Use an external lid and not the IP lid. I ferment for only 7 to 8 hours in the oven & IP.
11. Check if properly fermented: Well fermented dosa batter will rise & increase in volume. It will be frothy and bubbly. To check, drop half a spoon of this batter into a bowl filled with water. Well fermented batter will float & not sink.
12. Stir the dosa batter once. Transfer a portion of this to another small bowl to make dosas. Refrigerate the rest for up to 1 to 2 weeks. 
13. The fermented batter usually becomes thick, so add little water good enough to thin it down. At this stage it has to be of a pouring consistency yet thick. (check video)
14. If making masala dosa, you will have to make this potato masala or any chutney from here.
15. Grease a dosa pan or tawa with few drops of oil.  You can also rub the oil with a slice of onion. This prevents the dosas from sticking to the pan.
16. Heat it until hot enough. To check you can sprinkle little water over then pan. If it is ready it will sizzle. 
17. Stir the batter well in the bowl. Take a ladle full of dosa batter & pour on the center of the hot griddle/ tawa. 
18. Immediately begin to spread it evenly starting from the center in a circular motion in clockwise direction to make a thin crepe. 
19. Increase the heat to slightly high and let it cook for a minute then add oil or butter towards the edges. 
20. The edges of the dosa will begin to leave/ come off the pan when done. Continue to toast until the dosa turns golden and crisp. 
21. Not all dosas need to be cooked on the other side. Only thicker ones need. If you wish to cook on the other side, flip it when the edges begin to rise from the pan. Cook on the other side of the dosa. Then flip back and toast until the base becomes crisp & golden. 
22. Before making the next dosa, reduce the heat to low. You can also rub with the cut onion and then pour the batter.
23. Serve dosa with coconut chutney, potato masala & tiffin sambar. ½ cup urad dal (or whole skinned black gram)
¾ to 1 cup water (to blend dal)
1½ cups rice (Refer notes)
½ cup water (to blend rice, may need 2 tbsps more)
2 tablespoon chana dal (bengal gram)
½ teaspoon fenugreek seeds (methi seeds) (optional)
2 tablespoon poha (flattened rice)
½ teaspoon rock salt  (or non iodized salt or crystal salt)
½ cup whole urad dal (skinned whole black gram)
¾ to 1 cup water (to blend dal)
1½ cup rice (refer notes) 
½ cup water (to blend rice, may need 2 tbsps more)
½ teaspoon methi seeds (fenugreek seeds) (makes dosas golden)
2 tablespoons poha (flattened rice, or substitute ¼ teaspoon methi seeds)
½ teaspoon rock salt  (or non iodized salt or crystal salt)

1. Add 1½ cup rice to a bowl and rinse it well a few times until the water runs clear. Pour fresh water and soak the rice for 30 mins. Then drain to a colander & set aside.
2. Heat a pressure cooker or a pot with 2 tbsps ghee or oil. 
3. Add cashews and fry until golden. Remove to a plate & set aside.
4. Saute 3 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon piece, ¾ tsp cumin, 3 green cardamoms and 1 small bay leaf. 
5. When they begin to crackle, add 1 finely chopped onion and 1 slit green chili. 
6. Saute until the onions turn golden. Next saute 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste until a nice aroma comes out for 30 seconds. 
7. Next add in 1 cup tomatoes, salt as needed and ¼ tsp turmeric. 
8. Saute for 2 to 3 minutes. Cover & cook until the tomatoes break down & turn mushy.
9. Add ½ to 1 tsp red chili powder and ¾ to 1 tsp garam masala powder. 
10. Mix and cook until the tomato masala turns completely soft and mushy. 
11. At this stage the masala leaves the sides of the pan. Pour water & stir well. Taste the water and add more salt if needed. 
12. Bring the water to a rolling boil. Add the drained rice. 
13. Cook until the water has almost absorbed. When the rice is still soggy, lower the flame completely and cover with a lid until the tomato rice is cooked completely. 
14. Sprinkle chopped coriander leaves and squeeze in some lemon juice. Tomato rice is ready to serve hot or warm with a raita. Garnish with  cashews.
15. Stir and cover with the lid. Cook on a medium high heat. Allow to whistle once. When the pressure goes down, open the lid. Fluff up the tomato rice.
16. Soak rice for 30 mins. Press SAUTE button & pour oil to the inner pot of the instant pot. Then fry cashews until golden and remove them. Stir in the whole spices and then add onions. 
17. Saute them until transparent. Add the ginger garlic paste & saute for 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and salt. Saute them until the tomatoes break down and turn mushy. 
18. Add chilli powder, garam masala & turmeric. Saute for just 1 to 2 mins untilthe moisture from tomatoes almost dries up. 
19. Next pour 1¾ cups + 2 tbsp water. Press CANCEL button. Scrape off any bits of spices stuck at the bottom. This prevents from getting a burn notice. 
20. Stir & check the salt. Add more if needed. Then add the rice. Then secure the lid. Set the steam release handle/ value to sealing. Press PRESSURE COOK button (highpressure) for 5 mins.
21. When the tomato rice is done, Instant pot beeps. Wait for 2 mins & release the pressure manually with the help of a spoon by moving the steam release handle to venting from sealing. If you like softer rice then let the pressure release naturally for 7 to 8 mins. Then release the rest manually. 
22. Sprinkle coriander leaves & fluff up the tomato rice with a fork. Garnish with cashews. 1 ½ cups basmati rice
2 tablespoons oil or ghee
1 medium onion (chopped or sliced)
1 green chili  (slit, optional)
1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste or crushed
1 cup tomatoes (2 to 3 medium sized) (chopped or pureed)
¾ teaspoon salt  (adjust to taste)
¾ to 1 teaspoon garam masala powder or curry powder
½ to 1 teaspoon red chili powder or paprika (reduce for less spicy)
¼ teaspoon Turmeric (haldi)
2 ½ cups water for cooker (3 cups for pot & 1¾ cups + 2 tbsp for Instapot)
3 tablespoon coriander leaves (cilantro) finely chopped
1 tablespoon lemon juice (optional)
12 whole cashewnuts (split & use) (optional)
1 small bay leaf or curry leaves
¾ teaspoon cumin seeds (jeera)
1 inch cinnamon piece (dalchini)
3 green cardamoms  (elaichi)
3 cloves (laung)

1. Powder ¼ cup fried gram in a mixer grinder jar. Measure and use only ¼ cup powder for the recipe. 
2. Place a sieve over a large bowl. Measure the flours including the powdered fried gram powder. Add all of them to the sieve. Sieve them together. 
3. Crush cumin seeds in a mortar pestle. Or using a rolling pin crush them on the chopping board. Add it to the flour, along with red chilli powder, sesame seeds and salt. Mix them. 
4. Then heat up 2 tsps oil in a kadai and pour to the flour. Using a spoon mix well. Then use your fingers and incorporate the oil well. Rub the flour well in between your palms to incorporate the oil
5. This step is optional. Make a fine paste of ginger and chili if using. Add 3 to 4 tbsp water to this and filter it to a bowl. Pour this to the flour.
6. Pour more water as needed and make a dough that is non sticky but smooth. If the dough is dry then sprinkle more water. If the dough turns sticky, then sprinkle little rice flour. Taste test the dough and add more salt and chilli if you prefer.
7. Pour oil to a deep fry pan or kadai. Heat it on a medium flame.
8. Meanwhile grease the mould and fit the ribbon pakoda plate to the mould.
9. Fill the mould with the prepared dough. Cover the rest of the dough to avoid drying.
10. Check if the oil is hot enough by dropping a small portion of the dough in hot oil.  The dough has to rise steadily without browning and must not sink.
11. Press the dough in the hot oil, moving the hand in circular pattern to make a disc of ribbon pakoda.
12. Fry until golden and crisp on a medium high heat. Keep stirring and fry. Towards the end if you want you may fry them on a low heat for even crispness. Once crisp remove to a steel colander. 
13. Make more ribbon pakoda and fry in batches until all of the dough finishes. Just ensure the oil is just hot enough and not too hot.
14. Cool ribbon pakoda completely.  Break them as desired to pieces and store in a airtight jar. ¼ cup gram flour (fine besan, senagapindi)
¼ cup fried gram (roasted gram, putani, putnalu)
1 cup rice flour (fine flour)
¼ to ¾ teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to taste)
½ teaspoon cumin seeds ( jeera or ajwain or vaamu/omam)
⅛ teaspoon asafoetida (hing)(optional)
1 to 1½ tablespoons white sesame seeds
2 teaspoons hot oil
½ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste
oil as needed for deep frying
2 green chilies
½ inch ginger  (adding more leaves a bitter taste)

1. Coarsely blend red chili and cumin. This step is optional, used to give a nice color.
2. Wash and soak all lentils for 2 hours.
3. Drain water from the lentils and rinse them well. 
4. Keep aside 2 tbsp of the soaked dal separately. 
5. Add the rest of the lentils to a blender jar and blend to a coarse paste.  If required sprinkle little water while blending.
6. To the ground paste, add garam masala powder, green chilies, ginger garlic paste, coriander mint leaves, onions, coarsely crushed red chilies and cumin. Mix well.
7. Heat oil in a deep pan for frying.
8. Pick up small portions, shape them to small balls, and flatten on a greased sheet.
9. Check if the oil is hot by dropping a small portion of the mixture. It must rise slowly without browning.
10. Transfer the dal vada on to your greased fingers and drop in the hot oil. You can drop 2 to 3 vadas in one batch, depending on the size of the pan.
11. After 2 mins, flip the dal vada around to the other side. Fry till golden and crisp. Remove and drain them on a kitchen tissue.
12. Repeat making vadas and frying till you finish the ground mix.
13. Serve mixed dal vada hot with your favorite chutney. ½ cup bengal gram chana dal or senaga pappu
½ cup moong dal  or pesara pappu (optional, use any other dals)
½ cup urad dal  or minapappu (optional, use any other dals)
½ tsp garam masala
1½ tsp ginger garlic paste
1 onion fine chopped
3 to 4 green chilies  chopped (adjust to suit your taste)
3 tbsp mint  or pudina chopped
3 tbsp coriander leaves or daniya patta chopped
½ tsp cumin or jeera
2 red chilies or as needed
Salt as needed
Oil for deep frying https://www.indianhealthyrecipes.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/08/mixed-dal-vada-recipe.jpg

1. Add toor dal to a cooker or pot or a large bowl. Wash until the water runs clear. Pour 1 cup water to the dal. 
2. Then add tomatoes, tamarind,green chilies and turmeric. 
3. If using a pressure cooker then pour 1½ cups water to the pressure cooker and place the bottom plate. Place the dal bowl inside and cover. Pressure cook on a medium heat for 3 whistles. If you are coking directly in the cooker, then 2 whistles. Or you can also cook in a pot until soft.
4. Once the pressure releases open the lid. Add salt and mash the dal to slightly coarse or smooth to suit your taste. To adjust the consistency you can very well add more water. 
5. Heat a pan with ghee or oil.  Add cumin, mustard. When they begin to splutter, add red chilies,  garlic and curry leaves. If needed you can add more green chili as well. 
6. Fry till the leaves turn crisp. Add red chili powder & hing (optional). Quickly stir in the pan and pour the mashed dal to the tempering.
7. Mix well and do not cook further. Serve tomato pappu with with rice, ghee and avakaya. ½ cup split pigeon peas  (kandi pappu or toor dal)
2 medium tomatoes cubed ( I also deseed)
1 to 2 green chilies slit or chopped
1 cup water
½ to 1 tbsp tamarind or chintapandu (use as needed)
1/8 tsp turmeric or haldi
1½ tbsp Ghee  (or oil)
1 sprig curry leaves or kadi patta
¼ tsp cumin  (jeera)
¼ tsp mustard seeds
2 to 3 cloves garlic crushed (if you don't use garlic, use ginger)
1 red chilli (broken)
½  tsp chilli powder
1 pinch hing (optional)

1. Rinse and soak rice until you prepare the vegetables.
2. Skip this step if you have the masala powder. Powder mace, cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, stone flower and saunf in a small grinder. Set aside.
3. Heat a pan or pressure cooker with oil. 
4. Add the whole spices - bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, star anise and shahi jeera.
5. When they begin to sizzle, add onions and chilies and fry till golden. 
6. While the onions fry rinse and slice the mushrooms.
7. Add ginger garlic paste to the onions and fry till the raw smell disappears. 
8. Next add chopped tomatoes, turmeric and salt. Saute until they turn soft. 
9. Add red chili powder, powdered masala, mint and coriander leaves and fry for about 1 to 2 minutes. 
10. Pour yogurt or coconut milk and mix well. 
11. Transfer mushrooms, fry for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain the water from the rice completely and add the rice here. Add salt.
12. Pour 3½ cups water if making in pot. If making in a pressure cooker use only 3¼ cups water or coconut milk. 
13. Mix well and taste the water. Add more salt if needed.
14. Cook covered on a medium heat till the rice is fully done.  If making in pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle on a medium flame.
15. Garnish with coriander leaves. Serve mushroom biryani with a raita.
16. Press the saute button on the IP and pour ghee or oil.
17. When it displays hot add all the whole spices - bay leaf, cloves, cardamoms, cinnamon & shahi jeera.
18. When they begin to sizzle, add the onions & green chilies. Fry until the raw smell disappears for 2 to 3 mins.
19. Then add the ginger garlic and fry for 30 seconds.
20. Add the tomatoes and salt. Saute until the tomatoes break down & turn mushy.
21. Next add the chilli powder, turmeric and masala powder. Saute just for 30 seconds.
22. Then pour the yogurt or coconut milk and mix well scraping any ingredients stuck at the bottom.
23. Add the sliced mushrooms, mint and coriander leaves. Fry for just 2 to 3 mins.
24. Then add the drained rice and pour water. Press CANCEL button.
25. Mix well and check the salt. If needed add more.
26. Secure the Instant pot with the lid and set the steam release handle to sealing.
27. Press the PRESSURE COOK button (high pressure) and set the timer to 5 minutes.
28. When it is done, IP will beep. Wait for 2 to 3 mins and release the pressure manually by moving the steam valve from sealing to venting. For softer rice you can wait upto 6 mins.
29. Remove the Inner pot of the IP and fluff up with a fork gently.

1. You can use urad dal or roasted gram for this recipe. If using roasted gram, just blend 3 tbsps and use only 3 tbsps powder in the recipe.

8. Pour water little by little, just enough to make a smooth dough. 
9. Do not add too much water at one time. Too much water in the dough will make the murukku absorb lot of oil.

19. Place the murukku laddle in the oil or remove the murukku and slide it gently to the hot oil. 
20. Fry until golden and crisp on a medium high flame.

1. Measure and keep all the ingredients ready. Powder 2 to 3 tbsp fried gram in a mixer jar. 
2. Measure 2 tbsp flour and set aside.
3. Grease the murukku maker and put on the star plate.
4. Optional - You can sieve together rice flour, gram flour and besan if the flour is not fine.

6. Heat oil on a medium flame for deep frying. While the oil heats up knead the dough.
7. Pour water little by little as needed and mix together to form a smooth crack free dough.
8. Divide the dough to 3 parts.
9. Fill the mould with one of the part.  Keep the rest of the dough covered with a moist cloth.

1. Add urad dal & methi seeds to a bowl.  Add rice or idli rava to another bowl. 
2. Wash them very well separately until water runs clear. Soak them separately  in lot of water for at least 6 hrs. 
3. Rinse and soak poha with ¼ cup water for about 30 mins before blending. 
4. After 6 hours, drain the water from both the bowls.
5. Add dal, methi, soaked poha, salt & ¾ cup water to a blender jar or a wet grinder.  You may need another 2 to 4 tbsps water while blending.
6. If you live in a hot climate then skip adding salt now and add it just before making idli otherwise the batter turns sour. You will have to experiment with salt to know what works well for you.
7. Blend all of them till thick, smooth, bubbly & frothy. The idli batter should not turn hot or even warm as it makes dense idli.
8. Transfer urad dal batter to a large bowl.
9. A. If using rice : Add rice to the blender with water (mentioned in the ingredients). Grind to a little coarse batter (semolina texture). Pour this to the dal batter. Mix both of them well with your clean hands. The batter must be thick yet of pouring consistency. B. If using idli rava : Drain off the water thoroughly from the rava. Squeeze excess water from the rava with the help of both your palms. Rava must not look soggy. It must absolutely have no water in it, else the batter will become runny.
10. Transfer this to the urad dal batter and mix well.
11. Now mix everything well. Use your hand to mix as it helps to ferment faster and better. If needed can add little water, if the batter is too thick.
12. Set the batter aside in a warm place for at least 8 to 14 hrs. The batter ferments and rises well to double the quantity. Sometimes it may take up to 18 hours depending on the weather and temperature. 
13. If you live in a cold country, keep it in the oven with the light bulb ON. Or preheat the oven to 170 F or 80 C for 10 mins. Wait for 5 mins and then keep the batter inside.  If you have a instant pot or microwave (with yogurt function), then you can also turn it ON with the yogurt setting (low) for 6 to 12 hours or until the batter doubles.
14. A well fermented batter will yield good soft idli. The batter must rise and look fluffy but not turn sour. You will need to experiment to know the fermentation time.
15. On a high flame, bring water to a boil in an idly steamer or a pressure cooker. If using instant pot, pour 1½ cups water to your inner pot. Press the saute button and bring the water to a rolling boil.
16. Meanwhile grease your idly plates lightly. Mix the idli batter gently 1 to 2 times only. Do not over do as the aerated batter will turn flat. Fill the molds with batter.
17. When the water begins to bubble and steam up, place the stand in the steamer. Cover and steam for exactly 10 mins on a high flame. If using Instant pot, when the water begins to boil,   press CANCEL button. Keep the idli stand in the IP. Cover with the lid & position the steam release handle to venting . Then press STEAM button. Use an external timer to monitor & steam for 10 to 12 mins.
18. Once done turn off and wait for 2 mins. Remove the idly stand. Set aside to cool down for 2 to 3 mins. When cooled, the idli must not be wet on top.
19. With the help of a spoon remove the idlis to a plate. Serve idli with a chutney or sambar.

1. Wash and soak chana dal for 1 hour. Drain and set aside.
2. Dry roast urad dal or peanuts until lightly golden and cool them. If using peanuts, remove the skin.
3. Add urad dal to a blender jar along with fried gram. Make a fine powder. If using peanuts, then powder fried gram very fine, then add skinned peanuts and make a coarse powder. You can also powder sesame seeds.
4. To a mixing bowl, add rice flour, urad dal & fried gram powder, red chili powder, hing, salt, sesame seeds & chopped curry leaves. 
5. Drain the soaked chana dal and add it to the bowl.
6. Also add soft butter & mix all of them well to incorporate the butter.
7. Pour little water and begin to mix everything to make thattai dough.
8. Add more water as needed and make the dough.
9. Dough has to be non sticky, stiff and smooth. 
10. Too moist dough will make your thattai greasy as the excess moisture will soak up oil.
11. Next too little moisture in the dough will make the thattai crack a lot while spreading the dough and make them hard.
12. Taste the dough and add more salt if required.
13. Divide the dough to 14 to 16 balls. Keep it covered.
14. Heat oil on a medium flame in a wide kadai.

17. Begin to spread them moderately thin.

20. Make as many thattai as possible till the oil heats up.

27. Drain them on a kitchen tissue.
28. Repeat frying them in batches.
29. When they cool down, transfer them immediately to a tight air tight container.

6. Open the cooker when the pressure drops. If you desire, you can mash up the cooked rice & dal a bit to get creamy consistency. It should be mushy and soggy. If it is too try, add some hot water to bring it to a consistency you like. It should not be very runny or dry. Add more salt if needed and stir.
7. Heat a small pan with 2 tablespoons ghee. Split open 10 cashew nuts & fry them till golden. Remove these to a plate for garnish.
8. To the same pan, add ½ teaspoon cumin seeds & ½ teaspoon crushed pepper. When the seeds splutter, then add green chili (optional), ginger and turmeric. Saute well until the tempering turns aromatic. Then add hing.
9. Pour this to the cooked pongal. Mix and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes so the flavors are absorbed. Serve ven pongal with coconut chutney or sambar.
10. Rinse rice and dal a couple of times and drain the water. Press SAUTE button and pour ghee to the steel insert. 
11. Fry the cashews until golden and remove them to a plate. Then add cumin seeds and crushed pepper.
12. When they splutter, add ginger, curry leaves, green chilies and hing. Saute for 30 seconds.
13. Then add turmeric, moong dal and rice. Saute for 2 to 3 mins until the moong dal begins to smell good. 
14. Pour 3 cups water and add half teaspoon salt. Deglaze the pot by scrubbing the bottom with a spatula.
15. Press CANCEL button and secure the instant pot with the lid. Position the steam release valve to sealing.
16. Next press PRESSURE COOK button and set the timer for 9 mins. When the IP is done, it beeps. Let the pressure release naturally. 
17. Stir and taste test. Add more salt if needed. If the consistency is too thick, pour some hot water. Garnish ven pongal with fried cashews. ½ cup rice (or any - millets, oats, quinoa)
½ cup moong dal (skinned split mung beans)
2½ to 3 cups water (more if needed)
½ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
2 tablespoons ghee (½ tbsp more for serving)
10 cashew nuts  (or as needed, optional)
½ teaspoon cumin  (jeera)
½ teaspoon black pepper corn (crushed)
1 inch ginger  (grated or paste or sliced or chopped)
1 sprig  curry leaves
1 pinch asafoetida (hing)
1 pinch turmeric (haldi)
1 green chili slit (optional, skip if offering to god)

1. Steam or boil potatoes without making them mushy. You can boil in a pot or cooker.
2. Pour oil to a hot pan. Add dal, mustard and cumin.  Fry until the dal turns golden.
3. Saute ginger just for 30 secs.
4. Next add onions,salt, curry leaves and green chilies. Fry them. 
5. When the onions turn golden, add the turmeric, garam masala, coriander powder and saunf.
6. Add potatoes and mash them a bit without making them mushy. 
7. Mix well. Sprinkle lemon juice and coriander leaves.
8. Cool this and make 6 to 8 balls.
9. Add besan, rice flour, salt, chili powder and turmeric to a large mixing bowl.
10. Pour enough water little by little and mix it well to make a batter that is neither too thin or nor too thick.  The batter must be moderately thick and smooth.
11. Beat the batter well. 
12. Heat oil in a deep fry pan or kadai. 
13. When the oil is hot enough, do the heat test by dropping a drop of batter. It must raise in the oil slowly and should not sink or turn brown quickly.
14. With the help of a tbsp dip each ball in the batter, swipe off the excess and drop in the hot oil.
15. Each batch you can fry about 3 to 4 balls depending on the size of your pan and oil used.
16. After a minute begin to stir and fry until golden.
17. Repeat making all until all the balls are done.
18. Drain the golden fried aloo bonda on to a kitchen tissue.
19. Serve aloo bonda hot or warm with chai or chutney. 1 ¼ cup potatoes or aloo (cubed) - 3 medium sized 
1 small  onion  (chopped or thinly sliced)
1 ½ tbsps Oil
1/8 tsp turmeric or haldi
1 sprig  curry leaves  chopped
¼ tsp mustard seeds
¼ tsp jeera or cumin
1 tsp urad dal (skinned black lentils)
½ tsp ginger  grated
Salt  to taste
2 green chilies (slit or chopped)
¼ tsp coriander powder
2 pinches saunf  or sompu or fennel seeds crushed (optional)
¼ tsp garam masala  (optional)
Salt  to taste
lemon juice  optional
2 tbsp coriander leaves  optional
½ cup besan  or chickpea flour (1 tbsp more if needed)
2 to 3 tbsp rice flour (1 tbsp more if needed)
water  as needed
Salt  to taste
2 pinches chili powder for color (optional)
1 pinch turmeric  for color
Oil  for deep frying

1. Wash and slice bitter gourd thinly. You can also discard seeds if you prefer.
2. Heat oil in a pan. Saute cumin until they crackle and add hing.
3. Add chopped onions and curry leaves. Saute until they turn pink.
4. Add bitter gourd slices and sprinkle salt. Saute for 2 to 3 mins.
5. Cover and cook on a low heat until half cooked.
6. Add fennel powder, coriander powder, red chili powder. Mix every thing well.
7. Cover and cook again on a very low heat until soft cooked. If the curry looks very dry sprinkle very little water. Check for spice and salt, if needed add more.
8. Add coriander leaves and stir.
9. Squeeze in the lemon juice and mix well.
10. Transfer karela sabzi to a serving bowl.
11. Serve bitter gourd curry with rice or roti. 250 grams karela or bitter gourd
2 tbsps oil
½ tsp cumin / jeera
1 pinch asafoetida (optional)
1 green chilli  slit (optional)
1 tsp saunf powder  / fennel powder / sompu powder
1 tsp red chili powder
1/8 teaspoon turmeric  or haldi
1 tbsp coriander powder
Salt  as needed
1 onion , medium to large ,  chopped finely
1 sprig curry leaves
1 to 2 tbsps Lemon juice or as needed (I used half)
3 tbsps coriander leaves finely chopped

ingredients.ingredient: Saunf Powder Fennel Powder Sompu Powder

instructions:
1. Wash 1 cup rice until the water runs clear. 
2. Soak it for at least 20 to 30 minutes. Drain and set aside. 
3. While the rice soaks, slice 1 medium onion thinly & slit 1 green chilies.
4. Heat a pressure cooker or a pot with 2 tablespoons of ghee. 
5. Fry 14 cashews till lightly golden, add 14 raisins and stir up. 
6. When they turn plump set them aside in a plate.
7. To the same pan, add onions. You can also skip onions. 
8. Fry them till golden to make the fried onions / barista. 
9. These onions are used for garnishing and they add flavor to the rice.
10. Add all the whole spices to the pan & fry for a min until aromatic. 
11. Add green chilies, drained rice & fry on a medium flame for about 3 to 4 minutes. Stir to prevent burning . 
12. Pour 1¾ cups water and salt as needed.
13. You may need to add more or less water depending on the rice. 
14. Taste the water and check the salt. If needed add more.
15. If making in a pressure cooker allow the cooker to whistle once on a medium flame. If making in pot, cover and cook on a very low flame until the rice is done.
16. When the pressure releases, gently fluff up the rice with a fork. 
17. Transfer ghee rice to a serving bowl or plate. Garnish with raisins, cashews, fried onions and coriander leaves.
18. Serve ghee rice with any gravy like kurma, curry or even with egg roast. You can also eat it plain.
19. Press the SAUTE button & add ghee to the inner steel pot of the Instant pot.
20. When the ghee melts, add the cashews & saute until they turn light golden.
21. Then add in the raisins and stir until they plum up. Remove the cashews and raisins to a small plate.
22. Stir in the onion slices to the ghee and spread them in a single layer.
23. Next stir them every now and then until they turn golden to light brown & aromatic. If the pot is too hot, you can switch the saute to low by pressing (saute button again). Drain the ghee well and remove to the same plate.
24. Now add in all the whole spices, followed by the green chilli and drained rice.
25. Saute for 30 to 60 seconds & press CANCEL button.
26. Pour water and add salt. Deglaze by scrubbing the bottom of the steel pot with a spatula. Taste the water and add more salt if needed.
27. Secure the instant pot with the lid. Position the steam release handle/ vent to sealing.
28. Press the PRESSURE COOK button (or manual on older IPs) and set the timer to 5 mins.
29. When the IP beeps, wait for natural pressure release for 2 to 3 mins. For softer rice, you can wait upto 5 mins. Then release the rest manually by moving the steam release handle from sealing to venting.
30. Cool down a bit and then garnish ghee rice with fried onions, raisins and cashews. 1 cups basmati rice
2 tablespoons ghee or clarified butter
1 medium onion  thinly sliced (optional)
1¾ cups water for Indian cooker (1¼ cup Instant pot, 2 cups for normal pot)
1 green chilies (slit or chopped)
½ teaspoon Salt  (adjust to taste)
14 cashewnuts or kaju
14 raisins
2 inch cinnamon or dalchini
4 cloves or laung
3 to 4 green cardamoms or elaichi
1 strand  mace or javitri
1 star anise or chakri phool
1 bay leaf or tej patta

1. Firstly to make idli upma, crumble the refrigerated idlis. Set aside.
2. Heat oil in a pan and allow cumin and mustard to crackle.
3. Next add dals, peanuts and fry until the peanuts are golden.
4. Add onions, curry leaves, green chilies and ginger.
5. Saute just for 1 to 2 mins until the onions turn slightly pale.
6. Sprinkle 1 table spoon water and add turmeric and hing.
7. Add the crumbled idlis, coconut and coriander leaves. Mix everything well.
8. Lower the flame and cook covered until the crumbled idlis turn hot.
9. Adjust salt as needed.
10. Serve idli upma hot. 6 Idli
2 to 3 tsps oil
¼ tsp mustard
½ tsp cumin / jeera
1 ½ tsp chana dal
1 ½ tsp urad dal
Peanuts as desired
Pinch Hing / asafoetida
1 onion small to medium ,  thinly sliced
1 tsp chopped ginger
1 to 2 sprigs curry leaves
1 to 2 green chilies chopped or slit
Turmeric or haldi little
Very little salt
Coriander leaves few finely chopped
2 to 4 tbsps grated coconut fresh or frozen (optional)

1. Wash rice a few times and cook to keep the rice grainy. Mushy rice doesn't go well to make puliyogare. 
2. I usually cook rice with 2 cups of water in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles following the pot-in-pot method. 
3. Spread the rice and cool it completely.
4. Soak tamarind in ½ to ¾ cup water. Add jaggery and stir until it dissolves. 
5. When the tamarind turns soft, squeeze it well with your fingers and extract juice. 
6. I prefer to pass it through a filter. Set this aside.
7. Heat a pan on a low to medium flame. Dry roast chana dal, urad dal and red chilies until lightly golden. 
8. Add pepper corn. methi seeds and coriander seeds. 
9. Continue to roast stirring often until methi begins to smell good.
10. Add cumin, mustard, sesame seeds and coconut. Continue to roast stirring continuously. 
11. When the coconut begins to smell good. Add hing. 
12. Switch off the stove and cool this completely. 
13. Powder this as finely as possible in a blender. Set this aside.
14. Heat the same pan with oil and add mustard seeds. 
15. When they begin to crackle, add dals and peanuts. 
16. Roast them until lightly golden. Then add curry leaves, green chilies and red chilies.
17. When the peanuts and dal turn completely golden, add hing. 
18. Pour the tamarind and jaggery water and stir. 
19. Add turmeric and salt. Stir and begin to cook until slightly thick. 
20. Then add the powder little by little and mix. 
21. If the mixture becomes too thick, then add some more water to the tamarind and squeeze. Pour this water back to the pan.
22. Stir and cook on a medium heat until it thickens. 
23. You can add 1 tbsp oil at this moment. 
24. Cook on a low heat until the mixture turns thick and begins to leave oil. Add more salt if needed.
25. Add this to the cooled rice and mix. Do not add the entire mixture at one time. 
26. Add little by little as needed and mix to prevent too much of puliyogare gojju in your rice. 
27. You may be left with some extra puliyogare mix, which you can use up the next few days.
28. Allow puliyogare to absorb the flavors for about 30 mins then serve. 
29. Usually tamarind rice is served without any accompaniment. You can serve it with some plain curd.

1. Heat up little water and immerse tamarind in it for a while. 
2. Squeeze and extract juice. Set aside.
3. On a medium heat, dry roast peanuts until golden & aromatic, 
4. Then add sesame seeds and coconut. 
5. Fry until they begin to smell good. Cool them.
6. In the same pan, saute onions in little oil until golden.
7. Saute ginger garlic paste until the raw smell disappears. Cool this as well. 
8. Blend together with other roasted ingredients along with 2 to 3 tbsp. water. 
9. Make a thick slightly coarse paste.
10. Rinse the green chilies and wipe them dry. Make an slit lengthwise and deseed the seeds.
11. Heat oil in the same pan and fry chilies for 2 to 3 minutes. Set aside. 
12. Add mustard seeds & cumin. When they sizzle, add curry leaves and saute for a while.
13. Next add the peanut and coconut paste. 
14. Pour enough water. Stir and make a thin gravy. Break up any lumps in the gravy.
15. Next add chili powder, tamarind juice, garam masala and turmeric. 
16. Stir and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes.
17. Add fried chilies and simmer on a low heat until they wilt. 
18. Gravy also thickens by then.
19. Serve mirchi ka salan with any biryani. 2 tbsp peanuts
1½ tbsp sesame seeds
1 tbsp desiccated coconut or copra
2 tbsp oil
1 onion sliced thinly
1 tsp ginger garlic paste
6 green chillis (less hot or a mix)
½ tsp mustard seeds
½ tsp cumin or jeera
1 sprig curry leaves
1½ to 2 cups water (adjust as needed)
salt as needed
2 tbsp tamarind or small lemon sized  ball
1/8 to ¼ tsp turmeric or haldi
½ tsp garam masala
½ tsp red chili powder or as needed

1. Pluck the mint leaves from the stalks or stems. Rinse them well in a large bowl of water a few times. Drain them completely to a colander. 
2. To a blender jar, add mint leaves, roasted cumin powder,ginger, green chilies, chaat masala and salt as needed. 
3. You can also add some roasted fried gram or roasted peanuts if you prefer the chutney thick & smooth.
4. Squeeze in the lemon juice. Blend them well adding 1 to 2 tbsps water as needed. 
5. Make a fine smooth chutney.
6. Add mint, coriander leaves, salt, ginger, garlic, onion, green chilies, roasted cumin powder, sugar, salt and 1 tbsp yogurt to a blender jar. 
7. Blend to a fine paste. Whisk yogurt to smooth consistency and add the blended paste. 
8. Mix well and adjust salt, chili and lemon juice as needed.  Serve with kebabs.
9. If using chana dal and urad dal dry roast them until golden in a pan. Add cumin seeds and roast lightly. Turn off and cool. 
10. Optional - You can also saute pudina in oil for 2 to 3 mins first and use.
11. Add green chili, coconut, fried gram or dal, salt, ginger or garlic and mint to the blender jar. You can also skip coconut and use roasted peanuts.
12. Blend everything well. Add water little by little scrape off the sides. 
13. Blend again until it reaches a desired texture. If adding lemon juice, add it now. Adjust salt and chili as needed.
14. Heat a pan with oil to temper pudina chutney.  Next add red chili, mustard and dals. Fry until dal turns golden. Add hing and switch off.
15. Add this to the chutney. Stir and serve pudina chutney with sandwich, idli, dosa or any other breakfast or snack. 1½ cup mint leaves (pudina) (tightly packed)
¼ to ½ teaspoon roasted cumin powder (jeera powder)
½ inch ginger
1 to 2 green chilies
salt as needed
½  teaspoon lemon juice
¼ to ½ teaspoon chaat masala (adjust to taste)
1 to 2 tablespoon water or as needed
1 tablespoon fried gram or roasted peanuts (skip if making for chaats)
1 cup mint leaves
¼ cup coriander leaves (cilantro (optional)
2 teaspoons onions chopped (skip if not serving fresh)
½ teaspoon roasted jeera powder or cumin powder
½ teaspoon sugar
¼ teaspoon ginger grated
1 small garlic clove
2 green chilies deseeded
1 cup yogurt (thick curd)
½ cup coconut fresh chopped or 1 cup grated
¼ to ½ cup pudina or mint (loosely packed, do not use stalks) (as desired)
1 tablespoon fried gram (roasted gram (or ¾ tbsp each chana dal, urad dal)
½ teaspoon cumin seeds (jeera)
½ inch ginger  (or 1 to 2 garlic cloves)
salt as needed
2 to 3 green chilies
1 tablespoon lemon juice or 1 tsp tamarind paste
1 teaspoon Oil
1 dried red chili  broken
¼ teaspoon mustard seeds
½ teaspoon urad dal
1 pinch hing (asafoetida)

1. Add moong dal to a cooker or pot. Dry roast on a medium heat till you get a nice aroma.
2. Then rinse the dal very well and pour 1½ cup water. If cooking in a pot you may need to add more water.
3. Pressure cook on a medium flame until soft for 2 whistles.
4. Optional - Skip this step if the jaggery is clean. While the dal cooks, grate and add jaggery to a small pot with 3 to 4 tbsps of water. Boil it on a medium heat until slightly thick yet runny & of pouring consistency. When done set this aside.
5. When the pressure releases, mash the cooked dal slightly. If you prefer smooth payasam then mash it well. 
6. Dal must be fully cooked and should not be even slightly hard. If it is aldente then cook for some more time until soft adding more water if needed.
7. Pour the thin coconut milk or milk to the dal and bring it to a gentle boil on a low flame.
8. Add cardamom powder & ginger powder (optional).
9. Place a filter over the pot and pour jaggery syrup through it to the payasam. Mix it well.
10. Bring the paruppu payasam to a gentle boil. Optionally pour ¼ cup thick coconut milk. 
11. Turn off the stove. Do not boil any longer.
12. If using regular milk - Cool the jaggery syrup completely before you add here. If you pour the hot jaggery syrup to boiling payasam, it will curdle most of the times. So make sure you cool it.  Also turn off the stove and cook no longer.
13. Heat ghee in a small pan. Fry the cashews & coconut until slightly golden. Then add the raisins and stir until they become plump.
14. Pour this to the paruppu payasam. ½ cup moong dal (pasi paruppu)
1½ cup water
½ to ¾ cup thin coconut milk (or regular milk) refer notes
½ to ¾ cup jaggery  or sugar
½ teaspoon green cardamom powder
¼ teaspoon dry ginger powder (optional)
10 cashews
10 raisins
2 tablespoons dried  coconut slices (optional)
2 tablespoons Ghee  as desired

1. Boil potatoes either in a pot or pressure cooker.
2. If cooking in a pot, bring water to a boil and add the diced potatoes. Cook them just until done or fork tender and not mushy. OR If cooking in a pressure cooker, add the potatoes to a bowl and pour little water. Cover and pressure cook for 3 whistles on a medium flame.
3. Ensure potatoes are just cooked and not very soft or mushy.
4. Heat oil in a pan and add mustard and cumin. 
5. When they begin to splutter, add chana dal and urad dal. Fry until golden and then add hing.
6. Then add ginger and saute for 30 to 60 seconds until aromatic.
7. Optional step to soften the dal - Pour 2 to 3 tablespoons water to the pan and cook until the dal turns soft. This is an optional step done to soften the dal. Ensure you evaporate all of the water before going to the next step.
8. Add onions, green chili and curry leaves. Saute till the onions turn transparent. 
9. Once the onions turn transparent, add potatoes, turmeric and salt..
10. Mash slightly and add very little water or potato boiled stock to make the entire potato masala moist. Stir and cook for one to 2 mins. Taste test and add more salt if needed.
11. Add coriander leaves. Stir. Serve potato masala with dosa, puri, chapati, bread or rice.
12. Press SAUTE button and pour oil to the inner pot of the instant pot.
13. Add mustard, cumin, chana dal & urad dal. Fry all of these until the dals turn golden.
14. Then add curry leaves, onions and green chilies.
15. Saute onions well until they turn transparent or pink. Add ginger and fry for 30 seconds.
16. Transfer the diced potatoes (1 inch cubes), add salt, turmeric and pour ⅓ cup (80 ml) water.
17. Press CANCEL button. Deglaze the pot by scrubbing the bottom with a spatula to release bits of food stuck.
18. Secure the instant pot with the lid. Position the steam release handle or vent to sealing.
19. Next press PRESSURE COOK button and set the timer to 4 mins (high pressure).
20. When the instant pot is done, press cancel. Release the pressure manually by moving the steam release handle from sealing to venting.
21. If there is any excess moisture left, evaporate it in the saute mode first.
22. Give a good stir and lightly mash only after the excess moisture has evaporated. Add more salt if needed. Garnish with coriander leaves.
23. Serve potato masala with dosa, sandwiches, roti or even in wraps. 2 cups potatoes peeled & diced to 1 inch cubes (400 grams, 3 medium)
1 medium onions chopped or sliced (about ½ to ¾ cup)
½ tablespoon ginger chopped or grated (about 1 inch)
½ to ¾ teaspoon Salt (adjust to taste)
2  tablespoon oil
¼ to ½ teaspoon mustard seeds
½ teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon chana dal (optional)
1 teaspoon urad dal (optional)
1 sprig curry leaves
1 to 2 green chilies  chopped or sliced
¼ teaspoon turmeric (use more if needed)
1 Pinch hing (optional)
2 tablespoons coriander leaves chopped finely

1. Optional step: Boil tomatoes for 3 to 4 minutes in 2 cups water. This will loosen the skin. Once cool, remove the skin and discard. Discard the core as well and chop the tomatoes.
2. Toast the sesame seeds or peanuts on a low flame until aromatic and make a fine powder. If you do not have sesame, replace with almonds or fried gram. Set this aside.
3. Add oil to a pan and heat it. Add cumin and mustard, when they begin to sizzle add curry leaves, green chili and hing.
4. Next add chopped onions, salt and fry lightly till they turn pink. 
5. Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric. Fry for about 3 to 4 minutes. You can cook covered till the tomatoes turn soft and mushy.
6. Next add red chili powder, sesame seeds powder or fried gram powder. Mix and cook for one to two minutes until the curry turns thick. 
7. Taste the curry and add more salt if needed.
8. Add coconut milk and stir. When the tomato curry begins to bubble up, switch off the stove. Cooking for longer may coagulate the coconut milk.
9. Serve tomato curry with rice & ghee or with roti. 3 large tomatoes  
2 medium onions chopped
1 green chili slit
1 sprig curry leaves
1 to 2 tablespoons Oil
¼ teaspoon mustard seeds
¼ to ½ teaspoon cumin seeds
1 Pinch hing (asafoetida) (optional)
1 teaspoon red chili powder
¼ teaspoon turmeric (haldi)
⅓ teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
¼ cup coconut milk thick (refer notes)
1½ tablespoons peanuts or sesame seeds  (optional)

1. Heat oil in a kadai on a medium heat for deep frying. While the oil heats prepare the dough to make murukku.
2. Mix together flours, salt and butter in a bowl. Add water little by little as needed and make a smooth non sticky dough.
3. Grease the murukku maker and fix the round wholes plate. Fill the mould with the dough.
4. Check if the oil is hot enough. Drop a small flat piece of dough to check if the oil is hot enough. If the dough rises steadily then the oil is hot enough. If the oil is not hot enough the dough will not rise instead sinks in the oil.
5. Press the mould directly over the hot oil and fry on a medium heat. Do take care as the oil is very hot.
6. Allow to fry until golden and crisp. When the murukku is done, you will see the bubbles will reduce.
7. Drain them to a large plate and continue to make the next batch. With this recipe you can make about 2 to 3 very large murukku discs.
8. Cool these completely. Break them to 2 inch pieces. Transfer them to a air tight jar and keep covered.
9. Add jaggery and water to a large pot or bowl and heat it until all the jaggery dissolves.
10. Filter it to a wide pan for boiling the syrup. Get a small bowl ready with some water in it to check the consistency.
11. Boil the syrup on a medium heat until the syrup reaches a soft ball consistency.
12. When the syrup turns dark and thick, you will need to keep checking for the right consistency.
13. Drop about 1 tsp full of syrup in the cold water. Wait for 30 seconds. Try to make a ball with it. If you get a soft ball then the syrup is ready.
14. Switch off the stove and take it away from the hot burner.
15. Add cardamom powder and other flavoring ingredients you desire.
16. Stir well. Add half of the cooled murukku to the pan. Coat the syrup well to the murukku. Be gentle while you do this as the murukku may tend to break.
17. Drain off excess syrup and transfer them to a wide tray. If you prefer to make balls, then wait until the sweet murukku cools down a bit yet warm.
18. Moisten your palms with little water, take small portions and roll them to balls. Allow these to cool down completely. It may take several hours to dry completely. It took about 3 hours for me to dry completely.
19. Sweet murukku if prepared correctly will be dry and not sticky after drying.
20. Store them in a air tight jar and finish within 10 days. 1 cup besan  / chickpea flour / senaga pindi
½ cup rice flour
1 tbsp butter  softened or hot oil
pinch salt
Water  as needed to make dough
1 ½ cups Jaggery powdered or grated  (I used organic jaggery)
Water  as needed (I Used about ½ cup to make syrup)
½ tsp cardamom powder  / elaichi powder
Oil  as needed for deep frying
1/4 tsp dried ginger powder
pinch nutmeg  or mace powder

1. Wash rice at least twice and soak it for about 20 minutes. Drain to a colander and set aside.
2. Powder fennel seeds and pepper to a fine powder. Keep this aside as well.
3. Heat and pan, add oil and fry the dry spices until they begin to sizzle.
4. Fry ginger garlic paste until the raw smell leaves. 
5. Add fennel pepper powder and quickly stir. Be quick otherwise it gets burnt faster.
6. Next transfer the chopped veggies and green chilies. Fry for 2 minutes. 
7. Add mint leaves and fry them as well.
8. Pour coconut milk and add salt. Bring it to a boil.
9. Completely drain off water from rice and add it to the pan.
10. Cook on a medium flame until the coconut milk is absorbed by the rice.
11. When there is very little moisture left, lower the flame and cover with a lid. Cook until the rice id done for 5 mins. 
12. You can cook the rice for 1 whistle on a medium heat if using basmati rice. For other kinds of rice, you can allow to whistle twice.
13. Cook until the rice is done. If needed sprinkle water as needed. Keep the pot covered for some time.
14. Fluff up vegetable coconut milk pulao and serve. 2 tbsp Oil  or ghee (adjust as needed)
1 large  bay leaf  or tej patta
1 star anise  or chakri phool
6 to 8 cloves laung
2 inch cinnamon  or dalchini
small piece nutmeg or jaiphal
4 to 6 green cardamoms or elaichi
¾ tsp shahi jeera or caraway seeds
1 strand mace or javitri
¾ tsp fennel seeds or saunf
¼ tsp pepper corn
2 cups rice basmati 
2 tsp ginger  or ginger garlic paste
2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, potato go well)
½  cup soya chunks or meal maker (optional)
1 green chili  (deseeded and slit)
8 to 10 cashew nuts (optional)
¼ cup mint leaves or pudina (chopped finely)
3 ½ cups coconut milk
Salt as needed

1. Wash curry leaves in lot of water, drain them in a colander.
2. Soak tamarind in little warm water. Skip if using lemon juice.
3. Pour 1 tsp oil to a pan. Add the curry leaves and fry until crisp on a medium heat. Fry jeera in the same pan. Skip this step if you are using curry leaves powder.Set aside the leaves to cool in a plate.
4. If using green chilies and coconut, skip this step. Pour 1 tsp oil to the same pan. Fry chilies and chana dal until golden. 
5. Blend together curry leaves, jeera, chilies, garlic, chana dal or coconut, tamarind or lemon juice and salt with enough water.
6. Check salt and add more if needed.
7. Curry leaves chutney is ready to serve.

ingredients.ingredient: Chana Dal Senaga Pappu Coconut Peanuts

instructions: Prepare []. Heat oil if needed, add aromatics, add main ingredients and cook until done. Season to taste and serve.

1. Grease a tray and set aside. Please read the notes before you try. 
2. You can also use a parchment paper or greased foil. 
3. Grease a spatula or the base of the cup to level the barfi.
4. To a heavy bottom pan, add half cup ghee. Melt it and transfer to a cup or bowl. To the same pan, add ½ cup besan. 
5. On a low to medium flame fry until it turns aromatic. 
6. Then add ½ cup coconut or cashew powder.  
7. Fry for about 2 to 3 minutes on a low flame.
8. Keep stirring continuously to prevent burning. 
9. Next add 1 cup sugar. 
10. Pour ½ cup  milk and ¼ cup melted ghee. Stir well.
11. Cook on a medium heat until it begins to bubble well.
12. Add cardamom/ elaichi powder.
13. Continue cooking until the mixture begins to thicken.

1. Wash and chop very finely 1 small onions, 2 green chilies and handful of coriander leaves. Grate ½ carrot & ½ teaspoon ginger. If using sabsige, rinse well and chop finely.
2. Add 1 cup flour to a large mixing bowl along with 1/3 teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon cumin, chopped onions, chilies, coriander leaves and carrots. Mix everything well. You can also add about 2 to 3 tablespoons grated coconut & 2 to 3 tablespoons dill leaves.
3. Pour water little by little and make a soft dough. The dough must be smooth and moist. Divide the dough to 4 equal balls. Roll to smooth. Keep the bowl covered to prevent drying up.
4. You can make akki roti on a greased banana leaf, moist handkerchief, foil or parchment paper. 
5. Place a ball on the moist cloth or foil or greased banana leaf. 
6. Begin to spread it lightly with your fingers to make a round roti. If the edges of akki roti crack, then dip your fingers in water and join the cracks. Then continue to spread it.  
7. It can be made thick or thin to suit your taste. If making thick, make 3 finger sized wholes with one and half inches apart.
8. Heat the greased tawa on a medium high flame.  Lift the banana leaf or parchment paper and reverse it on the hot tawa. Gently peel off the leaf. 
9. When the base firms up & golden, flip it. Toast it on both the sides. After flipping it sprinkle some oil to prevent dryness. Press down with a spatula to cook evenly.
10. When brown spots appear, akki roti is done. Do not over cook it may turn hard. While you toast the akki roti, make another one on the leaf or cloth. Transfer to the tawa after the first one is done.
11. If you are making directly on the tawa then you will need 2 tawas to use them alternately. Or cool the tawa completely and then spread the next roti. 
12. Lightly grease a cool tawa & keep it on a kitchen counter. Place the ball on the tawa and spread it directly to a thin akki roti.  Place the tawa now on the stove and cook until the base firms. Then flip & cook on the other side until done. Press down with a spatula to cook evenly.
13. To make the next akki roti either use another cool tawa or wait until the first one cools completely. If you try to spread the dough on the hot tawa it will get stuck and not spread at all. Serve akki roti with chutney. 1 cup rice flour (akki hittu)

1. Wash ginger under running water to remove mud and dirt. Peel off the skin if desired. Dry it for some time or overnight on an absorbent paper or cloth.
2. Soak tamarind in boiled and cooled water till we need it. Do not use lot of water, it must be just enough to soak the tamarind, so that we get a thick paste.
3. Dry roast 1 tbsp. Fenugreek seeds and powder them to fine powder. Set aside only 1 tbsp. powder to use.
4. Chop ginger to bite sized pieces and fry them on a medium flame till they turn slightly golden in little oil, for 3 to 4 minutes. Cool these completely
5. Blend it in a mixer to a smooth paste without adding water. Do not let the blender heat up.
6. Squeeze filter the tamarind pulp to remove impurities. We need thick tamarind paste, if it is thin, then boil the filtered tamarind to thicken.
7. All the ingredients need to be cool at this stage. Add the tamarind pulp, red chili powder, turmeric and salt to the ginger mix. Blend well again.
8. Add jaggery and blend again. Do not add the sweetener before you blend all the other ingredients well since this will thicken the mix and the mixer becomes loaded. Check the taste of the pickle now, it has to taste sour, sweet, hot and spicy. Adjust any taste as needed.
9. To finish off add methi powder and mix.
10. Heat the rest of the oil in a pan, add mustard and garlic. Add curry leaves, red chilies and hing. fry till the leaves turn crisp. Off the stove. Add the ginger pickle to the seasoning and mix well in the hot pan.
11. Cool completely and store allam pachadi in a glass bottle.

1. Rinse and soak tamarind in ½ cup hot water. Once cool, squeeze up and filter to remove the pulp.

3. Rinse ladies finger under running water. Wipe them dry with a clean kitchen cloth.

5. Chop tomatoes and set aside.

16. Taste the pulusu and add more salt, tamarind water and jaggery if needed. It should typically have different tastes like sweet, sour and hot.

1. The recipe needs ¼ cup fried gram powder. You can replace it with besan. If using fried gram then add the gram to a chutney jar and make a fine powder. Use only ¼ cup powder in the recipe.
2. Add rice flour, besan, fried gram powder, salt, sesame seeds, ajwain, hing & chilli powder to a large mixing bowl. Mix up well.
3. Heat 1 tbsp butter or oil until very hot. Pour it quickly to the mixture. This will make the chakli crunchy.
4. Gently mix with a spoon as the oil is too hot. Then mix well with your hand to incorporate the oil evenly. 
5. Pour water little by little and make a dough. Do not knead it just mix to get a non sticky dough.
6. Grease the chakli maker and fill it with the dough.
7. You can make chakli either on a moist cloth, dry cloth or parchment paper. Slowly press the chakli maker to release the dough. Make spirals of the dough. Use your finger to end the spiral. Join the end of the chakli to the spiral. (check video)
8. Heat oil on a medium high flame. Continue to make the chakli while the oil heats up.
9. Check if the oil is hot enough by dropping a small portion of dough to the hot oil. The correct temperature is when the dough rises to the surface without browning.
10. Remove the chakli to your fingers and gently slide to the hot oil. You can fry about 3 to 4 chakli in each batch depending on the size of your pan.
11. Do not disturb them for 1 to 2 minutes. When they firm up, turn them to the other side. Fry on a medium flame on both the sides until crunchy.
12. Remove chakli to a colander and cool them completely. Transfer chakli to a air tight steel or glass jar. 1 cup rice flour (refer notes)

4. If using desiccated coconut set the pan aside for 15 minutes for the coconut to absorb the milk and soften.
5. Mix all of the ingredients well. 
6. Begin to cook till the coconut ladoo mixture thickens and all the moisture evaporates completely. 
7. The mixture must still be moist and not dry.
8. Add cardamom powder and nuts. Mix well. Cool the mixture slightly. 
9. When it comes down to warm temperature, take small portions of this to your palm and press down with your fingers to bind the mixture. This gives the round shape coconut ladoos. (Check video)
10. When they are still warm and moist you can also roll the ladoos in desiccated coconut.
11. Store coconut laddu in an airtight jar and refrigerate. Use within 5 to 7 days.
12. To a pan, add 1½ cups desiccated coconut, ¼ tsp cardamom powder and ½ cup + 2 tablespoons condensed milk. 
13. Mix up all of these and cook on a low flame stirring often. Taste test and If needed add more condensed milk for more sweetness. 
14. Cook stirring continuously, till the mixture thickens and turns to a mass. (check step-by-step photos above for consistency) 
15. Turn off the stove. At this stage the coconut ladoo mixture must be still moist. If you overcook then the ladoos will turn hard.
16. Cool and add chopped pistachios. When it is still warm, take small portions of this mixture to your palms and press down with your fingers to give a round shape to the coconut ladoos. 
17. Cool these completely. Store in a air tight box and refrigerate. Use up within a week.
18. Heat 1 tsp ghee and fry cashews. Remove and keep them aside. In the same pan, mix together fresh coconut and grated jaggery in a pan. 
19. Once the jaggery melts, taste test and add more if needed. Cook until the mixture smells good , turns thick & binds together. 
20. Add cardamoms and fried nuts. Cool down and roll to balls. 
21. Store coconut laddus in a air tight jar and store at room temperature. Use up within 7 days. 2 cups grated coconut (fresh or fine desiccated)

1. Wash and soak chana dal for 4 to 6 hours and rice for 20 minutes. Drain and set aside.
2. Heat oil in a pot and fry spices until they begin to crackle.
3. Add onions and fry until lightly done. Next add ginger garlic paste and fry until the raw smell is gone.
4. Transfer veggies and pudina, saute for 2 minutes.
5. Add soaked and drained rice and dal. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
6. Pour water salt and cook until the rice is done. Towards the end, when the water is almost absorbed, cover and simmer on a low flame. If using pressure cooker, cover and cook on a low heat for 5 minutes.

1. Clean the cauliflower and cut the florets to the desired size.
2. Soak thoroughly in salted Luke warm water for 10 mins.
3. Wash them under fresh running water, drain and set aside. If you have a chance to sun dry, do it for 3 to 4 hours. If you cannot sun dry, then dry them on a cotton cloth and fan dry or leave it for over night
4. Make sure there is no water in the florets, else the oil might splash on to you while frying.
5. Heat the desired amount of oil in a wide pan, once it is smoky hot, add cauliflower and fry them either deep fry or sauté in little oil just for 2 to 3 mins on a medium high flame. This is done to remove excess moisture from florets and increase the shelf life. Do not over fry the cauliflower, they must be crunchy after they are sauted or fried. So 2 to 3 mins of frying is good enough
6. Drain the oil and keep the florets for cooling. Do not leave the cauliflower in the oil else they will turn very soft, since it will continue to cook as the oil is hot.
7. Dry roast fenugreek seeds till you get a nice aroma. Do not burn them. Set this aside to cool.
8. Powder fenugreek seeds and mustard seeds.
9. In a wide utensil, put back the fried cauliflower and pour the oil (you can use deep fried oil)
10. Add the mustard and fenugreek powder, red chili powder, salt, turmeric, crushed garlic if using. Pour the lemon juice all over.
11. Mix everything well. Your pickle is ready, you can bottle it in a clean dry jar.
12. Stays good for about a month in refrigerator.
13. Serve cauliflower pickle with rice and ghee. 3 cups Cauliflower Medium sized ,  florets

1. Add curd, ginger garlic paste, chilli powder, salt, turmeric, pepper powder & chopped curry leaves (optional) to a mixing bowl. Mix & taste it. Add more salt if needed. 
2. Then stir in the cubed boneless chicken. Mix well. Set aside for at least 45 mins to 1 hour. You can also marinate overnight & pop it in the fridge for best results.
3. Sprinkle the dry flour over the marinade. If you chose to use egg, you can add it now. Mix well. If not using egg the marinade may turn dry so sprinkle some water if needed to bind the flour well.
4. If using yogurt for seasoning, whisk it well with a fork or whisk until smooth. Set aside.
5. Heat oil in a deep pan until hot enough. Test if the oil is hot by dropping a small portion of the batter to the hot oil. The batter must rise without burning a lot.
6. Slide in the chicken pieces one by one. Fry on a medium high flame until crisp & golden. When the chicken is done cooking, the bubbles will begin to cease. Drain them on a kitchen tissue.
7. Wipe off any moisture on the curry leaves & fry them in the hot oil & set aside for garnishing.

9. Quickly stir everything well. When the mixture bubbles well & turns thick, add fried chicken and toss well.
10. Fry on medium heat till it absorbs all the moisture & coats the chicken. This just takes 2 minutes. Over frying can make the chicken hard. So turn off in time.

instructions:
1. Add the following ingredients to a plate. - salt, ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, coriander powder and lemon juice. 
2. Mix all of these together to make a paste. Taste the marinade and adjust salt or spice as needed. 
3. Rinse the fish fillets thoroughly. If using a fish like salmon, make slits on the fillet.
4. Apply this marinade to the fish pieces. If needed add 1 tsp of water to apply the paste well. Set this aside.
5. Add flour, salt, red chili powder and curry leaves. Mix all of these. Taste this and adjust salt or spice as needed.
6. Place the fish in flour mixture. Make sure flour coats well on to the fish on both the sides. Fish looks floury at this stage. Set this aside till the dry flour turns moist. 
7. The moisture in the fish makes the flour damp and it sticks well to the fish. This takes around 10 to 15 minutes.
8. Heat a griddle, pan or tawa. Add 2 tbsp oil and spread it well. 
9. Heat it on a low flame. Fry the fish fillets till crusty on both the sides.
10. Be gentle while flipping the fish otherwise the masala comes out. 
11. Fish can be pan fried or shallow fried both yield almost the same result.
12. Garnish fish fry with sliced onion and grated carrot. Serve with a meal or as an appetizer.
13. After the second marination, Gently brush a generous amount of oil over the fillet. heat the oven at 170 C for 15 minutes and grill for about 25 minutes. You may need to grill for more or long depending on the thickness of the fillet or the variety of fish. ½ kg fish (pieces or fillets)

5. Place the paratha and cook until it is slightly firm on one side., Flip and cook on the other side as well until slightly firm and the layers get puffed & separated. Paratha has to be half cooked at this stage and not completely done.
6. Quickly remove the paratha to a plate. Gently open the top layer on one side keeping the other sides intact. Pour half of the egg mixture and gently spread. Cover back the layer.
7. Gently transfer the paratha to the tawa. Drizzle some ghee or oil. Allow to cook on a medium flame.
8. When the egg is almost cooked flip the paratha and press it gently.
9. Cook on the other side as well until the egg is done completely and the paratha has golden spots.
10. Serve egg paratha with chutney or vegetable salad. ½ cup wheat flour or atta
warm water as needed

1 pinch turmeric

1. Boil eggs, shell them. Pierce them randomly with a fork or knife and keep aside.
2. Add oil to a pan and heat it. Add cumin and allow to crackle.
3. Add onions, sprinkle salt and fry until golden.
4. Add ginger garlic paste and fry till the raw smell goes off.
5. Add tomatoes and fry until they turn mushy.
6. Add eggs, curry leaves, red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric and fry for about 3 to 5 minutes or till the spice powders blend well. If needed sprinkle 1 to 2 tbsp. water to prevent the roast looking dry. The raw smell of tomatoes should also disappear. Serve egg roast with rice, bread or chapathi. 1 tbsp oil  (adjust as needed)

¾ onions thinly sliced

1. Dry roast sesame seeds until aromatic. Cool and powder them finely. Blend it a jar to powder. Add  jaggery, cardamom and blend well. Make balls . Set aside.
2. Bring water to a boil. Switch off the stove and add flour.
3. Stir well and cover. Set aside for a while.
4. Knead the dough well to make crack free dough.
5. Make 11 equal sized balls. Grease your fingers and begin to flatten the ball. 
6. Spread the dough to a small puri. If the edges crack, dampen your fingers and join the cracks.
7. Place a ball and bring all the edges together. Give a modak shape to it.
8. Bring 2 cups water to a boil in a steamer or pressure cooker. Place the kozhukattai on a basket lined with cloth.
9. Place the basket in the steamer when the water comes to a boil. If using cooker, then do not use weight.
10. Steam ellu kozhukattai in a steamer for 8 to 10 minutes. 1 cup sesame seeds

1. Mix together all the marination ingredients except fish. Taste the marinade to check the spice and salt. Marinate the fish and set aside till the rice gets cooked.
2. This step is optional. Soak saffron in warm milk. set aside.
3. Wash basmati rice under running water until the water runs clear. Then soak for at least 20 to 45 mins. Follow the instructions on the pack for the timing. Drain the rice to a colander.
4. Bring 6 to 8 cups water to a boil in a large pot of water. Pour 1 tsp oil and then add salt. 
5. Add the drained rice and cook till aldente. Do not make the rice mushy. It must be cooked fully but must be firm and grainy.
6. Drain the cooked rice to a colander. 
7. Fry the fish in little oil on both the sides till the fish gets cooked and the masala turns golden. Set this aside along with any stock or oil left in the pan.
8. Add more oil to the pan and fry onions till lightly golden. Stir often while you fry. Set aside a few for garnish.
9. To the same pan, add spices and fry them for a minute.
10. Add ginger garlic paste and fry until the raw smell goes off. If using tomato, add it now and cook until it turns soft. Add biryani or garam masala and coriander powder, red chili powder and fry quickly.
11. Pour yogurt or coconut milk and stir. Cook till the mixture thickens. Set this aside.
12. Add half of the rice to the biryani pot or handi, layer the gravy, add some chopped mint and coriander leaves. layer the fried fish along with oily stock if any.
13. Layer the rice again and then sprinkle coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried onions. pour the saffron milk. Sprinkle kewra water.
14. Seal it with a foil and put it on a hot tawa. Cook on high flame for 2 minutes and very low flame for 10 minutes.
15. Allow fish biryani to rest for about 15 minutes before serving.
16. Slice thinly 1 large onion, chop chilies and coriander leaves. You can deseed the chilies. Whisk one cup curd/ yogurt/dahi with salt, add the chopped ingredients and mix. You can add more or less curd as desired. Cumin powder can also be used. It aids in digestion. 500 grams fish or half kg
