instructions:
1. Add water to a heavy bottom pot and bring it to a boil, add 1 tsp. ghee and stir.
2. Pour sooji / rava slowly in a stream to the boiling water, while stirring the water with the other hand to avoid lumps. Switch off the stove. Barely in few seconds all the water gets absorbed by rava.
3. Cover the pot for about 5 minutes, to finish cooking the rava thoroughly.
4. Add sugar and cardamom powder. Do not cook now
5. Mix well, let the sugar to melt fully. The mixture looks lumpy. Break the lumps with a ladle or masher to remove all the lumps.
6. On the stove on a low flame. Cover the pot and cook for about 2 minutes. Mix everything once more and keep the pot covered for at least 5 minutes
7. Cool the mixture completely. Grease the palms and knead while the mixture is warm.
8. Roll to 12 equal sized balls, ensure there are no cracks on the balls. If you desire you can flatten them.
9. These need to be fried immediately, otherwise they will lose moisture
10. Heat ghee or oil in a pan. Add appalu and deep fry or shallow fry till golden

1. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy bottom pot and fry cashews until light golden. 
2. Then add raisins and fry until they swell up. Remove to a plate and set aside.
3. In the same ghee add the rava and fry on a low to medium heat until aromatic and crunchy. 
4. Do not brown or discolor the rava as the aroma of the rava kesari will change.
5. While the rava is getting roasted, pour water to another pot and bring it to a boil.
6. When the water turns boiling hot, slowly pour it to the rava by consistently stirring to prevent lumps. 
7. The water will be absorbed by the semolina soon. Keep stirring and make sure there are no lumps.
8. When you see there is no excess water in the pan, then cover and cook on a low flame for 2 to 3 mins. This is just to ensure rava is cooked completely and turns fluffy.
9. Add sugar and mix well. Sugar will dissolve and the entire rava kesari mixture turns gooey.
10.  Keep stirring and cook until the mixture thickens and the moisture is evaporated.
11. Then sprinkle cardamom powder, saffron or kesari and ghee. I used about 3 tbsp ghee. 
12. Mix well and cook for 2 to 3 mins until the rava kesari leaves the pan. Cover and rest for 2 to 4 mins.
13. Grease a mould or round cup and then scoop some rava kesari to it. Level the top.
14. Invert the bowl or mould to a plate. Gently shake off. 
15. Garnish rava kesari with cashews and nuts. 
16. You can also fluff up the rava kesari with a fork to make it fluffy.

1. Add semolina & desiccated coconut to a pan and dry roast it on a medium to low flame stirring constantly for 6 to 7 mins. 
2. It has to be evenly light golden without browning or burning. When it turns aromatic, light and crunchy, turn off the stove. Transfer this to a plate & cool down.
3. To a grinder jar, add sugar and cardamoms. Grind it to a fine powder and rest it in the jar itself for 2 to 3 mins.
4. When the semolina cools down, add it to the same grinder jar. 
5. Grind to a slightly coarse powder. Taste test this. It has to be slightly coarse and not very coarse. If it is too coarse the ladoos will not bind.Transfer this to a mixing bowl.
6. Pour ghee in a hot pan. Add cashews & fry on a medium flame until light golden. 
7. Then add the raisins and stir for 30 seconds. Turn off the heat.
8. Pour this hot ghee along with nuts and raisins to the rava laddu mixture.
9. Stir it with a spoon and not use your hand yet as it is too hot.
10. Once the ghee incorporates well, use your hand and mix everything well.
11. Take small portions of this mixture to your palm and press down hard with your finger to form a ball. (Check video).
12. Form the ladoos while the mixture is still hot. You will be able to make 10 to 11 rava laddus.
13. Store them in an air tight jar at room temperature and use up within a month. 1 cup rava (160 grams, semolina or suji) (refer notes)
¾ cup sugar + 1 tablespoon (165 grams, for less sweet reduce by 1 to 2 tbps)
¼ cup desiccated coconut or copra (25 grams, optional)
¼ cup ghee + (¾ tablespoon) (refer notes)
1 teaspoon cardamom powder (or 5 cardamom pods)
10 raisins
10 cashews (broken) https://www.indianhealthyrecipes.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/rava-laddu-recipe.jpg

1. Mix together yogurt and water in a bowl. Add rava and soak it for 10 minutes. The dough must bind well if it is dry you can sprinkle some water.
2. While the rava soaks, chop onions, chilies, curry leaves and coriander leaves. Grate ginger.
3. After 10 mins, add onions, chilies, leaves, cumin, salt and ginger to the soaked rava and make a dough. Beat the batter very well for 30 seconds to a minute with your hand in clock wise direction. This helps to make the rava vada fluffy. Lastly add soda and mix it gently.
4. The dough must bind well and must be sticky and easily spreadable. If it is dry you can sprinkle some water. If the dough is too stiff then they will turn hard.
5. Heat oil in a deep fry pan. Grease a foil or cling wrap. Divide the dough to 12 portions and make balls. Place them on the foil. Flatten and make a whole in the center.
6. When the oil is just hot enough, test by adding a bit of the dough to the hot oil. The dough has to rise without browning. This is the right temperature.
7. Grease your fingers, transfer the vada to your fingers. Then gently shake off the fingers. Rava vada will drop in the oil. Do not disturb them for a while until they turn firm.
8. Fry until the rava vadas on a medium high flame by stirring often. Drain them on a kitchen tissue when they turn crisp & golden. Fry all the vadas in batches similarly. Serve rava vada with chutney. 1 cup rava or semolina
½ cup yogurt or curd
2 tbsp water or more as needed
¼ cup onions finely chopped 
¾ teaspoon ginger  grated
2 sprigs coriander leaves finely chopped
1 sprig curry leaves finely chopped
2 green chilies
½ tsp cumin or jeera
¼ tsp soda-bi-carbonate or cooking soda

1. Wash urad dal until the water runs clear. Soak it enough water for 2 hours. If blending in a mixer then, soak for 3 hours.
2. Drain the water and add it to a blender jar along with 2 to 3 tbsps water and salt as needed. Do not add lot of water at one time.
3. Blend it to a smooth fluffy batter adding more water as needed. The batter has to be thick like the vada batter.
4. Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well. Beat the batter for 2 to 3 mins.
5. Heat oil in a deep pan. When the oil is hot enough, take small portions of this batter and drop in the oil.
6. Stir and fry until golden. Transfer them to an absorbent tissue.
7. Serve urad dal bonda hot with any chutney. ½ cup urad dal  or minapa pappu (or skinned black gram)
2 to 3 tbsps rice flour
Salt  as needed
1 pinch hing
½ tbsp pepper  crushed
1 to 2 green chilies  chopped
¾ tsp ginger finely chopped  (optional)
4 to 5 curry leaves  chopped finely
coriander leaves Few ,  chopped finely
Oil  as needed for frying

1. Cut the stem of the raw banana and boil till cooked. To check prick the banana with a fork or knife. When the banana is cooked it easily goes in.
2. Cool the banana a bit and then peel off the skin. Cut it to desired sizes.
3. Add oil to a hot pan. Add cumin and mustard when they splutter, add chana dal and urad dal. Fry until golden. Then add curry leaves and ginger. Fry until the raw smell disappears.
4. Add sliced onions, chili. Fry until the onions turn transparent.
5. Add salt and turmeric. Stir well.
6. Add the cubed banana and then fry for about 2 to 3 minutes.
7. Cover and cook on a low flame for 2 to 3 minutes. If the banana is not cooked. Sprinkle some water and cook further.
8. You can mash the banana a bit if you like. Add chopped coriander leaves. Stir well.
9. Serve aratikaya kura with plain rice and rasam or sambar. 2 raw banana large 
1 sprig curry leaves
1 tsp ginger grated  or ginger garlic paste
1/2 tbsp urad dal
3/4 tbsp chana dal
1/2 tsp mustard
1/2 tsp cumin  / jeera
1 pinch hing
1 onions large or 2 medium ,  thinly sliced
1 to 2 green chilies  slit (or red chili powder as needed)
1/8 tsp turmeric
salt  as needed
coriander leaves few 
lemon juice  as needed
1/4 tsp garam masala  (optional)

1. Wash and peel the skin of banana. Halve it vertically. Slice and add them to a bowl of water.
2. In a blender, make a fine paste of ginger, garlic and chillis. keep it aside for later use.
3. To the same jar add onions and coarsely pulse. Set this aside separately.
4. Add oil to a heavy bottom pan and heat it.
5. Add mustard, cumin, and dal.  Fry till the dal turns golden. Then add chili ginger garlic paste. Fry until the ginger garlic turns slightly golden.
6. Add drained raw banana slices to the pan and sprinkle turmeric.
7. On a medium high flame, fry till they are almost cooked. To prevent burning, stir constantly. If needed add little more more
8. Reduce the flame to medium and sprinkle salt. Fry till soft, cooked and tender.
9. Add the crushed chilli onions. Fry on high till the onions begin to caramelize or brown. Stir constantly.
10. Sprinkle gram masala and red chili powder if using. Fry on a low flame till they firm up.
11. Serve raw banana fry hot with rice and rasam or sambar. 3 Raw banana
2 pinches turmeric
¼ tsp mustard
½ tsp Cumin or jeera
1 tsp. Urad dal
2 to 3 Green chilies  or ½ tsp red chilli powder
½ inch ginger 
4 cloves garlic
1 large onion  sliced
1 sprig  curry leaves
½ to ¾  tsp garam masala powder  or as needed
2 tbsp Oil https://www.indianhealthyrecipes.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/raw-banana-fry-recipe.jpg

1. Wash & peel banana. Make sure the inner skin has been removed completely.
2. Cube them and steam in a steamer or pressure cooker until cooked al dente (just cooked). It takes around 10 to 12 mins on a medium heat. You can also boil them in a pot with 2 cups water. 
3. Heat a pan with oil and crackle cumin and mustard.
4. Add hing, curry leaves, onions and green chilies. Saute until the onions turn completely golden. Add ginger garlic paste and fry until the raw smell goes off.
5. Add tomatoes, salt and turmeric. Mix and saute until the tomatoes turn mushy.
6. Add red chili powder, garam masala and coriander powder.
7. Mix and saute for 2 to 3 mins.
8. Pour half cup water to the pan and stir well. Cook until the mixture turns to a thick gravy like. You can add more water if you like a moist curry. I made this to a dry raw banana masala curry.
9. Check the salt and spice now. Add the steamed banana. Stir well. 
10. Cover and cook for 3 to 4 mins on a very low flame. The banana must cook completely but not mushy. We prefer a dry curry, so I evaporate all the water by cooking for 2 to 3 mins more.
11. Add coriander leaves. Switch off.
12. Serve aratikaya masala kura with rice or chapathi. 2 raw banana  (unripe firm)
2 tbsp oil
1 sprig curry leaves
½ tsp mustard
½ tsp cumin
1 pinch asafoetida or hing
1 green chili
1/8 tsp turmeric or haldi
salt as needed
1 cup onions finely chopped or sliced
½ to ¾ cup tomatoes  chopped & mashed (deseeded)
1 ½ tsp ginger garlic paste
1 tsp red chili powder (adjust as needed)
1 tsp garam masala adjust to suit
½ tsp coriander powder
2 tbsp coriander leaves chopped

1. Wash rice several times and soak it in enough water.
2. Pour milk to a rinsed heavy bottom pot. 
3. Bring it to a boil on a medium flame.  Rinsing prevents the milk solids from sticking at the bottom.
4. Add grated jaggery to a pan along with half cup water. Mix well and heat it.
5. Boil on a medium flame until slightly thick and sticky. It doesn't need a string consistency but has to be sticky.
6. Cool this completely before using it.
7. To the boiling milk, add drained rice and stir.
8. Cook the rice till it turns mushy and soft. Stirring once in every few minutes is needed. Mash few grains of cooked rice with a ladle to the side of the hot pot, the rice should get mashed well.
9. Adjust the consistency of the payasam by adding more milk. Let the rice and milk bubble up after adding milk if needed. Mash the rice if you desire.
10. Turn off the stove before adding jaggery.
11. Add cardamom powder. Filter the cooled jaggery syrup to the cooked rice. If using clean jaggery then you can add the gratings now. Stir well until dissolved.
12. Heat ghee in another small pan. Fry cashews till golden, then add raisins. Stir till they swell and pour this to the rice payasam.
13. Set aside the nuts and raisins for garnish if desired.
14. Serve rice payasam warm or cold.

1. Clean dals, coriander seeds and cumin.
2. Heat a pan and regulate the flame to low. 
3. The entire roasting should happen on a low flame which brings out the aroma from each ingredient. 
4. Dry roast chana dal, urad dal, toor dal and red chilies until golden. If you are making this in large quantity then roast each ingredient separately until deep golden.
5. Add coriander seeds and methi seeds. 
6. Saute till the coriander turns crunchy and lightly roasted. By then methi seeds also turn slightly dark & aromatic. 
7. When you begin to smell the methi seeds nice, add curry leaves and stir well until they turn crisp.
8. Then add cumin and saute until it turns crunchy. Turn off the stove. 
9. At the end of this step, you should have deep roasted dal, methi, coriander seeds, crisp red chilies & curry leaves.
10. Add turmeric and hing. Transfer to a wide plate and cool completely.
11. Add these to a blender jar. 
12. Make a fine powder. Cool completely and store in a airtight glass or steel jar.
13. Use sambar powder as needed. It keeps good at room temperature for 3 months.

1. You can skip this step if you have sambar powder ready. To make the powder, heat a pan and dry roast urad dal, chana dal and red chilies on a medium flame until lightly golden. Meanwhile if you see the red chilies turn crisp you can set them aside.
2. Then add coriander seeds and roast till golden. Then quickly add cumin or jeera. When they smell good remove to a plate. Then add methi seeds & roast. When the methi seeds begin to smell good & turn deep golden, turn off the stove.
3. Cool all of these and make a fine powder in blender jar. For this recipe use only half of this powder.
4. Wash rice and dal together in a bowl or directly in the cooker. Then pour 2 cups of water & pressure cook them together on a medium flame. If cooking in a bowl cook for 3 whistles. If cooking in the cooker directly, then cook for 2 whistles. 
5. When the pressure releases naturally remove the rice & dal & slightly mash them.
6. Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin, mustard, red chilli & curry leaves. When they splutter and curry leaves turn crisp, add hing.
7. Next add veggies and saute for 2 to 3 minutes. Saute tomatoes along with turmeric for 3 minutes.
8. Pour 1 cup water and cook the vegetables until soft.
9. Take some hot water from the pan to a bowl and soak tamarind in it.
10. Mash the soaked tamarind when it softens and remove the pulp. You can also filter the tamarind water.
11. Check if the vegetables are cooked especially the drumstick. When the veggies are almost cooked, pour this tamarind water, salt and sambar powder to the boiling veggies. 
12. Cook until it begins to smell good for about 3 to 4 minutes. Next add the mashed rice and dal.
13. Stir well to blend the rice & dal in cooked veggies. Check the salt and spice
14. If needed add more water to bring to consistency. When it begins to bubble turn off the stove.
15. Serve sambar rice hot with papad or pickle.
16. If you prefer you can also do a additional tempering by heating another tbsp of ghee in a small tadka pan. Add a pinch of mustard, 1 broken chilli & curry leaves. When the leaves turn crisp, add hing & pour this to the sambar rice. ¼ cup toor dal plus 2 tbsps  or 6 tbsp (can use little moong dal)
½ cup rice brown rice white rice or millets
2 cups water
1 sprig  curry leaves
1 pinch asafoetida or hing
1½ tbsp ghee or oil as needed
2 pinches turmeric or haldi
8 to 10  Shallots or 1 medium onion cubed
1 drumstick small or half  (cut to 2 inch pieces)
1 carrot  sliced or cubed
1 tomato  medium, chopped
tamarind Small lemon sized 
salt  as needed
½ tsp chana dal or bengal gram
½ tsp urad dal or skinned black gram
1 red chilies

1. Bring water to a boil in a pot on stove or microwave. 
2. Heat a heavy bottom pot or pan with ghee.
3. Next add cashew nuts and fry them till light golden. 
4. Then add raisins and fry until they swell up.  Remove these to a plate.
5. Add semiya to the pan and roast them lightly on a medium flame. 
6. Do not let them brown. If using roasted semiya skip this step of roasting.
7. Pour hot water to the pan and increase the flame till the water begins to boil rapidly.
8. Next add saffron and cardamom powder. 
9. Reduce the flame to medium and cook till the semiya is fully cooked. 
10. If needed you can sprinkle some water if the semiya is under cooked.
11. Add sugar and stir gently. Sugar begins to melt and release moisture. 
12. Cook till all the moisture evaporates and comes to a semi dry consistency.
13. Garnish semiya kesari with nuts and raisins. If desired can add a tsp of ghee.

1. Firstly add 1 tablespoon ghee to a heavy bottom pot and heat up. 
2. Add 12 to 15 cashews and fry till golden. 
3. Then add in 8 to 10 sweet raisins and saute just until they plump up. Remove these to a plate and keep aside for garnish.
4. Next add another tablespoon of ghee and add ¾ cup semiya to the same pan. Roast till slightly golden on a low to medium flame. (skip this step if using pre-roasted semiya)
5. Pour 4 cups milk to the pot. Let the milk boil on a low to medium flame. 
6. Boil till the vermicelli is fully soft cooked. Keep stirring to avoid burning.
7. Add ½ cup sugar. Cook for 3 to 5 mins on a low flame until the semiya payasam becomes thick. 
8. Add ½ teaspoon cardamom powder. Turn off when the it reaches a thick pouring consistency. It will thicken further after cooling.
9. Garnish semiya payasam with fried nuts and raisins. Serve hot or chilled as desired.
10. Find video above the recipe card. Press saute button and add 1 tbsp ghee to the inner pot of the Instant pot.
11. When the ghee melts, add 12 to 15 cashews and fry until golden.
12. Remove them to a plate. If using raisins fry 10 raisins just for 30 seconds and remove to the plate.
13. Add 1 tablespoon ghee (optional) and ¾ cup semiya. Fry until lightly golden stirring often. If using roasted vermicelli then just fry for 30 seconds.
14. Pour 3½ cups milk and add ½ cup sugar.
15. Press cancel and stir well. Close the lid  and then press porridge button.
16. Set the timer to 8 mins and position the steam release handle to sealing.
17. The ip will beep when the semiya payasam is done. Wait for the pressure to release naturally.
18. Add ½ teaspoon cardamom powder and gently stir it. If the payasam is runny you can cook on saute mode for 2 mins.
19. Garnish with cashews and raisins. Serve semiya payasam chilled or warm.

1. If using roasted vermicelli, then skip this step. Dry roast semiya uniformly on a medium flame until lightly golden. Keep stirring and fry without browning them. They will turn light when done. Transfer to a plate.
2. Heat oil in a pan. Add peanuts or cashews. Fry them until golden and crunchy. Remove to a plate. 
3. To the same pan add mustard, cumin, chana dal & urad dal . Fry until the dals turn golden and roasted well. 
4. Next add hing, onions, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves.  Fry for about 2 to 3 minutes until the onions turn transparent.

6. Pour water and add salt. Stir and check by tasting the water. It has to be slightly salty. If needed add more salt. 
7. Bring it to a rapid boil. Transfer roasted semiya to the pan & stir immediately. 
8. Cook on a medium flame till all the water is absorbed by the vermicelli. (If you feel the semiya is uncooked then pour little boiling water.)
9. Cover the pan and cook on a lowest heat 2 minutes. Turn off and rest for another 5 minutes.
10. When the temperature cools down a bit sprinkle some lemon juice & coriander leaves. 
11. Garnish semiya upma with grated coconut (optional), roasted peanuts or cashews. Serve with peanut podi or pickle. 1 cup semiya (vermicelli)

1. wash and soak chana for overnight
2. Rinse them well and add to a pressure cooker along with little salt, turmeric and ¼ cup water
3. Let it whistle 5 to 6 times on a medium flame.
4. When the pressure goes off, drain off any left over water or evaporate it by cooking further on a high flame
5. heat oil in a pan, add mustard cumin. when they begin to splutter add red chili, curry leaves, hing.

1. On a medium to low flame dry roast sesame seeds in a heavy bottom pan stirring often. 
2. When done they will turn aromatic and begin to pop or splutter. 
3. Avoid over roasting as they tend to turn bitter quickly. Remove to a plate and set aside.
4. Take a small bowl with ¼ cup of water and keep it ready aside to check the syrup consistency. 
5. Heat jaggery in the same pan along with 2 tbsps water. 
6. Optional - Once dissolved you can also filter it to another bowl to remove the dust particles. Rinse the pan and pour back the syrup to the pan. 
7. Boil the jaggery syrup on a medium flame stirring often until it reaches a ball consistency.
8. The syrup reduces, turns to deep color & turns frothy. To check add a tsp of the syrup to the bowl of water we prepared earlier.
9. The syrup should stay in there in the bowl without dissolving. Gather the jaggery and make a ball. You should get a soft ball that turns firm upon cooling. It should not be too soft and should not turn to a brittle.
10. If the syrup hasn't reached that consistency yet, continue to cook for few more minutes.
11. When you get the correct ball consistency, turn off the stove.
12. Add cardamom powder and sesame seeds. Mix well.
13. Let the mixture cool down a bit. Then quickly dip your palms in water just to moisten and scoop out 1 tbsp of the mixture to your palm and shape to ladoo.
14. Be quick at this stage and keep dipping your hand in water as needed to avoid burns.
15. Roll the entire mixture to balls when the mixture is still hot.
16. Cool the til ladoos completely and store in air tight jar.
17. Dry roast sesame seeds till you begin to get a nice aroma. Set these aside to cool.
18. Meanwhile dry roast peanuts and cool them. Rub peanuts lightly with the bottom of a glass for the skin to become loose. Remove the skin and keep aside.
19. Grind sesame seeds and jaggery together with cardamom powder to a fine powder
20. Transfer this to a plate, add skinned peanuts and mix.
21. Take small portions and roll them to balls
22. Store sesame seeds ladoo in an air tight jar and handle with moist free hands.

1. Soaking : To make set dosa recipe, firstly add rice to a large bowl and wash very well a few times. Then soak in ample amount of water for about 5 hours. Add urad dal and fenugreek seeds to another bowl and rinse them a few times. Then soak in ample amount of water for about 5 hours. Wash poha just before grinding the batter.
2. Making batter: Drain the water from from both the bowls. Add urad dal, salt, fenugreek seeds and poha to a blender jar along with 1 cup water. Blend them till bubbly. If needed add more water to grind the batter smooth & frothy. Do not add too much water, batter should not be very runny.
3. Transfer the batter to a large batter bowl. Add rice to the jar along with 1/4 cup water. Grind to a smooth batter. Pour this to the urad dal batter. Mix everything well till well combined.
4. Fermenting : Set aside in a warm place for 8 to 12 hours for the batter to ferment and rise well.
5. Add few drops of oil to a tawa. Using a tissue or cut onion spread the oil very well. Heat the tawa. Mix the batter gently.
6. Pour one ladle full of batter and dab it gently to spread the batter do not spread like a normal dosa. Add oil across the edges.
7. Cover and cook for a while until it is cooked inside. You can flip and cook it for a minute on the inner side as well.
8. To get a crispy set dosa, lower the flame and cook for a while. Sprinkle idli podi if you have it or serve hot with chutney. Repeat making more set dosa on the tawa. 2 cups raw rice or parboiled rice (like idli rice or masoori or any rice)
1 cup poha medium attukulu or avalakki
½ cup urad dal  or skinned black gram
1 ½ teaspoons fenugreek seeds or menthulu or methi
salt as needed non iodised 
oil or butter  as needed

1. If making plain sev, skip this step. For flavoring, add ajwain powder to half cup boiling hot water. Cover and keep aside for 5 to 10 minutes. Filter the water and use for kneading the dough. If you like green chili or garlic flavour, blend 3 garlic cloves or 3 green chilies and add to cold water. Strain and use only as needed.
2. To a large bowl, add gram flour, rice flour, salt, chili powder, turmeric and hing. Mix well.
3. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a kadai until hot. Pour this to the flour.
4. Using a spoon mix it well. Then use your hand to incorporate the oil well to the flour. Rub the flour with your palms for a while to incorporate the oil evenly. Break up any lumps of flour and oil.
5. Add water only as required and make a non sticky dough. You can use plain water if you don't prefer the spiced water.
6. Heat oil in a deep frying pan on a medium flame. 
7. Meanwhile grease the sev maker/ mould with little oil using a brush. Fill the dough in the mould. Fit the plate with the smallest holes to your sev maker.
8. Fill ⅓ of the prepared dough or as much to fill your sev maker. 
9. Check if the oil is hot enough by dropping a small portion of dough. The oil is ready when the  dough rises without browning. 
10. Regulate the flame to medium. Press the mould gently over the hot oil in circular motion to release the dough in circular discs. 
11. If you are a beginner, then grease a perforated ladle with little oil. Squeeze the dough on to the ladle and keep the ladle in the oil. Within a few minutes the sev will release on its own to to hot oil.
12. Fry the omapodi until crisp and golden. Remove them to a colander or kitchen tissue.
13. To make the next batch of sev, ensure the oil is medium hot and not too hot. If the oil is too hot they will burn. If the oil is not hot enough they will soak up the oil.
14. Cool all of the sev and transfer to air tight jars. I usually break them and store in separate containers so they remain crisp and fresh for longer.
15. Serve sev as a tea time snack or garnish your chaat snacks with it. 2 cups besan (fine gram flour)
½ cup rice flour (fine flour, 2 tbsp extra for extra crisp)
1 tablespoon oil (hot)
¼ teaspoon turmeric (optional)

¾ tablespoon ajwain

1. Add sugar, ghee and water to a pot.
2. Heat them until sugar dissolves completely. Cool this down for sometime.
3. The syrup must be slightly hot and not completely cold. 
4. In a mixing bowl, mix together flour, salt and cardamom powder along with hot syrup. 
5. Bring the flour together and make a stiff dough. If the sugar syrup is not enough and the dough looks dry, then sprinkle some water. The dough should not be sticky.
6. Knead well until the dough turns soft. Divide the dough to 4 balls and roll them in your palms to smoothen. Keep them covered in a bowl.
7. Grease a rolling board and flatten a dough ball.
8. Begin to roll to a 6 to 7 inch roti which is neither too thick nor too thin.
9. Make cuts with ¾ to 1 inch apart vertically. Then repeat horizontally to get sweet diamond cuts. (refer pictures below)
10. Separate the shankarpali and transfer to a plate.
11. Heat oil in a kadai on a medium heat.  While the oil heats, keep rolling the dough and making more shankarpali.
12. Check if the oil is hot by gently sliding a small piece of dough. It should rise slowly without browning. This is the right temperature.
13. When it is hot enough gently slide them one by one to the hot oil. Do not crowd a lot of them in the pan. 
14. Ensure the flame is medium to medium high and not low. Keep stirring & fry until golden & crisp. Remove to a colander.
15. Repeat frying the next batches.

1. Bring 2 cups water to a boil. Pour half of the water to another small bowl. Soak almonds, pistachios and cashews in one bowl. Soak chironji seeds in another bowl.
2. After 30 mins, drain the hot water and pour cold water in both the bowls.
3. Meanwhile chop the dates to bite sized pieces and set aside.
4. Drain the water completely and peel the almonds and pistachios. Discard the skin and soak them in fresh room temperature water for at least 1 to 2 hours.
5. Drain the water from the chironji seeds and transfer them to a clean cloth. Pat them dry and rub gently. The skin begins to peel off.  Discard the skin and any brown seeds that seem to be rancid. Keep the seeds in a small bowl and set aside.
6. When the nuts are soaked well after 1 to 2 hours, chop them very finely. Keep them aside. Ensure the nuts are dry before frying them.
7. Fine vermicelli is usually long and not broken. You will need to break them a bit and measure 1 cup (50 grams) and keep aside.
8. Heat 2 tbsps ghee in a heavy bottom pot. Fry cashews and almonds in hot ghee for about 1 to 2 mins. 
9. Then add pistachios and chironji seeds. Fry all of them until crisp and golden. This takes about 5 to 6 mins as the nuts are soaked. When done, remove to a plate.
10. To the same pot, add dates and fry until they begin to smell good. Remove to a plate.

15. Add cardamom powder & sugar or condensed milk (optional).  If using mawa (optional) add it now. 
16. Simmer for a few more minutes until slightly thick yet runny. Sheer khurma will thicken upon cooling so turn off when it is of runny consistency. Add cardamom powder & rose water (optional).
17. Serve warm or chilled. Garnish with fried nuts, chironji seeds and dates. 4 cups milk (whole milk/ full fat)

2. Traditionally only fresh neem flowers are used to make ugadi pachadi. But if you live in a place where you don't get fresh flowers then use the dried ones.
3. While the tamarind soaks,  pluck the flowers from neem sprigs. Or alternate quick method: add the neem sprigs to a thin cloth, bring the edges of the cloth together so that they don’t fall off from the cloth. 
4. Hold the edges tightly and hit the cloth on to the kitchen counter several times. Neem flower or petals get separated from the sprigs and fall of in the cloth, collect them and set aside.

1. Wash fish and drain it.
2. Add all the marination ingredients to a bowl and marinate the fish.
3. Heat a pan with oil or ghee. Fry curry leaves until they turn crisp.
4. Add the fish to the pan.
5. On a very low flame, cover and cook for 2 to 3 mins. Flip to the other side carefully. Cook covered again for 2 to 3 mins.

1. Steam or boil veggies as desired. They must be just cooked without getting mushy.
2. Heat a pan with oil and saute mustard, cumin and dal.
3. When the dal turns golded, saute ginger and then add onions, chilies, cashews and curry leaves.
4. Saute until the onions turn golde, add all the spice powders along with salt. Stir and fry for a minute.
5. Add all the veggies and mash them lightly. Saute for 2 mins. Add coriander leaves and lemon juice. Mix and switch off.

7. Mix together flours, salt, chilii powder, turmeric along with water to make a thick batter.
8. Heat oil in a kadai for frying. Check whether the oil is hot enough by dropping a small amount of the batter in oil. The batter must rise slowly and not quickly. If you see the batter sinks, wait for a while and repeat the test. If the batter rises quickly and then turns brown quickly it means the oil is very hot. Allow to cool down a bit.
9. Dip each ball in the batter and coat it well. lift it using a table spoon, swipe off the excess batter and drop in the hot oil. Wait for a minute and stir consistently until they are fried to golden.
10. You make fry 3 to 4 balls in each batch, make sure there is enough space in the kadai to fry them well.

1. Steam or boil veggies until just fork tender. 
2. I pressure cooked all the veggies together for 2 whistles on a medium heat with half cup water. 
3. You can also steam them in a steamer or cooker until tender and soft. Do not make them mushy.
4. Drain any excess moisture if left and use up in your soups.
5. If you do not have bread crumbs, just add some poha to a mixer jar and make a fine powder.
6. Add the boiled vegetables to a mixing bowl and mash them well. 
7. Next add bread crumbs or powdered poha, salt, grated ginger, garam masala and chilies as well to the veggies.
8. Mix everything well to make a non sticky dough. If needed, add more bread crumbs or powdered poha to make it non sticky.
9. Divide the cutlet dough to 13 to 14 parts. Roll the dough to balls.
10. Then flatten them gently and make thick patties. Set aside the veg cutlets aside in a plate. 
11. In another plate add ¼ cup bread crumbs or powdered poha for the crust. Set this aside.
12. Add besan or rice flour to another small mixing bowl. Pour water just enough to make a slightly thin batter. 
13. If you want a thick crust over your cutlets then make a slightly thicker batter.
14. Arrange all the 3 - Cutlets plate, batter bowl & bread crumbs plate side by side. 
15. Next dip each vegetable cutlet in the batter on both the sides. 
16. Then Place them on the bread crumbs. Gently coat them with the crumbs all over.
17. Place them back on a plate aside for 5 to 10 minutes.  
18. Repeat the same steps of dipping them in the batter and then the crumbs for all the veg cutlets.
19. Just before frying, gently shake them off in the plate to remove the excess crumbs.
20. Lastly heat 1 tablespoon oil for shallow frying in a wide pan. When the oil turns hot, gently place the veg cutlet in the pan. 
21. Fry them on both the sides until golden and crisp. Set aside and fry them in 2 batches using oil as needed.
22. Bake for about 15 mins on each side or until golden and crisp.
23. To bake the veg cutlet - Preheat the oven to 180 C for 15 mins and place the patties on a greased tray.

instructions:

3. Add ginger garlic paste and fry till the raw smell goes off.
4. Add parboiled potatoes and the rest of vegetables. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
5. Add turmeric, masala powder and red chili powder. Mix and fry well for 2 minutes till you begin to get an aroma.

1. Dry roast urad dal and chana dal until golden. Switch off the stove and add sesame seeds , cumin and coconut. Toss them till the sesame seeds splutter. Cool this and powder. You can also use idli podi instead of making this.

8. Add the spice powder and red chili powder.
9. Mix everything well and fry for just a minute.

instructions:
1. Wash chicken thoroughly and drain completely.
2. Powder fennel, cinnamon, cloves and cardamoms to a fine powder in a mixer jar. Then add ginger garlic. Make a fine paste of all. If your blender doesn't do it finely, then add curd mentioned for marination and blend. You can also use a hand pestle to do this.
3. Add the paste, curd, turmeric, chili powder and chicken to a mixing bowl. Marinate and set aside.
4. Wash and soak rice for at least 20 to 30 mins. Drain the water.
5. Keep your coconut milk and water ready.
6. Add oil to a hot pot or pressure cooker.
7. Saute bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon.
8. Add onions and green chilies. Fry until they turn golden.
9. Add chicken and saute on a medium heat until the chicken turns pale and whitish.
10. Then add tomatoes, mint and coriander leaves. Sprinkle salt and cook covered on a low heat untl the tomatoes turn mushy. Chicken is almost half cooked at this stage. Do not cook on high heat as it will make the chicken hard. Cook without lid until the moisture from tomatoes and curd evaporates completely.
11. Add water and coconut milk. Bring it to a boil on a medium heat . You can also use hot water to prevent the chicken from turning hard. Some times adding cold water to the chicken makes it hard and tough to cook.
12. Add drained rice and cook on a medium heat.
13. If making in pressure cooker. cover and cook on a medium heat for 1 whistle.
14. If making in pot, Cook in open pot until almost the water is absorbed. Then cover and cook on a low heat until soft cooked. If the rice remains undercooked, you may need to sprinkle some water and cook until done.
15. Allow the cooked chicken biryani to rest for atleast 15 mins.
16. Open the lid and fluff up gently.

1. Wash the raw banana under running water and peel the skin. Cut off the ends and discard.
2. Rinse the banana well. Slice them to equal sizes. Do not slice them too thick or too thin.
3. Keep them in water until used to prevent browning.
4. Heat a wide pan with oil.
5. Add mustard, cumin, red chili and urad dal.
6. When the dal turns slightly golden, add the curry leaves and hing.
7. Lower the flame completely and wait until the leaves turn crisp.
8. Then add in chili powder, turmeric and sambar powder.

1. Grease a tray and set side.

1. Add ghee to a pan and heat it. Add coconut and jaggery. Mix well and cook on a medium heat.

6. Continue to cook on a medium heat stirring often until the mixture comes together. The mixture turns gooey and then turns thick. At this stage it begins to leave the pan. Do not overcook otherwise the mixture discolors and turns to brown.

9. Divide the mixture to 10 balls.

11. Cover the coconut lado with the kova / khoya.
12. Gently smoothen the ladoo. Do not press or put pressure on the ball.
13. Follow the same procedure to complete all the ladoos.
14. Allow them to dry for 2 to 4 hours.
15. Store kova ladoo in a air tight jar and serve with in 3 days or refrigerate and use up to 2 weeks.

1. Mix together flour, salt, rava and oil in a large mixing bowl. 
2. Pour ¼ cup water. Begin to make a little stiff & tight dough, adding more water as needed. (check video)
3. Smear ½ tsp oil, knead lightly and smoothen the ball.
4. Do not knead it a lot otherwise poori will turn soft and absorb oil while frying. 
5. Keep the dough covered all the time until the last poori is rolled. Do not rest the dough for more than 3 to 5 minutes. The longer it rests quicker the puffed puri will collapse. They will turn oily after frying.
6. Divide the dough to 8 to 10 portions. Avoid kneading them. 
7. Smoothen all the balls by rolling them lightly in between your palms. Keep them covered in the bowl. 
8. Drizzle a few drops of oil on the rolling area and spread it. 
9. Smear oil over the dough ball & flatten it.
10. Begin to roll it evenly from the center to a round puri.
11.  It should not be too thick or thin. It must be moderately thick which helps the puri to puff.
12. Make 5 to 6 puris and set them aside. Do not stack them.
13. Begin to heat the oil on a medium high flame and continue to make rest of the pooris.
14. The oil has to be hot enough. Check by dropping a small portion of dough to the pan. It has to rise immediately without browning. 
15. If it browns quickly then reduce the flame slightly and allow the temperature to come down.
16. Slide the puri carefully to the hot oil. Do not disturb until it rises half way to the surface.
17. Quickly but gently begin to press down with a perforated ladle. This helps the poori to puff well.
18. Once puri puffs, flip it carefully. Fry on the other side as well until golden and crisp. 
19. You can fry flipping too and fro once more until slightly crisp & to get the desired color - light golden to dark golden.
20. Remove the puri to a steel colander. Fry the next poori the same way. 
21. Make sure the oil is hot enough, but not smoking before frying the next puri. Serve poori with potato curry, chutney or kurma. 1 cup wheat flour (atta)

1. Wash the lentils in a large bowl at least thrice. Drain the water and add fresh water. Soak for at least 4 hrs. You can also soak it overnight.

1. Wash amlas under running water and drain water completely.
2. Dry them on a clean cloth to keep them moisture free.
3. Boil 3 cups of water until it comes to a rolling boil. Turn off the heat and cool completely.
4. Deseed the tamarind and remove the fibers and shells if any.
5. Spread tamarind on a wide plate and sun dry for at least 2 hours just to ensure it is moisture free.

8. Keep the garlic flakes in the sun for sometime just to ensure they are moisture free.

23. Transfer this to the garlic and mix both of them.
24. Blend this mixture to a smooth paste.

2. Pour enough water and soak them for 2 to 3 hours. 
3. You can also leave them overnight for 8 hours.
4. Add rice to another large pot and wash 3 times. 
5. Same this one too you can leave the rice overnight for 8 hours.
6. Next add red chilies to the rice and soak them for 2 to 3 hours. 
7. Drain the water from both the pots.
8. Add rice and red chilies to a blender jar along with little water. Blend to a slightly coarse paste or thick batter.
9. Transfer the batter to a pot.
10. Add dals, jeera and ginger to the jar. Also add little water and blend to a slightly coarse thick batter.
11. Mix this with the rice batter. Allow to rest for 2 to 4 hours. You can also skip resting.
12. Heat a pan. Add few drops of oil and smear it all over the pan with a tissue.
13. While the pan heats, add chopped onions, salt, hing, coriander leaves to the batter.
14. Mix everything well.
15. If you prefer to make thick adai, the consistency of the batter must be thick but of spreading consistency.
16. If you prefer thin adai, then add more water as needed. 
17. Mix well to bring the consistency to a slightly less thick batter, not runny. 
18. The batter must be easily spreadable on the pan.
19. Regulate the flame to medium. Make sure the pan is hot.
20. Pour one ladle of batter and spread it quickly like a dosa. Spread it to thick or thin adai as per your liking.
21. Add 1/2 tsp oil or ghee across the edges. Cook on a medium heat.
22. When it gets cooked on one side, the edges loosen from the pan slightly. Flip it and cook on the other side as well. Make sure it is cooked on both the sides until crisp.

1. Pour 1 tbsp ghee to a small tray and grease it well for setting the mysore pak. Set this aside.
2. Place a sieve over a large bowl. Measure and add besan to the sieve. 
3. Next sieve it well twice. Divide the flour to 3  parts and transfer them to small bowls. Set this aside.
4. On one burner of the stove place a kadai and pour ghee and oil. Begin to heat it on a low to medium heat.
5. On another burner, place a wide deep pan. Pour the sugar and water. Begin to heat it.
6. Boil the sugar syrup stirring often until it reaches a one string consistency.
7. To check one string consistency of the syrup, take a small portion of the syrup in between the thumb and index finger. Move the fingers apart. You must be able to see a single string in between the fingers.
8. Ensure the oil and ghee are turning hot. 
9. Add 1/3 rd portion of flour to the bubbling sugar syrup. Flame must be medium and the sugar syrup bubbling well otherwise mysore pak turns flat. Stir well until all the flour blends well with the syrup.
10. Then add the next 1/3 rd portion of flour. Repeat adding the last part too following the same process.
11. At this stage there must be no lumps & the flour must blend well with the sugar syrup.
12. Next add in 1 ladle full of hot ghee & oil to the pan. Then immediately  oil and ghee must sizzle, meaning it is hot enough. Make sure the ghee is really very hot otherwise increase the flame of burner 1 to keep ghee & oil consistently hot. Immediately stir well until all the ghee has been absorbed.
13. Repeat adding the ghee in parts & repeat stirring until the ghee is well absorbed every time.
14. As the ghee is added every time it has to sizzle. Then stir well until absorbed. If you do not have enough ghee left in the kadai, then pour 2 tbsp more each of oil and ghee. Then heat it quickly. I did not use any excess.
15. Quickly pour some hot ghee and stir. Do not add a lot at as it will leave out the excess.
16. When the mysore pak is about to finish,  the mixture will turn very thick with lot of pores or bubbles. Do not add any more ghee at this stage otherwise it will ooze out the excess. The mixture will leave the pan completely within few seconds.
17. Be very very quick and transfer to a greased pan. Level the top with the help of a greased spoon. Keep this aside for 10 to 15 mins. Invert it on a board. Cut to desired sized pieces.
18. Cool mysore pak completely. Store in a air tight jar at room temperature 1 cup besan or gram flour

1. If using basmati rice, wash it and soak for atleast 30 mins and drain it.
2. Bring 6 to 8 cups of water to a rapid boil. Add spices, oil and salt. Cook the rice till al dente and drain it to a colander.
3. If using jeerakasala rice, then just wash and drain the water.
4. Add ghee to a hot pot and saute the spices for a while. Add drained rice and saute for 2 to 3 mins.
5. Add salt and hot water (3½ cups) to the rice and cook until al dente cooked.
6. Powder all the spices to make kerala garam masala. You can skip this step if you have ready kerala garam masala.
7. Heat ghee or oil and saute star anise, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom.
8. Add onions and fry until golden.
9. Saute ginger garlic until the raw smell goes away.
10. Then add tomatoes and salt.
11. Cook until the tomatoes turn mushy.
12. Add red chili powder, garam masala and turmeric.
13. Mix and cook just for a minute or 2.
14. Add eggs and saute with the masala for 2 mins.
15. Pour coconut milk and stir. Check the salt and spice. Adjust if needed. Egg biryani gravy is ready.
16. Lower the flame completely. Add coriander leaves and then spread rice.
17. Add ghee and coriander or mint leaves over the rice.
18. Cover the biryani pot with a tight lid. You can also use foil or moist cloth to trap the dum or steam. You can also use a plate and then place something heavy over it.
19. Cook for 10 mins on the lowest, very low flame. If your stove doesn't have a small burner, then heat up a old pan/ tawa and place the biryani pot over that. Cook for 10 mins.
20. Rest for 10 more minutes. Squeeze in some lemon juice before serving.

instructions:
1. Wash and drain jowar. Air dry them by spreading on a cloth for about 30 mins or until they dry completely (no dripping water).
2. To a dry heavy bottom pot, add some jowar and spread them across to a thin layer. Do not crowd them. You can add as much as possible but there must be enough space for them to pop well.
3. Cover with a loose fitting lid leaving a small vent allowing the steam to escape.
4. Put on the flame to medium high. Do regulate the flame as needed. With in few minutes, they will begin to pop. Do not do them on a very high or very low flame.
5. Once they stop popping, switch off and set them aside.
6. Allow the jowar puffs to cool completely.
7. Add oil to a wide mixing pan, heat the oil slightly and switch off. If you like to have some roasted peanuts in this, fry them in the same pan until golden. You can also add some chopped garlic and curry leaves if you like.
8. Add salt, chili powder and turmeric. Cool the ingredients in the pan, add the jowar puffs and mix.
9. Cool completely and store spiced jowar pops in a air tight jar. Keeps good for 2 to 3 weeks. 250 grams Jowar / sorghum/ Jonnalu of good quality

1. Heat ghee in a pot, fry cashews until golden. Set them aside.
2. Add oats and saute on a low to medium flame until well roasted and slightly change the color. This reduces the stickiness.
3. Next pour milk and cook until the kheer becomes thick. Stir often.
4. If needed you can add more milk to bring it to consistency.
5. Add cardamom powder and sugar. If using jaggery first turn off the heat &  add it. You can also make a jaggery syrup and cool completely before adding to the oats kheer.
6. Mix and cook for few more mins.
7. Add some more ghee and turn off the stove.
8. Transfer oats payasam to a serving bowl and garnish with nuts and few drops of ghee.
9. Serve oats kheer hot or warm.

1. Measure all the ingredients and keep them ready.
2. Add besan to a large mixing bowl and pour water just as needed to make a free flowing batter that is not too thin or too thick. Please check the step by step photos to understand the consistency.
3. Heat up the ghee or oil in a kadai until hot enough.
4. Pour little batter over the boondi ladle to check if the consistency is right. You must get them right in round shape. More details in the step by step photos below.
5. Pour one large ladle of batter over the boondi jhara and spread the batter continuously to drop the batter in the shape of boondi.
6. Stir and fry just until the bubbles begin to reduce.
7. Do not fry the boondi till crunchy but fry them just until the raw smell goes away. 
8. Drain them to a large bowl.
9. Continue to make more boondi in batches until all the batter finishes.
10. In the same ghee or oil, fry cashews until light golden, then add raisins. 
11. When they plump up remove them to the boondi bowl. if using rock sugar add it to the bowl now.
12. Add sugar and water to a pot. Boil until 1 string consistency. Turn off the stove.
13. Next add cloves, cardamom powder and edible camphor. Mix well.
14. Add boondi, cashews and raisins.
15. Mix well and set aside until the sugar syrup is absorbed completely. 
16. This may take about 5 to 10 mins. But keep checking.
17. Take small portions of this mixture and make ladoos.

1. Wash black gram a few times and soak in lot of water for 4 to 5 hours. Drain it in a colander.
2. Make a fine powder of cumin and pepper along with salt.
3. Add dal and blend without water. Then sprinkle 2 to 3 tbsps water and blend to a coarse paste.

6. Divide the dough to 12 equal parts and shape them to balls.

1. Chop onion, chilies, coriander leaves and capsicum. Rinse a bowl and break the egg to it. Discard the shell. Beat the egg until frothy. Add the chopped onions, chilies, coriander and capsicum. Add salt and turmeric. Beat the mixture once more.

1. Dry roast peanuts until they begin to smell good and turn light brown. 
2. Add sesame seeds and allow them to splutter. Switch off the heat and add coconut. 
3. Saute it in the hot pan till the coconut smells good. 
4. Cool these and blend with little water to a coarse or smooth paste as desired. Set aside.
5. Heat oil in a pan, brinjals can be deep fried or shallow fried. 
6. While the oil heats up, partially slit to 8 sections, leaving the stem intact. 
7. When the oil turns hot fry them until the skin looks wilted completely, meaning the brinjal is almost cooked. Set these aside.

1. Add rava, rice flour, all-purpose flour, salt, ginger, green chilies, coriander leaves, curry leaves to a bowl.
2. Next add cumin, crushed pepper, onions and yogurt.
3. Pour 2½ cups water and begin to make the batter. Add more water and bring it to a runny consistency. 
4. Taste the batter and add more salt if needed. Rest the batter for 20 mins.
5. Heat dosa pan on a medium high heat. If using cast iron pan, then drizzle few drops of oil over the pan and spread it well with a sliced onion or kitchen tissue or cloth. Wipe off the excess oil & let it heat.
6. While the pan heats, stir the batter well. Ensure it is very runny and is pourable. At this stage you can add more water to bring to the desired consistency.
7. When the pan is hot enough, stir the batter very well and begin to pour it from the edges across the pan in a circular motion. 
8. Then fill up the gaps if any by pouring more batter.
9. Reduce the flame to low. Pour 1 tsp oil across the edges and a little over the rava dosa.
10. When it is done cooking, it will begin to peel off the edges on its own. Do not pull the dosas forcibly.

13. Optionally If the rava dosa has browned at the bottom but still moist on top, then you can also flip and toast the dosa on the other side. And back again.

1. Soak rice in water overnight, next morning change the water and soak again. Do that two more times - 8 hours each. This will ensure the final batter is soft not gritty
2. Then wash and drain the rice. Dry the rice in the sun until crisp
3. Next, send to the flour mill to grind into rice flour. (make sure no other flour is mixed in with this) 
4. Combine rice flour, jaggery, salt, and enough water to make a thick pouring consistency similar to chitaps or pan rolls.
5. Strain thru a sieve and divide into different bowls to make different colors.
6. Soak the rice overnight - wash and drain well in the moring. 
7. Blend to a smooth paste with a little water in the mixer (if the rice is not soaked long enough the mixer will be grainy, so soak longer than you think you need, and use less water when grinding) 
8. Combine with the jaggery and strain thru a sieve
9. To make the paprees you will need a few stainless plates, a steamer with water and another bowl with cold water ready
10. Tip - stainless steel plates are easier to work with. Do not use ceramic. Coated tin plates tend to get ruined when dried, this is due to the heat/coolling in the steaming process
11. Pour a few tablespoons of batter on the back of the plate. 
12. Tip - The final fried paprees become almost twice their size so don't make large ones. (otherwise you will need a big wide pot of oil) 
13. Swirl the plate to help spread the batter into a thin sheet
14. Place the plate in the steamer and steam for 3 minutes until opaque or no longer wet
15. Remove from the steamer and dip the plate into cold water. Use a small knife to loosen the edges of the papree. 
16. Then carefully peel it off the plate. This needs to be done patiently and delicately to prevent them from tearing 
17. Tip- A little ice in the water makes them easier to peel
18. Place them on clean kitchen cloths, or cheesecloths to dry. Traditionally, these were dried in the sun for a few days (they can also be dried under the fan) 
19. Tip - These get stuck to the cloth so try not to move them. Once dried they will release easily 
20. Once dried the paprees must be stored in airtight containers. 
21. These are then deep-fried in oil for 30 seconds, turning once.
22. These are made with rice so are supposed to be pale white in color (or the colors you made) Don't expect them to be golden when frying.

dish_name: Wedding Rice - Fruit and Nut Rice
instructions:
1. Clean, rinse and soak rice in water for 30 mins
2. In a saute pan heat oil and butter.ghee.
3. Saute the whole spices for a minute.
4. Add the nuts and fruits – saute for two minutes until lightly toasted
5. Then add in the onions – saute a minute or two until onions are golden brown
6. Remove some onions, fruit, and nuts for garnish.
7. Drain the rice and add it to the pan.
8. Saute for about 2 to 3 minutes until the rice is lightly toasted
9. Add 3 /12 cups water and let come to a boil.
10. Cover the pan and lower the heat to low.
11. Cook on a low simmer for 20 minutes – set the timer for 20 minutes
12. When the timer sets off – switch the flame off. But do not open the pan.
13. Let the rice continue to cook in the residue heat for 10 more minutes.
14. After 10 minutes - fluff with a fork
15. Serve garnished with brown onions, and sliced boiled eggs 2 cups Rice 
4 tbsp Ghee 
2 tbsp Oil 
½ cup Cashew nuts 
½ cup Raisins 
2 cup Onion 
3 ½ cups Water 
¼ cup Cilantro 
2 inch Cinnamon stick 
3  Cloves 
2  Bay leaves 
2  Hard-boiled eggs

instructions:
1. Grease, flour, and line an 8-inch baking pan with greaseproof paper
2. Combine the flour, with baking powder, salt, finely chopped cashews. Make sure to separate the date pieces.  - set aside.
3. Add 2 tbsp flour to the dates - set aside. Tips - adding the dates to the flour will prevent the dates from sinking to the bottom. 
4. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy
5. Add the beaten egg yolks - combine well with a whisk
6. Then add the vanilla extract
7. Add the semolina - combine well - Set aside for 2 hours. Tip - resting the batter with the semolina will give the cake a soft texture. 
8. After two hours - preheat the oven at 170 C/ 430 F
9. Add the flour mixture to the batter - the batter will be stiff at this time. It's ok 
10. In a separate bowl whip the eggs whites until almost stiff peaks.
11. Fold the egg whites into the cake batter.  Do not over mix Tip - overmixing will cause the eggs to deflate.
12. Finally, add the dates - combine well but do not over mix.Tip - overmixing will cause the dates to sink at the bottom
13. Pour into the prepared baking pan.
14. Bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the center comes clean
15. When baked let cool in the pan for 10 minutes then invert onto a coollng rack and cool completely.tip - taking it off the pan and cooling on the rack will prevent the cake getting soggy.

1. Separate eggs - make sure there are no yolks in the white. If you have any yolk in the whites it will not whip. Tip -It's ok to add the egg white to the yolk but not the yolk to the white
2. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy
3. Add beaten egg yolks - a little at a time
4. Add the vanilla  and almond extract
5. Add the sujee and combine well
6. Cover the bowl and leave the mixture at room temperature for 6 hours or overnight (no more than 8 hours) 
7. Preheat the oven at 160 C/ 320 F 
8. Butter, flour, and line an 8-inch round or square pan with parchment paper - Set aside 
9. The next morning, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, spices, and salt.
10. Add the flour mixture - a little at a time.
11. In a clean grease-free bowl, whip the egg whites until almost stiff peaks. Tip- egg whites will whip well if they are room temperature or warm, not cold.
12. Carefully fold the whipped egg whites into the cake batter. 
13. Finally, add the mixed fruits, plums, and nuts in two batches - do not over mix (or the cake won't rise)
14. Level the top of the cake with a spatula
15. Sprinkle more chopped cashew nuts on the top of the cake
16. Bake in the preheated oven for about 40 to 50 minutes or until the skewer inserted in the center comes clean.
17. Remove from the oven at cool in the pan for 10 minutes 
18. Then invert onto a cooling rack and cool completely Tip- inverting on a cooling rack will prevent the cake from getting soggy 500  grams Butter

1. Preheat the oven at 160 C/ 320 F 
2. Grease and dust 4x9-inch thali
3. Separate the egg whites and egg yolks
4. Cream the white butter with sugar until light and fluffy
5. Add the egg yolks one at a time - Combine well. 
6. Add the semilina (rawa) 
7. Followed by the ground almonds and ground coconut.
8. Add the rose extract
9. Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks 
10. Fold the egg whites into the batter
11. Divide the batter between the prepared baking thalis and bake for about 15 to 20 minutes
12. Cool completely 
13. This thali sweet will keep fresh for 2 days at room temperature or 4 days in the fridge.

1. Grease a 9 x 9-inch square baking pan with butter - set aside
2. Soak the dal for 2 hours then boil until tender and can be squished easily between your fingers
3. Put the dal in a food processor and blend until smooth
4. Combine the ground dal, sugar, rosewater, and nuts into a heavy bottom saucepan
5. Cook on medium heat until all the sugar dissolves 
6. Reduce heat and continue to cook on medium-low until the mixture becomes thick and starts to leave the side of the pan. 
7. Pour the mixture into the greased baking pan - let cool slightly 
8. While still warm cut into diamond shapes. 
9. Let cool completely before you transfer to an air tight container

1. Lightly oil a 7-inch square pan - set aside
2. Soak the gelatin in water for 5 minutes 
3. In a saucepan combine juice, sugar, and soaked gelatin mixture 
4. Stir on medium heat until the sugar and gelatin are dissolved.
5. Bring to a slow simmer and let simmer for 5 minutes.
6. You will know when it's done - when you lift some on a spoon it will pour into threads and makes small triangles on the edge of the spoon 
7. Add flavoring and color 
8. Remove from the pan and let rest for 15 minutes. This will cool the scum on the top. 
9. Remove the scum from the top so you have a clear jelly mixture at the bottom. 
10. You can now pour this into your prepared oiled baking pan. If the mixture has cooled too much just warm it gently until it is pouring consistency again. 
11. Leave the jelly to set overnight or at least 8 hours at room temperature
12. Then carefully remove the slab from the pan onto a sugar-dusted surface.
13. Oil the blade of your knife and cut into strips then each strip into squares. 
14. Dust each piece of jujube with castor sugar. 
15. These will stay at room temperature for a few days

1. Grease a stainless steel plate with ghee or butter and set it aside
2. In a heavy bottom saucepan and wooden spoon or spatula - combine condensed milk, sugar, and cashew nut powder 
3. Place it on medium-low heat - stir cooking continuously.
4. When the mixture is thick and all the sugar has dissolved add the butter  (15 - 20 minutes)
5. The butter will help the mixture leave the sides of the pan easily. Continue stirring for 5 more minutes 
6. Lastly, add the vanilla - combine well. 
7. Take it off the heat and pour it into the prepared greased plate. The mixture is hot do not touch with your hands.
8. Using the same wooden spoon keep mixing (not stirring) the mixture - use a folding motion - fold the bottom to the top - this will help cool faster as well as prevent any crust. 
9. Cover with a cling wrap - and let cool for 15 minutes 
10. Then roll into small balls and fill in the milk cream molds. 
11. You can also cut spread the mixture in a greased 8 x 8-inch square baking pan and cut into squares for a milk fudge.

1. Preheat the oven at 170 C/ 340 F 
2. Grease and line with parchment paper (or dust with flour) one 8-inch round (20 cm) baking pan
3. Cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
4. Add the eggs one at a time
5. gradually add the semolina (sooji/rawa)  along with the coconut milk. 
6. Lastly, add the ground coconut and mix thoroughly
7. Finally, add the vanilla and other extracts.
8. Pour into the prepared baking tray 
9. Bake in a preheated oven for 45 to 50 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the center comes clean
10. Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes then invert on a cooling rack to cool further.
11. When cooled dust with powdered sugar (optional)

1. Generously butter a 9 x 9 square baking pan - set aside
2. Grind the fresh coconut with the rosewater until smooth - set aside
3. In a large saucepan, heat the sugar and water over medium heat - cook until all the sugar has dissolved and you have a thick syrup consistency. 
4. Next, add the ground coconut and ground cashew nuts to the sugar syrup and continue to stir over medium-low heat 
5. Continue to cook until the mixture become thick and start to leave the side of the pan. 
6. Add the food color and ghee - stir well. 
7. Pour the mixture to a buttered 9 x 9 square baking pan. 
8. Spread the mixture evenly - then use the bottom of a flat bowl or glass to press it down 
9. Cut into desired shapes - traditionally coconut cordial is cut into square or diamonds.

1. Combine milk and sugar in a heavy bottom saucepan. 
2. Bring to a boil then reduce heat to a simmer and continue to cook on low stirring continuously until the mixture is reduced to about ⅓ its original volume (about 20 minutes)
3. Then add the ground cashew nuts and continue to stir until it thickens even more
4. Add vanilla and butter - continue to stir and cook 
5. Cook, until you have an almost, paste-like consistency and the mixture leaves the sides of the pan
6. Remove from heat and pour into a greased baking tray
7. Let cool slightly. Then press into flower-shaped silicone molds. Alternatively, you can spread it in the baking tray and cut into slices, squares or bars. 
8. Once molded - let dry at room temperature for 4 to 6 hours before you transfer to an airtight container

1. Preheat the oven at 180 C / 360 F 
2. Grease and line with parchment paper an 8-inch round cake pan or 7-inch square cake pan
3. Cream together butter and sugar until all the sugar is dissolved
4. Add eggs one at a time
5. Combine the flour with baking powder - then add flour in three batches - combine well. 
6. Lastly, add the vanilla and other flavoring
7. Pour into the prepared baking pan 
8. Bake in the preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.

1. Clean, cut and pat dry the mutton
2. Season with salt, pepper, lemon juice, and bottle masala 
3. Cover and leave to marinate for an hour up to 8 hours in the fridge. Thaw the meat at least one hour before cooking (room temperature meat cooks evenly) 
4. Dry roast the red chilies, coriander, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds along with all the garam masala like cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Remove and set aside
5. Then, dry roast the onions, garlic, and ginger until onions are fairly chared but not burnt

dish_name: Indian Squid Curry or Makli Curry
instructions:
1. Clean, wash and chop the squids/makli into small pieces (about 2 inches)
2. Place all the paste masala ingredients in a mixer or food processor and blend until smooth - use a little water if necessary 
3. In a pressure cooker (or instant pot) add oil and saute the paste masala until fragrant
4. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft
5. Then add the bottle masala and saute until fragrant
6. Next, add the squids (makli) saute for two minutes until well coated with the masala
7. Add ¼ cup water, season with salt and pepper.
8. Close the pressure cooker and cook for 5 minutes after the first whistle. For instant pot, close the valve and pressure cook for 5 minutes - natural release
9. Open the cooker, add the tamarind paste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as necessary. 
10. Serve with roti, chapati or rice. 250 grams Squids

3. Peel and mash with a potato ricer

5. Cool in the fridge for at least 4 hours (or overnight)

dish_name: Chitiaps or chittaps or chitaps - RIce Flour crepes
instructions:
1. Combine rice flour, all purpose flour and sugar in a bowl
2. Warm the coconut milk (no more than 110F) - add the yeast - mix well
3. Let the yeast rest for 3 to 5 minutes until foamy
4. Then add the egg and combine well. 
5. Combine the yeast mixture to the flour mixture
6. Mix well until you have no dry flour
7. Cover and leave to ferment overnight at room temperature - minimum 8 hours
8. After 8 hours - stir the mixture well. 
9. If necessary add more coconut milk and make a dripping consistency
10. Heat a cast-iron skillet on medium low heat
11. Lightly grease the pan with oil - wipe off any excess oil 
12. Pour about ¼ cup batter into the skillet 
13. Twirl the skillet and let the mixture spread evenly into a thin layer
14. Cover the skillet and cook for a few minutes until the chittap is ready
15. Continue in the same way with the rest of the batter until all the batter is used up. 250  grams  Rice flour 
125 grams All-purpose flour  
50 grams  Sugar 
½ Cup Coconut milk 
1 tsp  Instant yeast 
1  Egg yolk

1. Combine warm water, honey, and yeast in a bowl. Use a whisk to combine. Tip - the water must be barely warm, close to room temperature. If it's hot, it will kill the yeast and your bread won't rise) 
2. Set it aside for 5 minutes - until foamy. Tip (if it does not become foamy either the water was too hod so the yeast died or the yeast as expired - either start over or buy new yeast) 
3. In a bowl combine both the flours and salt. 
4. Make a hollow in the  center and pour the yeast mixture in
5. Starting from the center out, bring the flour and yeast together. 
6. Use no more than ¼ cup extra flour if necessary. The dough must be soft and sticky
7. Continue to knead on a lightly floured surface - the dough will become less sticky as  you continue to knead - Knead for 3 minutes
8. Then add the soft butter and knead for another 2 to 3 minutes. Now the dough will be soft, smooth and elastic with a slight stickiness.
9. Place the dough in an oiled bowl and cover with a damp kitchen cloth.
10. Leave to rise for one hour or until double in volume. Tip- You can also let the dough rise in the fridge overnight. Next day remove and let come to room temperature first.
11. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Spread the dough into a rectangle (approximately to the length of the light pan)
12. Roll the dough from one end to the other -like a jelly roll. Pinch the seams at the end.
13. Place the rolled dough into the greased loaf pan seam side under
14. Cover with a pan with a clean damp kitchen cloth - let proof for 30 to 45 minutes or until almost double in volume. 
15. Preheat the oven at 200 C/ 390 F 
16. Prepare eggwash - combine half egg with 2 tbsp water. 
17. Brush the top of the bread with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds
18. Use a sharp knife and cut some slashed on the top of the bread (this will allow steam to ascape)
19. Place the loaf in the oven on the middle rack. Bake for about 20to 25 minutes or until the top is golden and the bottom sounds hollow. 2 ¼  tsp Instant dry yeast

1. Combine all ingredients in a bowl with warm water. 
2. Let ferment overnight at room temperature
3. Heat oil for deep frying (about 325 F)
4. Take a small amount of dough on the palm of your hands with water
5. Form a ball then make a hole in the middle with your finger
6. Drop in hot oil and deep fry until golden brown.
7. Remove the varias with a proforated or slotted spoon over absorbend paper to remove excess oil. 
8. Each varias takes about 2 minutes on each side. 500  grams  Urad dal flour

1 tsp Salt

1. Add flour in a bowl with salt, sugar, rice flour - mix to combine
2. Combine eggs, coconut juice, and yeast - mix well to combine
3. Add liquid ingredients to the dry ingredients 
4. Combine well - knead for three minutes.
5. This is not a stiff dough. The dough will be loose and sticky. 
6. Cover with a damp towel and rest for at least 2 hours or overnight (traditionally this dough is kept to prove and ferment overnight) 
7. Pour 1-liter oil in a deep pan for deep frying 
8. The traditional method to make fugias is to squish the dough in the palm of your hands. The little dough that escapes between the thumb and forefinger on top forms a ball. Pinch this ball with damp hands and drop it in the hot oil.
9. Fry them in batches until lightly golden.
10. Remove onto a paper towel with a perforated spoon. 
11. Continue until all dough is used up. 1 kg Plain flour, maida
